strings.USA_THENEWORDER_DESC:
While America joined the Second World War, support came too late to save her allies. The United States performed admirably, humbling the Kriegsmarine in the Atlantic and beginning to turn the tide in the Pacific, but the invention of the atom bomb ended any hopes of American victory for those few remaining Allies.

Now, twenty years later, America stands divided. While the great American Depression is slowly ending, the American political scene sits in chaos. The government remains locked between the uneasy Republican-Democratic Coalition and the National Progressive Pact, a failing union of America's progressives, socialists, and authoritarians. With the Civil Rights movement greatly shifting the political sphere, many predict that the 60's will herald the greatest threats America has ever faced.
strings.USA_Channel_Crisis_buildup_desc: What was once thought of as a faint hope has become a paradigm- shifting reality - Britannia, our old friend has come back to life, seeking to stand with the free world once more. But how Germany will emerge from the flames that still engulf Europe is a mystery, and with the Isles' status as the Pakt's Atlantic gateway any move could turn ugly fast. While we can only hold our breath for now, we have to be ready for whatever happens next.
strings.USA_Channel_Crisis_confrontation_desc: It is clear. Even now, any breach of its European Fortress will be bitterly contested by the Reich. Regardless of if this was the best course to take, we are now locked in a dangerous standoff admist growing unease in the White House. We cannot falter at this hour; a corner of the world that has finally witnessed dawn after a long night risks being plunged back into darkness. If we aren't careful, stopping it could plunge the globe into an even darker abyss.
strings.USA_CC_embolden_nuclear_fears_in_reich_t:
If German Readiness is high, it will decrease by 30%
But if German Readiness is low, the decision will backfire and it will increase by 35%
strings.USA_CC_approach_and_confront_enemy_vesse:
If German Readiness is below 50%, it will decrease by 30%

strings.USA_CC_negotiations_desc: Despite the fact it means continued stipulations for Britain and the OFN, maybe we can cut a deal with Germania in exchange for their recognition of the new government. But are we sure we want to compromise with the world's foremost tyrants?
strings.USA_CC_meet_with_the_nsc: Meet With the National Security Council
strings.USA_CC_embolden_nuclear_fears_in_reich: Embolden Nuclear Fears in the Reich
strings.USA_CC_deescalate_desc: This is getting out of control. We cannot let a war break out at any cost.
strings.USA_IBC_desc:
The British Isles have become the newest hot commodity of the Cold War. The Einheitspakt and the Organization of Free Nations both eagerly vie for her membership, and are attempting to court it through various means. This battle of influence lies on a knife's edge however. Should one of these factions' influence overpower that of England's, they will be forced to join a faction, as reliance on their militaries and economic might becomes a must. Overpowering the influence of Germany will surely grant us a victory in the Cold War.

Influence of the Einheitspakt, the Organization of Free Nations, and {getenglandunificationenglandorbritain} herself:

strings.USA_Faction_Join_OFN_Mission_desc: Our diplomats have informed us that if the diplomatic situation is to continue in this course, {getenglandunificationenglandorbritain} will join us in the Organization of Free Nations, strengthening our position in the Cold War.
strings.USA_Faction_Join_Pakt_Mission_desc: Our diplomats have expressed their concern that if the diplomatic situation is to continue in this course, {getenglandunificationenglandorbritain} will join {ger_getflag} Germany and the Einheitspakt at the end of this diplomatic standoff.
strings.USA_Faction_Close_Faction_Mechanic_Missi: Our diplomats have expressed their concern that if the diplomatic situation is to continue in this course, {getenglandunificationenglandorbritain} may decide to stay neutral in the Cold War.
strings.USA_Faction_Join_OFN_Mission.tt: {eng_getflag}{getenglandunificationenglandorbritain} will join the Organization of Free Nations.

strings.USA_Caribbean_Situation_Improves_med: As a result of our actions, Caribbean Stability has improved.
strings.USA_Caribbean_Situation_Improves_big: As a result of our actions, Caribbean Stability has greatly improved.

strings.USA_colombia.7.desc:
In an air-conditioned corner of Bogotá, three floors above the city, Dirk Holden watched the traffic and sipped that ever-delightful Colombian coffee. In his typewriter was the last page of a report that would launch his career in the Company into the stratosphere: a report on the success of our new allies in the Colombian Civil War. Langley would hear of the crucial role he played in the affair, and they would reward his ten long years trapped in what he once thought was a God-forsaken jungle. Perhaps the coffee was a little bitter, but his victory tasted sweet.

The victors were an odd bunch: from progressive hawks to liberal democrats alongside a myriad of other squabbling factions. Holden would assure his superiors that the latter would not interfere with the general pro-American sentiment growing within the Country. Gaitán was himself a staunch pan-American who sought to warm his country with the torch of freedom, and his successors can now carry that torch. All Langley needed to be cautioned was against overt interference with their markets. He couldn't help but editorialise: let the Colombians develop their economy, offer them capital and let them decide for themselves which foreign companies should be permitted to invest. You'll still get a grip on their economy, and everyone will be happy.

It wasn't patriotic pride that made Holden smile. It was pride in his own efforts. Ten long years in Colombia, helping run this station, and he had an entire nation to show for it. He took a sip of his bitter coffee, the prized crop of this country. At first he hated it - his cups were once always three-quarters milk - but over time he grew to appreciate its strong, bold flavour. His appreciation for Colombian coffee grew with his appreciation for Colombia, from hated exile to proud caretaker. America had won here, and America - or, at least, her intelligence services - would come to know the vital role he played in securing their position in Colombia.
strings.USA_colombia.7.a: He made sure that was clear in the report.
strings.USA_colombia.8.desc:
Henry was running for his fucking life. He sprinted through the thick forest, barely avoiding the roots and branches that reached up to trip him. Holden ran behind him. Henry never liked him, and had privately called him a “CIA bastard”, but that didn't matter now. The revolutionaries had been routed, and they were on the run. Henry could hear the government soldiers advancing, seemingly just at their heels.

Holden slumped wheezing against a tree. Henry turned and yelled “What the fuck are you doing?”

“Just need to get my brea-” Holden's words were cut off by a gunshot followed by a scream. Henry ran with doubled speed. Bursting through the trees, he found himself staring down at the Orinoco River. Henry took a deep breath and leapt off the edge of the bank.

He had planned to swim to the other side, but found that impossible. His eyes burned in the murky water, and the rush of the river stole all sound from his ears. He tried to push in the direction he assumed was the opposite shore, but his muscles quickly tired and his lungs burned. When a hand grabbed his back and pulled him from the water, the relief almost drowned out the fear.

He was sprawled on the deck of a small motorboat, driven by a soldier. Another soldier sat near him, his gun at the ready. Henry sat up and looked to the shore they were headed for. On it he saw several more soldiers and Holden, sitting with a bloody bandage on his leg. The situation wasn't ideal, but it at least seemed like they wouldn't be killed.
strings.USA_colombia.8.a: An embarrassing end to the adventure.
strings.USA_colombia.9.desc:
Dirk Holden tried to summon the information in his head: the field manuals, the informational movies, the conversations between veterans he overheard. Only a jumble emerged, thousands of scraps fighting for relevance in his mind as his body marched through the Colombian jungle. He was stripped and blindfolded, forced to march through the unforgiving jungle by a victorious enemy. He tried to explain who he was - not an agent, not a soldier, but a secretary. His captors do not care. He marches to his death with the rest of the Yankees.

Peeled bark and fallen branches crunch and splinter below his bleeding feet. The cold barrel of a rifle presses into his back, driving him forward whenever his body tries to rest. Holden wishes he could hear the birds above him clearly. He would like to die with their song to comfort him, but the jeering of soldiers and the loud crunch of the debris below him drown out their song.

In the din of his mind, new thoughts emerge, memories of reports terrifyingly clearer than the ones he tries to remember. New Granada's forces had been creative with their torture of local collaborators. Holden read the reports; he even wrote a few of them. They had long eschewed conventional force and developed new ways of inflicting pain on men. They had even taken to mimicking medieval forms of torture. He tried to fend off these thoughts, but once they revealed themselves it was impossible to forget. Holden's legs almost gave out, but another sharp thrust of a gun barrel in his back forced him to keep stable and walk towards horrors he'd only read about.

Some four thousand miles away, a report crosses the Resolute Desk. It puts the Colombian situation in plain terms: assets that have not been extracted at the time of writing are considered lost. The torch of liberty shall not fall on New Granada. With sorrow, anger or boredom - few know now, and none will remember later - the President accepts this information and passes it along the desk like a clerk.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
In his second term, Democratic President Franklin D. Roosevelt faced a growing conservative backlash—one that viewed his New Deal as starting the United States down the same dangerous path as Russia. Afraid another term might bring political ruin, Roosevelt decided not to seek the presidency again.

Instead, he convinced the party to nominate his close friend and one-time Administrator of the Works Progress Administration Harry Hopkins. To ensure his friend's election, Roosevelt tacked to the center and made concessions to isolationists. Meanwhile, conservative Republicans—including Ohio Senator Robert A. Taft—threw their support behind the charismatic but inexperienced Manhattan District Attorney Thomas Dewey.

Soon after, Hopkins learned he had stomach cancer. Bedridden, with rumors about his condition swirling in the press, he lost to Dewey by less than .4% of the national vote.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
President Thomas Dewey rewarded his isolationist backers by appointing many officials allied with Senator Robert A. Taft. He then embarked on a campaign of dismantling Roosevelt's New Deal while his cabinet dismantled the United States' military capacity to avoid direct confrontation with the rising German Reich and Japanese Empire.

These developments proved disastrous. Recession hit. Japan and Germany declared war. By 1944, with the war effort collapsing, Dewey would find his hopes of re-election saved by Gen. Eisenhower's defense of Scotland as well as a split in his opposition between the moderate party insider James Farley and Progressive Republican Henry Wallace.

President Dewey limped into a second term. With the country coming apart, Dewey agreed to a negotiated peace with the Axis in which the United States would surrender its Pacific holdings and place the territory of Hawai'i under a 100-year lease.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
The Republican Party faced landslide defeat in 1946, but many Americans blamed the “socialistic” policies of Roosevelt for weakening America and making the war inevitable. The 1948 Election tested these attitudes, matching isolationist Republican Robert Taft against internationalist Democratic Dwight D. Eisenhower. Ike would win, but not before exposing deep dissatisfaction with the Establishment.

Ike attempted to complete Roosevelt's unfinished work. However, a rift with progressive Vice President Burton Wheeler over an intervention to defend Portuguese Angola from Germany sabotaged his presidency. In 1952, he only narrowly won re-election.

Ike's second term was disappointing. Wheeler proved unable to guide the Senate to popular policy and Eisenhower resorted to executive orders to pass his agenda. As dissatisfaction grew, a new Nationalist Party formed to support Gen. George Patton in 1952.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4:
After Ike, the Establishment was unwilling to support his progressive Vice President Burton Wheeler. Instead Democrats nominated moderate Estes Kefauver while Republicans nominated moderate Everett M. Dirksen. The Nationalists and a revived Progressive Party became home for those disaffected by the mainstream.

Kefauver barely triumphed but the backlash was swift. In the midterms, dozens of new parties forced themselves on the ballot. Chaos reigned—with senators elected with a third of the popular vote and allegations of fraud and corruption.

The Nationalists, Progressives, and others realized they could vanquish the Establishment if they worked together. They formed an alliance of convenience, the National Progressive Pact, led by Progressive Scoop Jackson and States' Rights leader James Fullbright. Republicans and Democrats, seeing an existential threat, formed a coalition of their own led by conservative Richard Nixon and liberal John F. Kennedy.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5:
The Republican Party, a party of conservatives, finds itself led by the greatest survivor of all: Richard Nixon. A master of negative campaigning, Nixon survived a finance scandal in 1952 and near-defeat in the 1954 California gubernatorial election and forced his way into Kefauver's cabinet as Secretary of State. He styles himself as the leader of the Silent Majority, even as his domestic unpopularity grows.

Beneath him stand the Hardline Republicans of Barry Goldwater, deficit hawks who believe in immediately ending Roosevelt's excesses, and the Responsible Republicans of Nelson Rockefeller, New England moderates who prefer gradual conservative reforms.

The last few years of crises have made it a struggle for Nixon to retain his leadership. However, he is determined to retain leadership of the Republican Party, preserve the RDC, and see himself re-elected in 1964 at any cost.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.6:
The Democratic Party, heirs to the legacies of Roosevelt, Eisenhower, and Kefaufer, finds itself led by the charismatic Vice President John F. Kennedy. Epitomizing all the hope of this new age, Kennedy has urged his nation to look past its failures and embrace the future. His decisions to meet leaders of the Civil Rights Movement, urge military restraint, and advocate for aggressive solutions to economic stagnation have made him a beloved figure to many—even as they infuriate the President.

Beneath Kennedy, factionalism rages. On one side stands the Labor Democrats, represented in Congress by Senator Lyndon Baines Johnson. These figures see the New Deal as incomplete and seek to expand and build upon its programs.

On the other side stands the Dixiecrats, led in Congress by Senator Richard Russell Jr. These figures, largely Southerners, stand outraged by Kennedy's meetings with Black leaders. They seek to preserve segregationism.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.7:
The Nationalist Caucus is the largest group in the new Nationalist Progressive Pact, representing not just the Nationalist Party but various populist conservative groups such as the Conservative Party of New York, States' Rights Party, and Louisiana Progressive Party. Animated by reactionary passions, the coalition has many faces it presents to current events.

Leading the caucus into 1964 is Alabama Governor George Wallace, an avowed segregationist outraged by what he sees as the “lawlessness” of the civil rights movement. Also among the Nationalists are many former War Hawk Republicans led by Margaret Chase Smith, who defected from the Republican Party after US defeat in World War II, and the remnants of Senator Robert A. Taft's Midwestern isolationist movement, which is seeing a revival among the Christian Right who feel adrift in a rapidly changing nation.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.8:
The second-largest NPP caucus is the Progressives, a grab bag of different liberal groups. It includes not just the resurrected Progressive Party but also the Farmer-Labor Party, Nonpartisan League, and Liberal Party of New York. While more ideologically unified than the Nationalists, the Progressives are no less volatile.

Leading the party into 1964 is Scoop Jackson, a New Deal liberal and warhawk hoping for a rematch with Nixon. However, fortunes change in a day. Many Progressives, particularly those unhappy with Scoop's attempts to make peace with anti-civil rights officials, have been seeking a different challenger in 1964. Whether they succeed could depend on forces outside their hands.

In caucus's fringes sits Michael Harrington, leader of the Democratic Socialists of America. While many scoff at a socialist in the White House, Harrington is happy to bide his time.
strings.USA_CountryInfo_Content_desc.9:
While “more respectable” NPP leaders try to ignore them, the Pact also includes many smaller groups whose hostility to the Establishment includes not just the two main parties but the American system itself. These parties view the Republic as a failed state, with radical action needed to save its people.

The Marxist Caucus, led by Communist Party USA's Gus Hall, is one such group. Composed of avowed communists and socialists, the Marxist Caucus sees the average American as exploited by the capitalist class and the current fight over civil rights to be a symptom of a larger class struggle.

Even smaller and more fringe than the Marxists are the Sovereigntists, a vile group of fascists and white nationalists. Few but the most radicalized Americans would dare associate themselves with them. Their leader, Francis Parker Yockey, has made a reputation giving voice to the dark fantasies of aggrieved whites who see Germany as an ally, not an enemy in a coming war.
strings.USA_enable_homefront_mech: Enable the Most Insane Fucking Thing You've Ever Seen
strings.USA_load_USA_WAL_64_CRA: Load Wallace's Tree with CRA Repeal
strings.USA_debug_SAF_flag: Load SAW Tree for Current President
strings.USA_WAC_info_tooltip:
The West African War is shaping into a complicated affair with many factors affecting our involvement in it. Discontent with the war will tend to increase as time goes by, and the higher it gets, the worse the effects it'll have in our country.

Escalation of the war will unlock more radical and stronger methods to undertake the war, but at the same time it will worsen the negative effects of the war and may result in unforeseen consequences.

Garrison Strength is a necessity for us to maintain effective operational capacity in the region due to the constant presence of guerrillas. This is our most vulnerable flank, as it's a constant expenditure and drain of resources, and it's a clear objective for our enemies to strike, so we must be careful in how we handle this resource.
strings.USA_congo_civil_war_desc: The Congo has fallen to chaos, and with the Japanese and Germans trying to control the remains, it falls upon us to deny these tyrants the benefits of the Congo. Our victory in the Congo will solidify our influence, and continue to deny Africa to our enemies.
strings.USA_GZCW_PW_desc_mondlane:
Politics makes strange bedfellows, and in the world of superpower conflict waged via proxy, some bedfellows can be stranger than others. A premise aptly demonstrated in Mozambique. Eduardo Mondlane is not your typical American proxy, an avowed socialist, nationalist, and harshly critical of the Cold War waged across the third world. Relations are tense at the best of times, and there is no delusion over where his true loyalties lie.

Yet, as Mozambique buckles under the weight of warring factions, Tokyo looks on with a keen eye. Mondlane represents America's best shot at keeping this part of Africa out of the Sphere's grasp. Even if it means placing it in the hands of neutrals.

strings.USA_GZCW_PW_desc_simango:
Mozambique buckles under the bloody specter of Civil War. Competing interests and bloody rivalries spilling out from closed rooms onto city streets and rural plains and inevitably drawing the attention of the Superpowers eager to exploit national tragedy for international gain.

Uria Simango heads neither the strongest nor the most numerous faction in the conflict, but what is lacking in strength is more than made up for in pliability. Heavily reliant on American support, a victory for Simango not only means keeping Japan out of Africa but also ensuring Mozambique's place in the ranks of the Free World.

strings.USA_MLY_aid_category_desc:
After our defeat in the Second World War, a crested wave has descended upon the Pacific Ocean, the wave of Japan's so called Co-Prosperity Sphere. Recently however, an opportunity has arisen from the war-torn region of Malaya. Having endured decades of occupation from the Japanese invaders, the Malayan people have seen the government alternate between collaborators and rebels from time and time again, and have fought a relentless guerrilla campaign against the Japanese occupiers.

The 25th Army, which are stationed there by the Japanese, has launched a final desperate offensive in the hopes of destroying rebel presence in the region once and for all. This has led the rebels to contact us in search for aid to defeat the Japanese.

Despite our clear ideological differences, the opportunity that Malaya provides is immeasurable. We are finally able to strike them where it hurts, and if the stars align, we will tear down the Crested Wave piece by piece, and we will watch as their glorious Sphere crumbles before our eyes.
strings.USA_instigate_local_revolts_tt: Using our connections and the UMAJF's network of sleeper agents, we'll arm peasant revolts across the countryside.
strings.USA_congo_confrontation_WA_desc: The warlords and petty tyrants of the northern Congo are not exactly fond of our attempt to govern their territory, but they are no more fond of their West African neighbors who similarly threaten their rule. In exchange for weapons and the promise of a lighter touch, we may be able to get them to focus their attention northward.
strings.USA_mano_timer_desc:
It's only been a few years since we last came to the Golden Coast to rescue our ally from the red flood and its Japanese backers, and we failed. Now, the same forces that massacred France's last hope are back for West Africa's last democracies, but we refuse to make the same mistakes we made in the previous war.

The sheer size of the Pan-African invasion has made plans for minor support or limited intervention futile; if we are to force them out and secure our allies' borders, we must deploy boots on the ground in force. The distance between West Africa and America is vast, and crossing it in detail will be time-consuming, so we must do all we can to hasten our mobilization and deployment. Every hour counts.
strings.USA_mano_success_tooltip: We'll complete the mobilization into the Mano Pact territory.
strings.USA_mano_air_operation: Unlock decisions to conduct air operations in this region
strings.USA_mano_allow_air: We are able to conduct air operations in this region
strings.USA_mano_focus_resource: Focus Resources on the Mano Pact
strings.USA_mano_divert_resource_to_air: Divert Resources to the Air Force
strings.USA_angola_civil_war_desc: In the aftermath of the collapse of the prior authorities in Angola, that once-Portuguese colony has fallen apart. The native resistance was for long years divided into two factions, the pro-Western, democratic UNITA faction and the pan-Africanist, socialist PLUAA faction. The tensions have at last risen to an uncontrolled level as war breaks out; conflict once again erupts in southwestern Africa. As always, there is risk and opportunity for us in this chaos.
strings.USA_angola_plant_mines_desc: We will instruct local forces in [?From.GetName] to plant mines across the region to slow motorized advances.
strings.USA_angola_bombing_campaigns_desc: We will authorize our bombers to begin sorties targeting [?ANL.GetName] forces in [?From.GetName].
strings.USA_guns_for_diamonds_ANG_desc:
Angola's Northeast Lunda province has a wealth of diamonds. The current civil war means they would be more than willing to exchange these gems for arms, at a favorable rate.

“These ain't conflict diamonds, is they, Jacob? Don't lie to me, man.”
strings.USA_ANG_sit_down_with_savimbi_desc: Savimbi has drawn the approval of several notable American conservatives. We will arrange an informal meeting between these leaders and the Angolan, as a sign of goodwill.
strings.USA_ANG_CIA_intelligence_SAF_desc: The CIA, in coordination with South African intelligence, will provide details into [?ANL.GetName] troop movements, allowing our allied forces to better counter their strikes.
strings.USA_ANG_CIA_intelligence_desc: CIA assets in the region will provide details into [?ANL.GetName] troop movements, allowing our allied forces to better counter their strikes.
strings.USA_ANG_economic_aid_desc: We will direct funds to prop up [?ANG.GetName] industry in support of the war effort.
strings.USA_ANG_send_military_advisors_desc: American military advisors will train [?ANG.GetName] forces in modern tactics and weaponry.
strings.USA_MAD_remove_1_action_tt: This will utilize 1 available action from our loadout.
strings.USA_MAD_will_violate_strike_tt: This will result in a strike, coming closer to the discovery of our illegal actions in Madagascar.
strings.USA_MAD_result_strike_3_tt:
This will be strike 3.
Reaching strike 3 will result in withdrawal from the war.
strings.USA_MADCW_investigation_shut_down_MADCW: With an investigation underway, we need to cut off any activity in Madagascar.
strings.USA_Madagascar_desc:
We have involved ourselves illegally in the Malagasy Rebellion. Absurdly, this involvement is through supporting our Japanese enemy as they fight the Reich. We must ensure that the provision of supplies and advisors is done in such a manner as to
ruin Germany here without strengthening
the Japanese too much—or letting
others know what we're doing.
strings.USA_MADCW_expanding_assets_do_more_more_: Expanding CIA Assets will make certain operations more effective, although we will be able to do less if we're worried about getting caught.
strings.USA_MADCW_folks_rise_tt: Malagasy Troops will rise up in this state and claim it!
strings.USA_MADCW_folks_rise_ger_tt: Malagasy Troops will rise up in this state and contest its control versus Germany
strings.USA_MADCW_abidjan_airlift_tt: PADESM exiles from Free France will be brought to Madagascar.
strings.USA_MADCW_operation_drawstring_tt: CIA shell companies will recruits mercenaries and Free French exiles in South Africa to fight in Madagascar.
strings.USA_MADCW_operation_swingset_tt: A CIA training program for Malagasy marksmen will be established, which trains instructors and provides materials under the guise of a private Free French organization.
strings.USA_CIA_Maurice_Decisions_TT: Emil Maurice is in our captivity. Decisions in the Africa tab of the Intelligence Menu have been unlocked.
strings.USA_Maurice_InterceptHome:
We know where he is! We've got to finish the job!
Decisions in the Caribbean America tab of the Intelligence Menu have been unlocked.
strings.USA_Maurice_To_America_tt: We will continue our efforts to bring Emil Maurice to America.
strings.USA_Maurice_To_Death_tt: We will continue our efforts to kill Emil Maurice.
strings.USA_cement_hattas_legitimacy_among_prim_: Cement Hatta's Legitimacy Among PRIM Leaders
strings.USA_set_up_port_garrisons_in_prim_territ: Set Up Port Garrisons in PRIM Territory
strings.USA_Provide_Staff_Assistance_to_FRI: Provide Staff Assistance to FRI and PRIM
strings.USA_INS_not_exceeded_bombing_limit: We have not exceeded our state bombing capacity of [?USA_INS_max_bombings|0].
strings.USA_authorize_operation_linebacker_tt: Major Indonesian cities not under the control of the PRIM will be heavily bombed to weaken their war machine and to weaken the civilian apparatus of state.
strings.USA_PHI_PW_1_desc:
Of the 30,000 Americans who had made their last stands in Bataan and Corregidor, only half would return stateside by war's end. The rest had either died in combat, died in captivity, or fled back into the jungles after repatriation ended abruptly, abysmally. Tales thereafter told of men continuing the good fight to the south, in the mountains and forests Manila cannot reach.

Twenty years have passed hence, and recent developments have shown the true extent of their long campaign. Where before they were cast to the untrammeled wilds, now only a hundred miles stand between them and Manila. Many have clamored the President to send our old soldiers aid lest they falter and fall. And so he shall.

No longer will we idle from the sidelines. One way or another, we'll finish our boys' fight and bring them back home.

We shall not fail a second time.
strings.USA_PHI_huks_Irregular_Exhaustion_tt: The Blitz has taken at least 5 months
strings.USA_PHI_huks_Irregular_effect_tt: We shall launch an operation aimed to further our cooperation with the Huks. It will allow us to directly aid them through military volunteers, although this will prevent us from escalating our support in the USFIP.
strings.USA_PHI_huks_Irregular_desc:
The Balintawak Blitz, true to its name, was meant to be a quick and relatively bloodless war against the Japanese-aligned government in Manila, in the hopes of crippling Japanese influence in the Pacific. Yet, the Manila government has put up more of a fight than what we anticipated, and the war grinded down to a bloody standstill with no clear winner.

Perhaps the AFRSR might be willing to work with us. Cooperation may just give us enough boost for us to drive the Japanese out of the islands, and perhaps make the future of post-war Philippines certain, once we win that is.
strings.USA_PHI_advisors_tt: We can send a Volunteer Division to the {uph_getflag}{uph_getname}.
strings.USA_PHI_olive_men_tt: Using our equipment, the Filipino rebels will be able to field an additional division.
strings.USA_PHI_GDP_tt: Our industrial aid will slightly increase their GDP.
strings.USA_PHI_instability_cooperation: This will alienate the Huks in the north, preventing us from engaging in any potential future cooperation with them.
strings.USA_PHI_aid_from_west_point_buffs: Increases {uph_getflag}{uph_getname}'s Organization and Reinforce Rate by 5.00%.
strings.USA_PHI_PW_2_desc:
As the 14th Army's boats scurried full speed to Tokyo, a commodore left one last burst of Morse code to a watchtower by the coast: “We shall return.”

The exact date is muddled by rumormongering and disinformation, ones Intelligence hasn't even begun to disentangle. Nevertheless, Japan's parting shot is as direct as it is profuse with irony: that the Empire would so easily surrender is laughable at best, and a lethal jape at worst. The real test begins soon, at the rare moment in a man's life where history repeats and legends are retold.

So rally the men, raise the palisades, man the guns - but above all, never lose hope. If we've beaten the devils once, we'll beat them again.
strings.USA_PHI_mcarthurt_fort_tt: In cooperation with the Huks, we will build a line of fortifications in Luzon to prepare for the Japanese invasion
strings.USA_PHI_mass_conscription_tt: 5 Auxillary brigades will be raised in the {uph_getflag}{uph_getname}.
strings.USA_PHI_expand_army_tt: 2 Infantry divisions will be raised in the {uph_getflag}{uph_getname}.
strings.USA_PHI_IJN_blockade_dummy_desc: Our capacity to provide further support to the Filipino rebels has been effectively neutered due to an ongoing blockade on the islands by the IJN. We can only afford to slip through supplies for our volunteers, and nothing else, lest our ships are to be blown out of the waters.
strings.USA_PHI_doing_preparation_decision: Doing another decision to prepare against a Japanese invasion.
strings.USA_PHI_disallow_other_army_choice_tt: Due to limited time and resources, we must choose between expanding the Philippine Army proper or raising conscription for more auxillaries.
strings.USA_UPH_reconstruction_desc:
Although the parties have died down and the beer taps have finally run dry, the Filipino people must still contend with the pains of a nation exhausted both in land and spirit. American aid in easing this process goes without saying.

Our analysts estimate that we have no more than six months of leeway to fix the war's worst damages before public sentiment compels a withdrawal. By then authority should be restored to an elected civilian government, whether it is of Diosdado Pangan Macapagal Sr.'s Partido Liberal or Carlos Garcia's “new Filipinos.”

Note that Mr. Diosdado has staked his legitimacy on us delivering not merely reconstruction, but a timely, well-managed one at that. Should we exceed the six-month deadline, Mr. Garcia will likely succeed the late Sergio Osmeña, Sr. as President and establish a government less open to our suggestions than the Lawyer.
strings.USA_SPH_Coalition_reconstruction_desc:
In response to the 14th Army invasion, the USFIP and the Communist insurgency brokered an agreement which elevated their non-aggression pact during the Blitz into a full-fledged alliance. Among its stipulations was a binding pledge to organize a post-war government composed of appointees from the Communist Party of the Philippines, the military and civilian halves of the USFIP, and miscellaneous groups opposed to the former KALIBAPI. Thus, the so-termed United Filipino Front evolved into the Coalition Government following the Evacuation.

Acting President Lorenzo Tañada's popularity with left-wing forces and Ramon Magsaysay's popularity with the Nacionalistas is a direct threat to our candidate, Diosdado Pangan Macapagal Sr.'s Partido Liberal. What happens in either case is anyone's guess, but it certainly won't be good for the country - or for us, after all we'd sunk into prying it off Japan.
strings.USA_PHI_disallow_demobilization: Unable to demobilize the Philippine Army
strings.USA_PHI_disallow_demobilization_tt: Choosing this decision will disallow us from demobilizing the Philippine Army.
strings.USA_PHI_disallow_hunt_bandidos_tt: Choosing this decision will disallow us from performing anti-bandidos actions.
strings.USA_delegitimze_leyte_proclamation_tt:
Delegitimizing the Leyte Proclamation will put Diosdado Pangan Macapagal Sr., our preferred candidate for the President of the Philippines, in charge of the country.

His friendliness to us will grant us another ally within the Organization of Free Nations.
Should we not do this, someone else who is less cooperative with us, will become President.
strings.USA_USFIP_anti_referendum_campaign_tt: Campaigning against the Popular Referendum guarantees Diosdado Pangan Macapagal Sr., to win the coming elections, and prevents the anyone else from taking over the government in the future.
strings.USA_UPH_recon_timeout_tt: We will lose the favor of the Philippine Government, placing an undesired candidate in charge of the Philippines.
strings.USA_SPH_recon_timeout_tt: We will lose the favor of the Philippine Government, placing an undesired candidate in charge of the Philippines.
strings.USA_assist_reconstruction_desc: We will directly send aid to the government of the Philippines for reconstruction in many forms, be it material or monetary.
strings.USA_Send_in_Experts_desc: We will send several experts in economics to help the Republic in its long road to recovery. Their aid is sure to be beneficial to the reconstruction and may even provide us with opportunities to innovate at home.
strings.USA_dismantle_manila_forts_desc: The many fortifications in the city of Manila is an unfortunate sight to see. Along with its horrible look, it also hinders the process of reconstruction by taking up space that can be used for more useful buildings or infrastructure. Thus, a demolition and clean-up is in order.
strings.USA_emergency_price_fixing_laws_desc: The economic situation in the Philippines is at a critical, with the war-torn country struggling to feed and provide the people with their needs as a result of decades of endless war. We must impose emergency price fixing laws to ensure that the people suffer the least, and to ensure that the economic situation does not degrade further.
strings.USA_bandidos_hunt_success_tt: The hunt against the bandidos rampant in the Philippines succeeds.
strings.USA_bandidos_hunt_fail_tt: The hunt against the bandidos rampant in the Philippines fails.
strings.USA_IBW_PW_desc: As Iberia falls to civil war for the second time in mere decades, the Spanish Republic has emerged once more. Franco has proven himself a tyrant - so we will support the Republic and set history right. Perhaps the second time will be the charm.
strings.USA_Plane_Bombing_desc:
The outbreak of war with the Americans' puppet has brought the wrath of the US Air Force down upon us. Bombs rain down upon critical infrastructure and military installations and our ability to offer resistance in the air is minimal.

This will disrupt the organisation of our forces and will damage domestic support for the war effort, but we have little choice but to press on and hope that this bombardment does not escalate further.
strings.USA_military_advisors_desc: Our friends in the US have seen fit to dispatch military advisors to aid our armed forces. With their support we shall see a significant improvement in the overall performance of our soldiers, as well as learning important lessons about modern warfare which will improve the efficiency of our armed forces in the future.
strings.USA_technician_aid_desc: The United States has seen fit to dispatch technicians to aid our war effort and we are already seeing significant benefits to a range of different areas of our military and economy as a result. We can only hope that aid such as this shall continue to be forthcoming.
strings.USA_sabotage_effort_desc:
The outbreak of war with the American puppet has resulted in the CIA being unleashed against us. A wave of sabotage and paranoia has swept our country as their agents set to work stealing state secrets, sabotaging military operations, and assassinating officials.

This is proving detrimental to the war effort, not only because of the direct consequences of the sabotage but also because of the paranoia gripping our government as our own agents struggle to prevent further damage.
strings.USA_rules_of_engagement_desc: The rules of engagement are a set of internal rules and policies defining how, when, and where a soldier can use force. Amid our interventions abroad, the President has issued an order to the secretary of defense mandating that these rules be updated and more strictly enforced. While some criticize this move as forcing the military to fight with “one hand tied behind their back,” others believe it will limit potential atrocities and preserve US credibility at home and abroad.
strings.USA_War_Immigrants_desc:
Where war breaks out, Washington is never far behind. While we are beating back the tide of Fascism and Imperialism, there are consequences. Our proxy wars have resulted in thousands of refugees flocking to America. While we may gain more people, the societal tension of a refugee crisis cannot be understated. However, America is nothing without immigrants. Just like the Statue of Liberty says:

“Give me your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free.”
strings.USA_mano_campaign_desc:
West Africa has gone from crisis to outright disaster! It was bad enough to see the colors of the PALF, masking those of the Rising Sun, flying over the ruins of democratic nations we failed to defend. Now Japan's bloodthirsty stooges have taken advantage of the Oil Crisis to continue their 'liberation' efforts, striking at Sierra Leone and Liberia.

These two nations, imperfect as they may be, are the OFN's only friends left in the region. The alternative to victory in this war is absolute Japanese dominance of West Africa and its vast resources. America will not stand by while slavery is reimposed upon Africans - defeat is not an option!
strings.USA_PP_invasion_desc:
The Dominican Republic has grown to be the largest thorn in our side in Latin America at large. The regime has found a niche in exporting its cancer, establishing closely knitted networks of support with other fascist regimes. Trujillo's actions threaten to turn into a time bomb, and in the future could hinder our position in the region.

An opportunity to topple the dictator has appeared with the collapse of the Triumvirate. Our Cuban allies have been training the organization known as the “Second Caribbean Legion”, a small anti-fascist army of volunteers from all across the Caribbean, and we will direct them against Trujillo.

strings.USA_PP_ongoing_tooltip: We must make sure that the Supplies are enough to sustain the Caribbean Legion until the end of the campaign, or they will receive negative effects.

The Caribbean Legion is currently equipped with
[?USA.USA_PP_Army] brigades. Employing over 5 brigades will drain supply faster after landing.
strings.USA_PP_ongoing_bottom: The Outcome of the Caribbean Legion's campaign will be decided in two months.
strings.USA_PP_collapse_tooltip: Within the next two months, the outcome of the Puerto Plata Invasion shall be decided...

strings.USA_PP_minimum_supply_decrease_tt: Our £GFX_PHI_supply_floor_texticon Minimum Supply will decrease by {invasion_minimum_supply_temp}.
strings.USA_PPI_CAL_training_tt: All £GFX_decision_icon_small Decisions to prepare and train Legion forces will become unavailable.
strings.USA_PPI_show_infantry_desc: The Caribbean Legionnaire is often green, though they are numerous and willing to give all for the cause.
strings.USA_PPI_hide_infantry_desc: The Caribbean Legionnaire is often green, though they are numerous and willing to give all for the cause.
strings.USA_PPI_show_cuban_forces_desc: Cuban battalions are composed of highly-motivated Cuban veterans of their Revolution.
strings.USA_PPI_hide_cuban_forces_desc: Cuban battalions are composed of highly-motivated Cuban veterans of their Revolution.
strings.USA_PPI_Train_Brigade_tt: This Column will have higher experience at the moment of landing.
strings.USA_PPI_USN_support_tt:
{cal_getnamewithflag} will be stronger during the first week of the invasion.

strings.USA_PPI_USAF_support_tt:
{cal_getnamewithflag} will receive air support from the United States Air Force.
£GFX_decision_icon_small Decisions to organize air drops will become available after the invasion starts.
May increase £GFX_discontent_texticon tensions with future Dominican governments.
strings.USA_PPI_Sleeper_Cells_tt: Sleeper Cells will distrupt the rear lines of our enemy and stronger £GFX_decision_icon_small Sabotage Decisions will become available after the invasion starts.
strings.USA_PPI_Batista_Escapes_desc: Fulgencio Batista, former Cuban dictator, escaped to the Dominican Republic four years ago. Since then, he's so far been the largest threat to the future alignment of the island. If the Dominican rebels manage to bring the Trujillo regime to its knees fast enough, we might be able to kill two birds with one stone.
strings.USA_PPI_Batista_Escapes_tt: Batista will manage to escape the island unscathed...
strings.USA_PP_negotiations_tooltip: The joint civil-military government in Santo Domingo is negotiating the terms of peaceful unification with the Dominican Revolutionary Front. Should Tensions not escalate, they are anticipated to succeed on terms favorable to the US, Mexico, and Cuba.
strings.USA_PP_ceasefire_legion_tt: £GFX_decision_icon_small Decisions to prepare the Rebels become available.
strings.USA_PP_ceasefire_balaguer_tt: £GFX_decision_icon_small Decisions to lower £GFX_discontent_texticon Tensions become available.
strings.USA_PPI_ceasefire_sit_down_with_iberia_t: We will officially approach Iberia for peace mediations
By reaching a détente, both sides will agree not to deploy troops in Colombia
strings.USA_ffr_reclamation_desc:
In 1776, the French aided the USA in the fight against tyranny - now, it's time to return the favor. The Free French have reached the next step in their campaign to reclaim their homeland from the Nazis - and we will aid them in any way we can.

We've gotten this far - France's military victories in West Africa would have been impossible without our aid - and now we must take them over the finish line. The French are excited - and rightfully so- but we must ensure that their actions can back up their words.
strings.USA_french_civil_war_desc: Although France did not take sides in the American Civil War, we will take a side in theirs: we will send men, guns, and other types of aid to the Free French. We will help them reclaim their homeland - and thus return to the world stage as a staunch ally of the OFN. We've gotten this far - France's military victories in West Africa would have been impossible without our aid - and now we must take them over the finish line. The French are excited - and rightfully so - but we must ensure that their actions can back up their words.
strings.USA_INDCW_desc:
The Indian subcontinent has seen centuries of war against foreign invaders, from Alexander the Great, to the British Empire, to the Japanese fascists. Now a new bloody chapter in India's martial history is written as the Indian Civil War, or War of Reunification, rages between the pro-American Republic of India and the pro-Japanese state of Azad Hind. Any and all peaceful negotiations have failed, and only war can reunite the broken country.

The ROI is one of the world's largest democracies, and stands to be one of the most important OFN allies by being a major player in Middle Eastern and Asian affairs. Losing India to the Japanese would be a nightmarish fiasco as big to Washington as it was to London all those years ago. But should freedom win over fascism, Japan may never recover from the blow.
strings.USA_IND_empty_space_desc: Most £GFX_decision_icon_small decisions to aid the {getindiancwside} will cost them their own £stability_texticon stability, so use your decisions wisely.
strings.USA_IND_humanitarian_aid_desc: The Indian Civil War has become the largest humanitarian crisis in Asia, and the massive famines that it caused have horrified the world. As international pleas to do something mount, the United States and the OFN shall step up to feed the Republic of India in its hour of need.
strings.USA_IND_start_blockade_desc: By cutting off Azad Hind's maritime trade, we can dry up their materiel supply and thus end the war faster. The blockade's effectiveness, however, will be determined by our previous performance in Malaya and Madagascar.
strings.USA_IND_military_advisors_tt: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +10% War Support for the next 120 days.
strings.USA_IND_military_advisors_tt_2: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +20% War Support for the next 120 days.
strings.USA_IND_military_advisors_tt_3: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +30% War Support for the next 120 days.
strings.USA_IND_military_advisors_tt_4: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +40% War Support for the next 120 days.
strings.USA_IND_military_advisors_tt_5: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +50% War Support for the next 120 days.
strings.USA_IND_admin_assistance_tt: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +10% Stability for the next 180 days.
strings.USA_IND_admin_assistance_tt_2: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +20% Stability for the next 180 days.
strings.USA_IND_admin_assistance_tt_3: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +30% Stability for the next 180 days.
strings.USA_IND_admin_assistance_tt_4: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +40% Stability for the next 180 days.
strings.USA_IND_admin_assistance_tt_5: {ind_getnamewithflag} will receive +50% Stability for the next 180 days.
strings.USA_IND_start_aid_bill_desc: We will introduce a bill to Congress to allow future shipments of aid to India, permitting heavier packages in the process. Otherwise, we risk leaving them empty-handed if the situation deteriorates.
strings.USA_IND_aid_bill_submitted_tt: A bill to increase military aid to the Republic of India will be sent to Congress
strings.USA_IND_obq_reaction_desc: A Western front has suddenly erupted, with German-backed Muslim militias under a 'Pakistani' flag storming in from Afghan bases on the northwestern frontier, clashing with local police and army reserves. The Pentagon has identified several critical smuggling routes and supply caches that will nip this insurrection in the bud and prevent the Republic from facing the nightmare of a two-front war. Let's hit them, and hit them hard.
strings.USA_IND_operation_big_stick_desc: Bose's forces are smashing through the Republic's men on every front, with Japanese arms powering their relentless assault. Some in the Pentagon see worrying comparisons to 1940 - except now, we have a choice to stem the tide. Though it will raise tensions with the other superpowers, we must send men to hold the line.
strings.USA_IND_increase_pu_1_tt: The Republic of India will Gain 1 Production Unit!
strings.USA_IND_increase_pu_2_tt: The Republic of India will Gain 2 Production Units!
strings.USA_IND_increase_pu_5_tt: The Republic of India will Gain 5 Production Units!

Ready our counterstrike to end the {ven_getflag} Venezuelan threat.
This will add a division to the forthcoming Expeditionary Forces.
