Additionally, Bolivia's position at the center of growing geopolitical tensions between Brazil and Argentina means any upset to the status quo could destabilize the region and reignite a dormant rivalry. Should Brazil secure economic dominance it would give them a leg up against Argentina, and undermine the position of hostile power blocs in the Southern Cone.

3. Preparations underway to use connections in the Bolivian elite to ensure that the treaty does not damage American interests regardless of the outcome. Whether we push these contacts to support a treaty that favors our allies in Brazil or maintain the status quo is still an open question.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.2.desc:
“Let me assure you again my friend, the US has nothing to fear from these negotiations,” the Bolivian oligarch said as he took a puff from the Havana cigar, the smoke drifting off to join the dirty air of the New York skyline. FBI Special Agent David Atlee Phillips nodded trying to conceal a smile, the meeting with Antenor Patiño was going splendidly. The heir to the tin empire of his father Simón Patiño 'the Andean Rockefeller' had in short order dismissed many of his bosses' worries about the Transandean Treaty negotiations.

“My compatriots would not dare consider cutting you Yanquis out of Bolivia, our relationship with the states is ironclad, think of this as the other parties fighting over the scraps”.

Phillips chuckled. “Of course, the US still has an interest in those scraps. It would seem to be in both our interests to ensure our partners in Brazil come away victorious.”

Patiño looked Phillips in the eyes his expression losing its previous softness. “It can be done, but I wouldn't be so hasty my friend, there are many forces at work in my homeland. Malcontents and foreign agitators writhe like maggots in our floorboards. The neutrality of Bolivia has staved off the worst of these vermin, but if Brazil were to gain the upper hand... well I can't see the jackboots in Buenos Aires just standing by”.

“So perhaps a treaty that favors no side would ensure future stability?” Phillips said.

“Perhaps... Or perhaps the time of plenty in Bolivia will come to an end regardless,” Patiño said shrugging “There is a reason I spend my time in your hotels and not on my estate. It's not for the fresh air.” Harding thought for a moment on the oligarch's words before.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.2.a: “This is too big of a chance to pass up. Tell your friends to ensure the Brazilians get what they want.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.2.b: “Breaking the balance of power could be too risky, let's push for a more neutral treaty.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.3.desc:
SECRET/[?global.date.GetDateStringNoHour]

FROM: FBI DIRECTOR J. EDGAR HOOVER
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: UPRISINGS IN BOLIVIA

1. Bolivia has entered a state of low-level civil war. Following a coup against the neutral former oligarchic regime, General Ovando of the Bolivian army taken control of the government aligning the country firmly with our allies in Brazil. The new regime faced immediate resistance from insurgent organizations and organized labor. Mining industry halted by strikes and sporadic violence. Insurgent organizations express anti-American sentiment and sympathies for the fascist powers. Evidence of substantial backing from hostile foreign powers including Argentina and Germany. Preserving access to Bolivia's heavy metal deposits critical to American strategic interests.

2. HUMINT collected from contacts within the Bolivian economic elite indicate that Argentina has been supporting radical labor movements in Bolivia for years to be used in case of a Bolivian abandonment of neutrality. It is common knowledge that a large-scale network of Nazi-aligned agents in Latin America exists. HUMINT and SIGINT from intercepted diplomatic cables indicate this network is increasing activity in Bolivia.

3. The survival of the Ovando government would ensure the stability of heavy metal mining critical to US strategic interests and undermine the ongoing infiltration of the continent by hostile outside powers. Bureau has plans to provide covert material assistance to government, including the creation of paramilitary counterinsurgency organizations to root out rebels and Nazi spies.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.4.desc:
For all the layers of bureaucracy and formality, people like Tony Poe always made Special Agent Phillips feel the differences between the Bureau and the Gestapo slip away. A burly man with a wicked grin and a greasy receding hairline, Poe looked more street tough than an intelligence officer. The gaggle of mercenaries and thugs he had put together for this operation wouldn't look out of place in maximum security. This was what the times demanded though. As the chaos in Bolivia was showing, sometimes the world needed a sharp kick in the gut. From a hidden black site deep in the jungles of Brazil, Poe had set to work creating a paramilitary unit for just such a purpose. Poe dabbed the last sizzling remains of his cigar onto the table, the grunting sounds of brawling in the yard outside provided a fitting ambiance.

He gave a leopard grin at Phillips, looking him straight in the eye, “The training was tough for sure, but I would bet I've put together the finest collection of grade-A killers this side of the equator. Now it's just a matter of pointing them at the enemy.” Phillips nodded. This was a question he had been pondering for a while now. Bureau resources in Bolivia were unfortunately limited.

The obvious course of action would be to have Poe's band rove the countryside rooting out insurgents and striking fear into their supporters. But on the other hand, recent evidence has come to light of another threat: A network of German agents embedded in the country training their own death squads, and as the adage said sometimes you needed monsters to fight monsters.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.4.a: “Where you're going there will be plenty of skulls to crack.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.4.b: “Hope your men are ready for some wild Nazi hunting.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.5.desc:
Álvaro crawled in the mud, nails digging into the sodden earth. “Please,” he muttered, more to God than his pursuer, who stamped through the mud with leisurely cruelty. “Please,” he muttered, trying to drag himself up and walk on broken legs. “Please,” he muttered through choked sobs, getting out one last word before his pursuer stepped over him and put a .38 round through his skull.

“Alright,” Tony Poe said, “enough playing with your fucking food.” The paramilitary shrugged with a faint smile, and then returned inside the bar. Poe brought up a cigar and took a long puff. Then he snuffed and bagged up the cigar, not wishing to leave any evidence of his presence here, and walked back into the bar. Poe was leading the rearguard covering the tracks of his comrades. He stepped over the corpse of another striker. It was a turkey shoot in these workers' favourite bar; half of them didn't see it coming, and half of them couldn't do anything about it. Even those that brought up their guns were too drunk to shoot straight. Poe's boys had only one wounded among their ranks tonight.

One of the paramilitaries had finished spray-painting their scapegoat's mark on the south wall. The burning torch in hand had to be drawn with care, so that no observer could confuse it for anything but the symbol of the Bolivian Falangist Party. Or Society. Poe had already forgotten what their name was. He didn't care; the important thing was the symbol, which he'd committed to memory, and knew that the artist had too. By the time that the police arrived, Poe's boys were long gone.

First responders closed off the street and preserved as much of the crime scene as they could. The attending detectives soon discovered shell casings along both sides of the bar's front door. They matched with World War 2 hand-me-down guns, the kind that the Falangists somehow kept getting their hands on. Rumours that the killers were FBI-trained faded in the midst of this evidence.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.5.a: It made people feel more comfortable with supporting the US' favoured dictator.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.6.desc:
“His name's El Caballero Negro,” said Tony Poe, throwing the report on the FBI man's table. He held it into the light of his desk lamp, one of the few sources of illumination in this dusty, smoke-filled backroom—were it not for the desk lamp and the clerestory windows, it would be pitch black. “Big-time drug runner, coke mostly, some guns, with a fleet of planes criss-crossing the continent. Plenty of airports, too. He'd been on our watchlist for some time once we got wind of another name of his, the kind that nobody said to his face.”

“El Sol Negro,” said David Atlee Phillips, adjusting his glasses as he skimmed over the report.

“Bingo. With a name like that, I figured he had to have some German connections. We kept digging, and boom, there he is with some Nazi big-shots.”

“Abwehr?”

“Something like that. Anyway, I got a guy in the organisation who says the Nazis are fucking him. Something about back taxes or some shit.” Poe leant in closer. “Now, a guy like that cares about one thing: cash. And under the Nazis, he's getting bled out.”

Phillips stared at Poe through the cigar smoke haze. “You're suggesting we bandage him?”

“Shit, wouldn't be the first time you boys made a deal like this.”

“That was different. That was-” Phillips stopped himself. Poe could see his eyes flick left to right, observing an internal argument that he lost. “Fine. Fine.” He pushed the report back. “But do it quietly. The last thing we need is for Germany to learn about our involvement. And make sure that we can remove him if need be.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.6.a: “Relax,” Poe said. “I get you. No blowback.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.7.desc:
SECRET[?global.date.GetDateStringNoHour]

FROM Agent Agee FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: Situation in Paraguay

1. Paraguay led by fascist strongman Higinio Morínigo is ongoing threat to our interests in Southern Cone and inroad for Nazi infiltration yet it is internally weak. Fascist regime relies on support base that is less committed than initially believed.

2. Our Bureau is in limited contact with opposition groups inside the country through (REDACTED) though our stronger links are with exiled opposition group FULNA, currently stationed in Uruguay, remnants of our previous (See attempt Report on Guaíra Falls incident). They are ideologically divided and skeptical of Bureau cooperation but have potential as unconventional fighters.

3. The Fascist regime in Paraguay still relies on the foundations of the previous more moderate political order. Many in government hold no sympathy or in some cases outright hostility to fascism. The Colorado Party is still moderate at the local level. German money holds much of the regime together. Military is uncommitted and join either side in a conflict, primary concern for the nation overall. Should a crisis befall Morínigo it is likely he would be ousted from office. Much of internal opposition are unfriendly and anti-democratic. Our Bureau can use opposition contacts in the event of a crisis to help speed up Morínigo's fall.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.8.t: Another Stone on the Path to Paraguayan Democracy
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.8.desc:
The safehouse was just outside the real center of the city, just far enough so that Agent Phillip Agee could wash himself of any pursuers in the narrow winding alleyways. The door opened and he was let inside. The men were strewn around, several with bandages. The leader stepped up to him, he wore a smile but had a furrowed brow.

“So it seems like we were able to fix you up a real nice place here. You know we also fixed up teaching some other boys the ropes back in Brazil for you. Looks like things are really starting to come together.” Agent Agee looks the leader up and down.

“Yes. You have been of great use. The people of Paraguay thank you for helping us take off the chains of our oppressors.” He pauses before continuing. “Still there are a lot of people hanging onto our movement, Febreristas, liberals, you and your friends as much as you do help us, you keep forcing these people onto us who are just looking to exploit and subvert the liberation of Paraguay to their own ends.”

Agent Agee pauses for a second. “Look, you gotta face reality here, you're talking a big game here but let's face reality just for a minute here. From where I'm standing you need all the help you can get, even from liberals, or federalistas, or anyone else, you have to play nice.”

The leader's smile fully disappeared as he stared blankly at Agent Agee for a second. “You, Americans, you don't know anything, you're just looking for another market to open up for you, another nation to-” He stops. “Thank you for your continued support.”

As Agent Agee made his way back to the embassy he noted to himself. The radical left wing of FUNLA may indeed be more of a liability than an asset with their inability to form productive relationships with all other forces.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.8.a: Perhaps some stones will be thrown.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.9.desc:
The agent sat behind the desk in his hotel room, gazing over the plaza that was in view before him through the window. He could see the middle class of Asunción walking backwards and forwards, scurrying to their meetings and shopping trips. He took a sip of coffee. He had spent the last few days travelling under an alias, making contact with figures in the insurgency. He had finally collected enough intel to make a decision on where the FBI could place its resources. This work suited him. The travelling and the luxury hotels, and the play-acting under an assumed identity. He sighed a contented sigh, and drew the curtains.

Opening a briefcase he lay the intel out across his desk. He weighed up the maps and data relating to the Bush War against the documents pertaining to the available resources. He had already come to a few conclusions in his time in Brazil and Paraguay, and took the next few hours to weigh up the options against the intel. Ultimately it seemed to him that there were two possibilities - either spread resources out widely to help the insurgency, or focus on disrupting the activities of FULNA. Those socialists were proving to be a real cause of anxiety for many in the Bureau, and his data gathering had shown that their strength was very real. They were also clearly wary of American influence, especially due to the credibility that Che Guevara had within the movement.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.10.desc:
The men of Paraguay's National Police didn't much need to shout or assure when they left the outpost: Their hands were held firmly high, and that was all Tony Poe gave a damn about. Casings rolled across the ground, but only a handful, the unlucky few who'd met Uncle Sam's dogs first being the only ones who needed to die today.

“They're all pretty well-behaved, yeah. Lookin' like some more greenhorns for our rebels, none of these fellas give a damn for Morínigo. Yeah, I'll have 'em over the border, Over.”

Slinging his M14 over shoulder, the special agent looked like any field grunt. It was another 'training' op he'd taken a more personal role in than his orders specified, and by damn was it another good one. The FBI never argued with results.

Suddenly, things picked up a bit. Stumbling, sun-weathered captives in scrappy garbs were dragged out of cells and thrown onto the dirt, one after the other. Poe's men announced: “Hey, we've got reds! Rojos!” The Paraguayans, now at ease and with fewer guns pointed their way than the bound men, chuckled.

Well, maybe not the only ones.

“FULNA supporters, right? Been rounded up and workin' here?” Poshepny gestured for confirmation, and received it from the policemen and his lieutenant. Already, some of the paramilitaries were flipping off their safeties—most hadn't needed to when they took the station.

“Alright, then, I want you to take these out back and smoke the lot of 'em. 'Fraid we ain't got any use for these comrades. Vint, catch up to us when your guys have finished burials.”
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.10.a: REPORT: SUCCESSFUL LIBERATION OF REGIME POSITIONS
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.11.t: To Live and Die in Asunción
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.11.desc:
It was dark, a rathole buried so deep not even Morínigo had eyes on it, but it was her's. She lit a cigarette as the man at the end of her bed buttoned up his shirt, closing up fabulous muscles. He wasn't like her other client; they had a much deeper relationship, a special one. She felt his eyes strip her for parts, taking in her smoke, before she finally spoke.

“I saw the milico again. Same time, Sunday after Church, it felt different. He talked for some time afterwards; I pushed the same pressure points like you told me, and it must have worked this time. He said he had doubts that Morínigo could stop this chaos, and he heard his officer friends whisper similar sentiments.”

He waited intently, familiar with how her information game worked by now, as he flexed big strong arms. She could see it in his eyes; she knew by now not to keep him waiting, stubbing out her cigarette on the wall before continuing.

“He told me they were also worried about the Chaco, that with more and more forces being deployed elsewhere to deal with the guerrillas, and that the Bolivians could get an in.” The man on the bed relaxed, fully dressed again, before getting up and walking to the door. His arm moved to open it, but was restrained by her's, a weak presence.

“Please, I don't know how much more of this I can take; what would happen if the officer knew I was a spy for the Americans... take me with you.”

“If you're mine, you're safe. I'll get you out of here, I promise.” He shook off her arms and left. Of course, it was a lie. He had a wife and four kids in Atlanta, and she was far too useful here anyway, but as for the information...
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.11.a: ...sent to FULNA for the most damage possible.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.11.b: ...sent to the Liberals to best secure our interests.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.12.desc:
“Welcome to Paraguay, Ambassador,” a jet black-tuxedoed man said, walking in for a handshake and back to the embassy. “Special Agent David Phillips, FBI. Hope you had a good flight.”

Harry Stimpson politely smiled back. “Can't complain, anyway.” He noted the comparatively solid, modern building from the reports, the U.S. Eembassy. It stood out from the pastel-colored storefronts with far fewer bullet holes and signs of damage, save for a scattering of broken glass here and there. “I'm more worried about having complaints here in the city. But it looks better than it did in the pictures.”

“Yes, our boys sure have fixed up the place in the past couple months. Would look even worse if we let the commies win, but hey, we stopped that from happening too.”

The new ambassador to Paraguay smirked. “Not only that, we've got a new friendly government. I mean, we could really do something here. Brazil's a country away, our biggest ally this side of the Americas, a government we can get along with and little opposition to get in the way. I don't see what we can't do now that Old Glory's flying high.”

“I wouldn't be so sure about ”little opposition“, Ambassador. Sure, FULNA lost a war, but that doesn't mean they don't have supporters. Lots of anti-American activity, and Argentina is just across the river, even closer than Brazil. We do, however, have one ace up our sleeve. Follow me.”

He gestured to a door with a small window, through which Stimpson could discern several swastika-emblazoned dossiers. They filed in, and the ambassador's eyes flitted from pile to new pile of German titles and text. Argentina might cause trouble, but they were not the owners of decades of Nazi intelligence Morínigo left behind.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.13.desc:
David Atlee Phillips watched the treelines and boxes on the Paraguayan border spin beneath him, the roaring rotor blades above washing every other thought away. FBI wetworks extraordinaire Tony Poe himself sat beside him, to the chagrin of literally everybody else. Even his smirk unsettled the man: Phillips often wondered if there was any soul left behind those sunglasses.

“That's a herd of people if I've ever seen one,” Poe remarked, gesturing toward the sprawling refugee camp where hundreds gathered to cross into Brazil. “No. A colony. Heh, Bush War's got them all running.” He had a point, somewhere. It was a massive camp. The helicopter veered left.

“I was with the guerrillas,” Poe continued. “When things died down, they all came here, fleeing. But they should be fighting like the Dominicans in Puerto Plata. Listen, we'll take the enemy back to Asunción. I've got operatives ready.”

“I don't know, Tony,” Phillips quickly interjected. He detected the man's internal rage rise as he continued speaking. “There's not a whole lot to show that these kinds of ops work and the insurgent funding and all the rest of it? They're not doing any fighting, things are static, I mean, what are we doing here? It's a waste of...”

Poe glared at Phillips, kicking the seat in frustration. “Really? You too? God fucking damn it, Dave, just like those Washington suits, only working with half-measures. If it weren't for them, we wouldn't be in this mess. If we don't win, that's on you and them. I don't care what the brass says.” He sulked, turning to the window.

Phillips stared out the window, biting back his thoughts. He had the power to reprimand him, but a useful loose cannon was still useful. Let him dig his own grave before bringing out the shovels.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.13.a: It's a miracle they didn't wrestle each other out.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.14.desc:
SECRET/[?global.date.GetDateStringNoHour]

FROM Agent Borenstein FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: Annexation Referendum in Guiana-Cayenne

1. The Brazilian military authority in former French Guiana-Cayenne has announced a referendum in the coming months on a potential annexation into Brazil. This would constitute a realignment of Brazilian military presence and reopen questions about U.S. support of the Brazilian government's role there.

2. The Bureau has been informed of the announcement which recently appeared in local newspapers. The Brazilian Ambassador in Washington has also reached out to REDACTED to confirm.

3. After the fall of France in 1940, a joint American-Brazilian allied occupation was run in French territories in South America, but power has since consolidated in the Brazilian military which maintains a strong presence in the region. Local tensions and a growing Brazilian settler program catalyzed a decision to end the occupation by a vote to decide the nation's future.

While Brazil is nominally a global partner, President Adhemar de Barros has shown hostility to American interests and a successful annexation would be considered an international setback. The controversial nature of the occupation has also drawn extensive criticism from those who view the U.S. as having played a role in it.

4. The FBI has already contacted local labor movements, namely REDACTED, and various political organizations in the region. Substantial funding remains available to support the anti-annexation campaign, as well as ensure such engagement would not damage or compromise American involvement.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.15.desc:
Laughter, howls, chants, and drinks overflowed the establishment in Cayenne. Though, among all of it was a table that was distinct. The chair squeaked as one of the last of the Creole men to show up finally did so.

“Finally, Bruno! Any later and we'd have to kick you out of the union-” Those who had arrived beforehand let out a small chuckle before returning back to their discussions at hand. “I mean, think about it, with this 'referendum' we might as well be the Czechoslovakia of the Amazon. Adhemar wants to repeat what hitler did with us.” The greeter piped up, another man sighing before getting his turn to speak.

“Apparently that's obvious enough to have got the boss up and arms about it. He was always neutral on it and now he's all 'let's give them a thrashing in the referendum!' and getting anyone he can to vote for independence.”

“Well, I think all of us have seen those posters-” The man's eyes darted to the one on the dartboard, the poster was one of Adhemar with the mustache of Hitler slapped onto him in a way that was as equally comedical and truthful.

“You know-” Another man got his turn to speak, his hand putting down the now empty glass, and moving his finger to the poster. “Why don't we show the bastard and his cronies moving in here, taking our jobs, flooding in so that they can fucking take our country that it won't be so easy.” Their cheers filled the bar, the men stumbling out with the best weapon they could get, mostly glass bottles. A danger to good people, they were not. The union men's thoughts deviated as they gripped their weapons tighter.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.15.a: A danger to the skulls of Brazilian scabs and fascists, they were.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.16.desc:
You know, when Jorge first heard that he'd be sent on some propaganda trip in Cayenne, he almost puked. Spreading Adhemar's bullshit in an area filled with people who hated Brazil? Pass. It's not like he voted for that slimy bastard anyway, why the hell would he peddle his narrative? But then Jorge realized something. See of all his issues with the President, his propensity for giving certain... gifts wasn't one of them. Money exchanged hand, some of it with Jorge, and through a few nods and delicate wording, Jorge was convinced of the necessity of such a mission.

See Brasília didn't care what Jorge and his coworkers were doing so long as the right reports were reported and the right stamps were stamped. So Jorge and his companions decided instead to take a well-deserved break from such arduous bureaucratic work. Afterall, you can't change the people's opinions without knowing the people, and where better to learn than in their bars and brothels. Oh, Jorge has to go, they've got reservations at some local inn and he promised he'd do shots. Wouldn't want to make him a liar, would you?
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.16.a: Changing hearts and minds, one drink at a time.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.17.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM THE VENEZUELA OFFICE OF THE FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT
SUBJECT: IMPENDING VENEZUELAN ELECTIONS

Following the ousting of the dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez, Venezuela is currently under the rule of Wolfgang Larrazábal. Previously responsible for helping restore democratic rule, Larrazábal is nearing the end of his term in office. Our intelligence indicates three parties in prime place to take the Presidency soon.

The Democratic Republican Union, the incumbent party, is seen by many local commentators as the favourite to win thanks to Larrazábal's successes in office. The party is generally in favor of liberal values and considered compatible with the OFN. However, there is also a significant socialist contingent within the group, anathematic to the military.

The other most noteworthy party is Democratic Action, a favourite of many after their slim defeat in the last election. They are a Gaitanist party in favor of greater cooperation with us to counter the spread of fascism and secure democratic rule. This has attracted the ire of Venezuela's military, many of whom are still sympathetic to Pérez Jiménez.

Last and likely least of our concerns is the Independent Electoral Political Organization Committee. A moderate and centrist faction, the party is often seen by local pundits as a distinct contrast to the more left-wing inclinations of the other parties. Led by Rafael Caldera, his diplomatic cool-headedness is likely to aid in delicate matters, such as the Essequibo.

Our office advises that only one of these parties is backed out of budgetary concerns, and to avoid overly frustrating our Venezuelan partners, but the choice rests with you.
strings.USA_FBI_LATAM.17.a: The invisible hand of freedom prepares an intervention.
strings.USA_CIA_UK.101.desc:
“You're backing Lemass?” Tom McShane was frankly at a loss for words. For weeks, O'Connelly had agreed that Ireland needed to be truly independent. Subservience to the Americans was just as bad as to the Germans, and the economic collapse had shown just how bad indeed that had been. He had been one of the votes McShane was most certain of. But now, in McShane's office, he seemed to have changed his tune.

“I've taken a closer look at what the United States have done for Canada and Australia,” O'Connelly remarked, fidgeting with his shiny new watch as if he was entirely too anxious for the meeting to be over. He leaned in, his voice quieter. “Listen, Tommy. It's better the Yanks than the Germans or the Brits, and without someone keeping us afloat, it'll be the Germans or Brits who scoop us back up. We might as well try something new, eh?”

When no immediate response was given, O'Connelly clapped the stunned McShane on the back and briskly fled the office. He mumbled something about how he needed to meet the missus for dinner, but McShane was barely paying attention. O'Connelly was only the most recent in a long line of defections to Lemass, and not a single one could be explained. Had McShane missed something?

As he remained quietly in thought, a noise floated through the open window. O'Connelly was starting his car, preparing to go home for the day. As McShane watched the older man struggle with his keys, a thought struck him. Hadn't that car been red just the other day?
strings.USA_CIA_UK.101.a: Something suspicious is going on here...

strings.USA_RDC_Explanation:
£General_Decision_Linebreak


The odd couple coalition of the £GFX_rd_r_texticon Republican and £GFX_rd_d_texticon Democratic parties has rapidly become a fixture of American politics since its creation in the late 50s. It results from two beleaguered political establishments keen to preserve their power in the face of £GFX_npp_texticon surging political insurgency, and stands to only lose ground.

The alliance of elephants and asses runs on horse-trading and backroom dealing in smoke-filled offices to ensure that the wings of its two constituent parties remain satisfied. A gauntlet spanning from conservative Republicans to staunch New Dealers and mercurial Southerners, changing as factions rise and fall with the national mood.

Fulfilled promises, popular legislation, and palms greased with the pork and political capital of a successful Presidency will be key to keeping the £GFX_rd_texticon R-D Coalition in lockstep. Failure will risk this nation's very stability.
strings.USA_NPP_Explanation:
£General_Decision_Linebreak


The odd coalition of Progressives, Nationalists, Populists, and other... unmentionables that exist beneath the banner of the £GFX_npp_texticon National Progressive Pact has emerged as one of the most surprising political forces in the United States. Yet, the unlikely alliance between dissatisfied ex-Democrats and irate Patriots has produced the first real threat to the £GFX_rd_r_texticon Republican and £GFX_rd_d_texticon Democratic duopoly in a generation.

The ill-defined nature of the Pact is its strength and its Achilles heel. Those willing to vote for the Pact out of disgust with the establishment may think twice should the many parts of the NPP fail to muzzle the leaders of their more... extreme associates.

A well-disciplined pact will offer the American people a true alternative to the feckless Democrats and incompetent Republicans. On the other hand, an ill-disciplined pact will only validate claims about £GFX_npp_texticon NPP serving as stalking horse for radicals and extremists of every stripe.

strings.USA_MAD_impeach.1.desc:
Joe's office was a relatively small one, especially for someone who worked in the state department, though he liked it all the same. What he did not like was people barging into his office, both for sake of professionalism and because when they did the door nearly scraped the front end of his desk. Unfortunately, today would not be as calm a day as Joe would have liked, the door slamming against the wall as his superior, Andy, tramped into his office, slamming a tabloid onto his desk, “JAPANESE AGENTS TEACH ANTI-OFN REBELS WITH AMERICAN EQUIPMENT!” it read, with a photo printed into the top right of a training camp and crates clearly labeled with a hand and torch. Joe just looked up at Andy's fuming face and grimaced.

“Afternoon, Andy, why is this my problem?” Joe asked, placing his pen against the paper he'd been signing.

“Your job is to keep this secret. What the fuck happened?!” Andy pushed the cheap paper and ink across the table, right in front of Joe. After picking up the paper and reading for a moment, Joe held the paper so Andy could see it.

“First of all; this is page five. Not front page news. Second-” Joe flashed the cover to Andy, “-this is not The New Yorker, this is not The Washington Post. This is the Albuquerque Daily. How'd you even find this? Third of all-” Joe turned back to the photo in question, “-this could be anything. The Japanese took a captured Malayan supply drop and sent it to their friends. They leaked a doctored photo to some no-name paper so they spread propaganda. We can spin this basically any way we want to, because they have nothing against us.” Joe finished, only calming Andy slightly.

“Joe, this happens again, we might not be so lucky. We've gotta decrease support to Madagascar.” Andy said, halfheartedly. Joe sighed.

“A nice idea, Andy, but that's not my call. I hide what gets out, but the more we send, the harder that'll be.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.1.a: Let's try to keep this quiet.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.2.desc:
He was having a bad day, that much was clear. Despite the president's attempt at a jovial wave and the presence of his fourteen-year-old daughter gripping his hand, Nixon walked to the end of the White House Drive like a beast approaching prey. He looked at the reporters there. “How are you fellows doing? I was just taking, uh, Tricia here for a little stroll.”

“Mr. President, Theodore White, Time Magazine. Do you have any comment at all on story recently reported in the Albuquerque Daily on US weapons arming Japanese soldiers in Madagascar?”

Tricia attempted to hide behind her father, only to be pulled back in front with a small but perceptible yank. “Oh, well, you know. I can't really comment on matters of national security, especially with the little ones around.” He gave a forced laugh.

“The photos, though—?”

“Photos. Photos. You know, there's a great deal of photos taken all the time. Some of them doctored. Nasty stuff.” There was the flash of a camera. The president shifted to holding his daughter by the shoulders, appearing for a moment like a gargoyle perched over her. “I just want to encourage members of Congress and, uh, the media to avoid the kind of shrill, irresponsible rhetoric that might damage our national security. We'll get to the bottom of this, but through existing processes.”

Another voice rose from the crowd. “What processes?”

Nixon gave a taut smile. “Well, just before I came out I ordered a meeting of the National Security Council and told my Secretary of State to call a special meeting of the OFN. You better believe I'm working to get to the bottom of this. Now, if you'll excuse me, I think Tricia and I should return to our walk.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.2.a: The reporters continued shouting as the president dragged his daughter across the lawn.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.3.desc:
The jungles of Madagascar buzzed with life around the German compound, isolated as it was; with nothing more than a wood cabin and three posts with a man attached to each in the yard outside, the outpost was spartan, but not useless to the Germans. Of all three men, Steven the contact was whining the loudest, and the most.

“Fuck, man! We're not even supposed to be here, and we get caught! What are we supposed to fucking do-?”

The trio were each tied to a lashing post, though there were only two guards present- the third had driven off to fetch reinforcements to deal with such special “guests”. Carol, the eldest of the three, an operative for the CIA since long before Steven was even born, sat gagged and bound in the heavy jungle heat. He could handle the heat, the bugs, even the gunshot wound burning away at his shoulder. What hurt him most was that he could not tell Steven to shut the fuck up. John, the local expert whinged at Steven's complaining.

“Christ, man, you think your crying's gonna fix this? Because it won't. I'll bet they'll trade us back to the States in no time, that's what always happens to guys like us. Right, Carol?” John asked. He knew the answer was a no, yet he nonetheless hoped any offered solution might give his ears a rest.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.3.a: Relief for them, not the State Department.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.4.desc:
He'd done the best he could, thought White House Press Secretary Herb Klein glumly. For weeks he'd managed to keep the whole Madagascar business out of the national press through a combination of promises, threats, and stalling tactics. He'd told the San Francisco Chronicle that they'd be barred from the White House Press Corps and begged the New York Times for two weeks to preserve national security. Finally, though, the Washington Post had broken. There were pictures of American soldiers in handcuffs on the front page. The president had reamed into him for it and demanded a press conference to control the narrative.

“Alright, alright,” said the pale-faced Klein before swarming reporters. Let's all just settle down and—.“

There was a buzzing of voices from the crowd. A mass of limbs held out microphones and recording equipment. Lights flashed within their bulbs, appearing like the eyes of some terrible insect.

”I have a statement! I have a statement from the president if you'll all just settle down and be decent! Please!“

There was more buzzing but, slowly, the voices began to dissipate.

”Thank you,“ he said when the room had regained composure. ”President Nixon wishes to emphasize that his first priority, as always, is to ensure that all Americans are safe. While he cannot comment on matters of national security, his current focus is on getting back these boys safely. In the meanwhile, we urge the media not to use these men's status as political ammunition. The president is deeply concerned by irresponsible and reckless reporting and the great amount of speculation that he has seen in place of traditional journalism,“ There was a rumble of outrage. Klein began talking faster. ”Once these men are home and safe, we can begin the long and hard process of figuring out how they got there. Until then, the president has no further statements.“
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.4.a: Klein then fled from the crowd like a man fleeing a swarm of angry bees.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.5.desc:
“The one time the fat bastard goes for a walk.” Joe muttered to himself. Nearly running down the hallways of the State Department HQ, Joe was reminded of the feeling he would often endure when searching for his brothers at the bar to bring them home for the night in a childhood long past. Even now, he mused, Joe was forced to search through small groups of gathered hunched reprobates or depressed shambling boozers to find someone to save from the groups- only this time, he did so because he cared for the man, and not because he had to.

The crowds of men and some women were all huddled around lists of names kept in ad-hoc lists around the office. That afternoon, dozens of State Department employees were marched out of their offices or cubicles, and given 10 minutes to pack up what amounted to occasionally decades worth of careers. Needless to say, when word had gotten out, lists of the -effectively- deceased were drawn up by the secretaries who had made note of those who were led out. Joe had been yelling out to find Andy somewhere in the throngs of people on their lunch breaks, trying to uncover which of their coworkers were now gone with the wind. “Over here, Joe!” Someone yelled in the biggest crowd. Pushing forward to the center, Joe began to hear the man who had called on him over the other conversations,

“...not scheduled, these firings don't just happen! Kennedy, that piece of shit... tragic, goddamned- Joe!” the voice called out, “Mr. Abignale! Get over here!” Joe began to cut through the crowd to the voice. Upon inching closer, Joe realized it was one of his subordinates, naturally a luckier one, who was calling to him.

“Mr. Abignale, I just wanna say I'm sorry, I know you and Andy were close, this just cuts too deep,” he said with a look of genuine sadness. Immediately Joe realized what had happened.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.5.a: Another casualty of cleaning one's hands.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.6.desc:
“...As such, the fundamental processes of governance were disregarded, and the rule of law was subverted...” the paper read. Joe's work life had become immensely hectic, almost to the point of absurdity, and his private life had begun to reflect that. Sitting at home, enjoying a solitary moment of calm away from work and with his family, Joe had taken the time to read his copy of The Washington Post. Even away from work, Joe could not escape it. With a defeated sigh, Joe walked to his landline and dialed Andy's personal number. “This is Andy,” the voice on the line muttered, “if this is another journalist, I'm hanging up.” Joe felt a pang of guilt. Andy had spoken a whole sentence without cussing- the man must have been truly defeated.

“Andy, it's Joe. I'm calling to say I'm sorry.”

The line stayed silent awhile. Joe hadn't thought of anything to say, and Andy wasn't sure how to respond.

“Thanks,” Andy said, “but this still cost me my fucking job. Do you still have that Washington Post subscription, Joe?” Joe grunted to the affirmative. “And what did you tell me this wouldn't be, Joe?” Andy half-asked.

Joe sighed. “It wouldn't be on the front page of the Washington Post. And it is.”

Andy let out a light chuckle. “I know it wasn't really your fault- nobody could cover up all that, even with the team we had. Still, thanks for humoring me.”

“Anytime, Andy- this is a shitshow, isn't it? Americans giving cash to the Japanese-? I know that there was a lot more than that, but...”

“Since when would The Post give us a break?” Andy finished. The two men chuckled at the joke, one-part serious, another part sad that it was over for at least half of them.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.6.a: It's all falling apart, but at least I had a friend with me.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.7.desc:
The situation had deteriorated, thought White House Chief of Staff H.R. Haldeman. In the course of a few weeks, the story on Madagascar had gone from the back pages of third-rate newspapers to the International section in major papers to the nightly news. Haldeman stared at the back of his boss's head as Cronkite intoned on allegations of illegal shipments.

“This isn't good, Bob,” said the president. “The press will fuck me for this. They'll bend me over a table and fuck me like an old whore.”

Haldeman waited in silence. Nixon changed the channel to ABC and grunted approvingly at a story on protests in Quebec.

“At least Cochran's still giving us a good shake.”

The broadcast continued. Nixon changed the channel again. A blonde woman presented dish soap to the camera.

“Sir, do you want me to tell Klein to make another statement?”

The president waved a hand dismissively. “No, no, the bastard would find some way to put his foot in his mouth. I don't need to clean up any more messes.” The screen flashed to the smiling face of a young girl. “Get...Safire. Tell him I want to make a speech in the morning. We'll say the allegations are troubling, that we support a full nonpartisan FBI probe to get the people answers. Maybe mention my work on the whole Hiss thing and how that will be a picnic in comparison. Some stupid bullshit like that.”

“Of course, Mr. President. Any other messages you'd like me to deliver?”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.7.a: “Tell the assholes at State to bury this thing. I don't want any more stories reaching the press.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.8.desc:
When he'd first arrived in the United States House of Representatives almost two years ago, Nationalist Party Representative John B. Anderson had talked a lot about integrity. While so many men in Illinois were willing to sacrifice their principles to the Democratic machines that controlled the state, Anderson had vowed to remain true, to remain decent, to remain honest. He would speak truth to the powerful.

Which is why he now found himself huddled in the backroom of a restaurant on the outskirts of DC, surrounded by a ragtag group of young congressmen from all across the political spectrum.

“So,” he said lamely, “Nixon.”

“Nixon indeed,” said Democratic Congressman Mo Udall. Even sitting, he towered over the other representatives. “I know we all have our disagreements, but I think we can all agree that what's emerged from Madagascar is a disgrace. American dollars are financing the same men who attacked us at Pearl Harbor.”

There was a murmuring of angry voices.

“Mo's right,” said Anderson. “What we need now is action. Real action. No empty speeches. No censures. Real action.” He looked conspiratorially around the room, aware of the magnitude of what he was about to say. “We may even need to start drafting Articles of Impeachment.”

More murmuring. Udall cast his unlikely allies a look. “Most of us here are freshmen representatives, men with junior positions on our committees, but even that is enough to start moving things forward. If we can build a movement in Congress, if we can make the outcry loud enough, we can force an investigation and get rid of the most crooked president in our nation's history.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.8.a: Unlikely allies in an unlikely conspiracy.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.9.desc:
It was a warm night in Washington but Secretary of State William Rogers felt cold. Sitting at his desk, he found himself reading and re-reading a notice, delivered earlier that day, from the Capitol.

“Pursuant to lawful authority, YOU ARE HEREBY COMMANDED to appear before the SENATE COMMITTEE ON FOREIGN RELATIONS of the Senate of the United States at their committee room, 419, in the New Senate Office Building to testify on the Administration's activities regarding Madagascar...”

A groan escaped the Secretary's mouth as he scanned through row after row of the neatly typed subpoena, endowed with all the might of the United States Congress. In addition to his personal testimony, the committee compelled him to provide documents, logs, records, memoranda, correspondence, news summaries... The list went on. They even wanted his personal meeting diary.

Rogers blanched. His eyes fell onto the final lines.

“Hereof fail not, as you will answer your default under the pains and penalties in such cases made and provided.”

He got up and moved toward the dark window. It had taken weeks, but Congress's patience with the Administration had finally run out. The Committee on Foreign Relations was going to have the Sergeant-at-Arms detain him if he did not appear. It would go through all his files and refer the Justice Department to pursue criminal charges. Nixon would demand noncompliance, would demand that he stall, but what good would that do? Was he really willing to risk his legacy for a man like Richard Nixon?

Rogers stared out into the black. Then, he returned to his desk, moved toward his typewriter, and began to compose a message.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.9.a: Chairman Fulbright, members of the committee...
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.10.t: NYT: Rogers Quits Sec State Position, Admits to Misleading Congress
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.10.desc:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—William D. Rogers resigned as Secretary of State today following testimony before the U.S. Senate Committee on Foreign Relations in which he confessed to “unintentionally misleading” the body about the illicit selling of arms to finance Japanese and Malagasy forces.

The development, capping weeks of denial by the State Department, represents a stunning downfall for a man once talked about as a potential presidential candidate. The confession shocked his closest associates and has precipitated one of the largest crises in Washington since the end of the War.

“I have informed the president of my intention to resign my office, effective immediately,” Mr. Rogers declared in his opening remarks. “I wish to comply fully with the Congress in their efforts to investigate allegations of misconduct in Madagascar.”

Over the next two hours, senators from both coalitions pushed the former secretary about his conduct and the extent to which President Nixon was aware of either the arms deals or cover-up. While professing his own innocence in the affair, Rogers alluded to members of the White House staff involved in devising the “blueprints and plans concerning the scandal.”

His remarks are likely to increase pressure on the White House to testify and further embolden those members of Congress who have advocated for the impeachment of the president.

While no statement from the White House was available at time of publication, a source from within the White House indicated that the president had hired New York attorney John N. Mitchell to serve as his personal legal counsel.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.10.a: In his office, Vice President Kennedy threw down the paper in anger and disgust.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.11.desc:
Democratic Representative Mo Udall made a signal to House Judiciary Chairman Chauncey Reed, aware, as he did so, of the eyes of the entire room upon him. He adjusted his tie to look respectable before he detonated the explosive resolution.

The old man sighed. “The gentleman will state his motion.”

“Mr. Chairman, I move to introduce House Resolution 843.”

The Chair paused, as if he could stop the future by simply refusing to speak. Then, reality returned. In a miserable voice, he spoke, “The clerk will report the resolution.”

“House Resolution 843, impeaching Richard Nixon, President of the United States for high crimes and misdemeanors in the House of Representatives, [?global.date.GetDateStringNoHour]. Mr. Udall submitted the following resolution, which was referred...”

The clerk droned on. Over the next few days, Establishment leaders would raise objections and force protest votes. Udall was sure there would be speeches to delay the proceedings or to beg members to abandon this course of action. There would be attempts to cajole Representative Udall's activist cabal with more hearings, with backroom promises for senior appointments in the RDC. There would be fiery threats from the White House, threatening to end his career and have him blacklisted.

But he didn't care. The wheels of history were turning and Udall had done his math. He knew there were enough members on the Judiciary Committee willing to move the resolution forward. Plus, he had one piece of information that no one else had yet, that would make impeachment seem like an inevitability, a necessity:
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.11.a: His brother, Secretary of the Interior Stewart Udall, had resigned in protest one hour ago.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.12.desc:
Speaker of the House John McCormack looked and felt like death as he stared down from the rostrum at the assembled body. For days, there had been debate in the Judiciary Committee over Articles of Impeachment for Richard Nixon. When the committee had finally voted to move the measure forward to the full chamber, it had fallen on him to find some way of dealing with the vote in a fair and even-handed way. His decision to privately tell RDC representatives to “vote their conscience” had led to angry, late-night calls from the president. His decision to allow a full floor debate before that vote had led Udall and the rest of his freshman cabal to accuse McCormack of delaying, of defending a failing status quo.

Still, he was determined to be fair. He was determined to handle the second impeachment vote in American history with grace and dignity. He was determined not to let himself be flattened by the terrible weight of history. As Udall finished his fiery final statement, the Speaker nodded to the clerk.

“All time for general debate has expired. Pursuant to House Resolution 843, the previous question is ordered on the resolution as amended. The question is on adoption. The question of adoption of the resolution as amended shall be divided between the six articles: His approval and acquiescence in shipping arms without congressional approval; his approval and acquiescence in covert actions conducted by the Central Intelligence Agency...”

It went on. McCormack banged his gavel to signal the start of a fifteen-minute voting period and watched as members moved across the room. For once, there were no signs of party divisions among the NPP, who were all solidly united in favor of impeachment. Among his own members, though, he made a miserable note of deep factions emerging. Richard Nixon had left the once-stable RDC more divided than ever.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.12.a: With 238 voting in favor and 190 voting against, Richard Milhous Nixon has been impeached.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.13.desc:
JK: John, that House of yours has caused more grief dealing with that silly bastard—. Did you see the Post this morning?

JM: Uh, yes, Jack I did.

JK: I'd been talking to Udall about resigning at the start of this whole mess and now he and his brother's going around doing a victory lap over it, cutting me out. It's crazy! I can't trust anyone.

JM: Now, Jack, let's hold on before you go on resigning.

JK: No, no. The whole thing is falling apart here. Dick's barricaded himself in the Residence. This new Mitchell bastard is looking for leakers with an axe. Bobby's kept the press at bay so far, but I know if I stay here much longer they're going to start talking about me as “damaged goods” going into '64.

JM: Listen, Jack, I hear you. I know you're frustrated, but we have to think about the here and now. The president is... not himself. I think he called me drunk last night after the impeachment vote. He's a cornered animal and, if he sees no way out, he might start making messes. We could wind up with tanks in DC if you leave and it looks like the Senate will convict.

JK: Jesus Christ, that crazy bastard.

JM: If you don't stay on, the cabinet will fall apart. The RDC will fall apart. Nixon will destroy the country and then himself. I know you have ambitions, but please... stay on. We need you.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.13.a: JK: Goddamnit. What a fucking disaster.
strings.USA_MAD_IMPCH_JFK_tt: The Director of the FBI read through the conversation with mild interest before sending it to the president's chief of staff.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.131.desc:
The two brothers—Bobby and Jack—stood in Bobby's Senate Office. The room was quiet; press attention had centered itself on the Senate chamber where, even now, the Chief Justice of the United States, was preparing for the second impeachment trial in the nation's history.

“Jack, please... don't do this,” said Bobby after a long moment. “You did nothing wrong. You have no reason to lie, especially not to protect a bastard like Nixon. Please...”

The Vice President stared into the pattern in Bobby's carpet.

“You think he'll lash out? Fine. Let him lash out. You think the Republicans will acquit him just so he can burn down the country? That's fine too. We can build something better out of the ashes.” He bent at the waist, trying to catch his brother's gaze. “Don't do this. Don't let him take your integrity from you.”

But Jack shook his head. “I can't, Bobby. I just can't. I wish I could but...” He trailed off. “I can't risk it. There's too much at stake.”

Bobby cursed under his breath and kicked a trash can, which clattered across the room, spilling papers across the carpet. When he spoke again, his voice was full of bitterness and hurt. “You were supposed to be better than this.”

Jack said nothing as Bobby stormed toward the door and slammed it behind him. He sat there in the empty room until his brother's footsteps vanished. Then he rose and made his way toward the Capitol's Senate chamber.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.14.desc:
Vice President John F. Kennedy had none of his characteristic warmth as the Senate Sergeant at Arms swore him in on a Bible. He did not look at the press packed into the gallery nor back into the eyes of his brother, Bobby, seated stone-faced behind him. Instead, he looked up at House impeachment manager Mo Udall.

“Mr. Vice President, I think it's fair to say you've often been excluded from the decision-making processes in the Executive Office. Is that accurate?” Said Udall.

“I would say that Dick and I have had our disagreements.” Kennedy shrugged with a forced casualness. “But I find ways to keep myself in the loop.”

Udall raised an eyebrow. His glass eye gleamed in his skull. “Oh? And did you manage to keep yourself in the loop on the affairs in Madagascar?”

Vice President Kennedy did not give Udall the benefit of a pause or a break in eye contact.“Yes, I did.” His eyes bore into those of the impeachment manager. “Dick and I spoke on it at length. The president and his chief of staff can attest to my involvement in key decision-making.”

“And in your, uh, involvement in key decision-making, Jack,” Udall dropped his name as if it were a curse. Beneath his lawyerly presentation, there was fury and disgust. “Did you witness President Nixon or any of his aides order the sale of arms or other resources to aid the Japanese military?”

“No, Mo, I did not. The president expressed a great sympathy for the Malagasy people's fight for independence, but I did not witness anything that could be construed as an order to provide aid in violation of US law. If any decision was made, it occurred without the knowledge or consent of the president and myself.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.14.a: Udall broke Kennedy's gaze and shook his head, “No further questions from the prosecution.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.15.desc:
“Scott, how are things in the Senate?”

“The, uh, Kennedy testimony has taken the wind out of the liberal's sails, Mr. President,” answered the nasally voice of Pennsylvania's senior senator over the phone. “Lyndon has kept quiet on the whole matter, but I do not believe he plans to let this impeachment affair come up for a full vote when the Senate comes back into session.”

“Thank you, Senator, we'll stay in touch,” Nixon put down the phone, rubbing his temples. He turned to his chief of staff. “Haldeman, do you think we've put this damned thing behind us?”

“I think so, Mr. President,” came the reply. “We'll let the big networks run with the Vice President's testimony, take the pressure off the Senate to act. It's hard to say right now, but in a couple of weeks, this probably won't be anything more than a minor story.”

“All thanks to Kennedy,” Nixon said bitterly. “That Harvard bastard, I know he's planning something. I want daily reports on what he's up to until we're sure he's not scheming with his brother to start a goddamn coup or something.”

“Yes, Mr. President.”
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.15.a: “And make sure there are no more goddamn leaks.”
strings.USA_weak_impeachment_Nixon_tt: Impeachment heads to the senate, dead on arrival.
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.16.desc:
“Mr. Bartlett? Mr. Bartlett, guilty. Mr. Bennett? Mr. Bennett, not guilty. Mr. Bible? Mr. Bible, not guilty...”

H.R. Haldeman listened to the roll call vote blasting through the Oval Office television. “Bible's a good sign. He'd been wavering.”

“No doubt afraid about the Kennedy brat being caught in the crossfire.” The president slurred, gripping his glass of whiskey tight. “Disloyal bastard. He'll pay soon enough.”

The broadcast went on. “Mr. Keating? Mr. Keating, not guilty. Mr. Kennedy?” There was a pause. “Mr. Kennedy?”

“Choke on it.” Nixon spat. He leaned toward the television, spilling his drunk onto the floor. Haldeman eyed the president warily. “Choke on it and die you fucking cocksucker.”

“Mr. Kennedy... not guilty. Mr. La Follette? Mr. La Follette, guilty. Mr. McGovern? Mr. McGovern, guilty...”

The president made a rude remark, but Haldeman was barely listening. Based on the votes so far, the president would avoid the two-thirds needed for removal. Even better, there was a good chance they'd saved the president from receiving a majority on any charge. The RDC had stayed together—if only barely.

“Bastards, the lot of them,” muttered Nixon.

Haldeman pursed his lips. Impeachment would lose the president support, yes, but they could still pull '64 off. They could paint the opposition as pet radicals of Eastern liberalism, the darlings of the New York Times persecuting the president of the Silent Majority. All they needed was to avoid further scandal. All they needed was for the president to pull himself together...
strings.USA_MAD_impeach.16.a: As Nixon raged at his desk, Haldeman made a note to keep the president away from the cameras.
strings.USA_MADCW_Nixon_Impeachment_TT: Nixon will remain President, although his image in the eyes of the public has been tarnished.
strings.USA_NIXON_RESIG_IMPEACHED_B4_TT: The nation knows Nixon has something to hide.
strings.USA_NIXON_RESIG_SAVE_FACE_TT: Nixon leaves disgraced, but without the administration's activities known to the country.
strings.USA_the_nixon_presidency_desc: Senator Nixon has now been proclaimed President Nixon, and with his inauguration through, it's time for a beautiful new decade for America. With the former Axis seemingly facing twilight, and twenty years of policy in America seemingly coming to a head domestically and abroad, this may be the most decisive presidency in American history.
strings.USA_the_campaign_trail_desc: While many claim campaigning should be separate from the presidency, the truth is that one of the most important roles of the President is ensuring his party remains in power, especially so that they may have the decade to rule. Let's make sure Nixon has the time he needs to properly see his vision through.
strings.USA_keep_it_clean_desc: A clean campaign is a good campaign, while maybe not the most effective, President Nixon is a good man, and knows that as an example to the American people he must show them that the rule of law must always win out.
strings.USA_keep_it_clean_flag: By going this path, we'll let some fucking Jew reporters from the New York Times write feel-good stories about us, not that they'll last. None of Sulzberger's boys are ever fucking satisfied with any of the goddamn good we do. All the press wants are sob stories or scandals or puff pieces about the Kennedys. They'll never give us the credit we deserve for saving this country. They'll always try to find some way to tear us down.
strings.USA_campaign_in_the_south_desc: The “Solid South” has been a stronghold of the Democrats for almost a century, and we're not about to let these NPP upstarts take it from us.
strings.USA_reassure_dixiecrats_desc: Many of the Dixiecrats are afraid that if reelected, Nixon would support the Civil Rights movement and even attempt desegregation. We must assure them that this is not the case.
strings.USA_campaign_in_the_west_desc: The West, especially California, is the place most affected by the treaty ports, and by campaigning there Nixon can demonstrate his commitment to retaking them, undercutting one of the NPP's biggest points.
strings.USA_calm_the_progressives_desc: Progressives across the West and North are concerned that Nixon will bend to segregationists and oppose the cause of civil rights, we need to promise them that he will not.
strings.USA_campaign_in_the_north_desc: The great cities of the north are excellent opportunities for Nixon to shore up his support among the urban population, a demographic likely to sympathize with the NPP, and to show the world American democracy in action.
strings.USA_friends_in_big_business_desc: Who are big businesses going to support, the anticapitalist radicals of the NPP or their trusted friends, President Nixon among them, in the Republican-Democratic Coalition?
strings.USA_reestablish_the_party_desc: A divided Coalition is a weak Coalition, and we Republican-Democrats need to focus instead on what unites us: opposing those crazy radicals in the NPP.
strings.USA_bring_back_the_unions_desc: If the unions aren't with us, they're against us! We'll make some promises to protect labor laws and get them to the voting polls.
strings.USA_against_the_NPP_desc: We will encourage all the moderates of America, liberals and conservatives, progressives and segregationists, to unite on one thing: supporting American democracy by opposing the un-American radicals of the NPP.
strings.USA_investigate_NPP_corruption_desc: How did a bunch of nutjob radicals get this much funding? Something smells fishy, let's get to the bottom of it. A full FBI investigation will be conducted on the NPP, and we will crack them wide open for the whole nation to see before they can subvert our democracy!
strings.USA_get_our_hands_dirty_desc: Sometimes, rolling up your sleeves and getting in it is the only way for victory. The NPP wants a war, let's God damn show these sons of bitches one.
strings.USA_steal_their_files_desc: Let's figure out what exactly these proto-Commie proto-Nazi fucks really have going on in their laundry!
strings.USA_the_juiciest_blackmail_desc: The information we have pulled from the NPP has been especially interesting, with money being wired in and out from the oddest of sources... Not American sources. We can use this against them.
strings.USA_wiretap_the_NPP_desc: Stealing their files can only go so far. To find out what illegal activities these fucks are really up to, we'll need to give Hoover a call and start wiretapping the sons of bitches.
strings.USA_estrange_the_democrats_desc: If not for Democrat Joe Kennedy, we wouldn't even be in this whole mess with the NPP and Japan in the first place! Those Democratic sons of bitches must be kept from power if we are to have any chance of winning.
strings.USA_everyone_i_dont_agree_with_is_hitler: Everyone I Don't Agree With is HITLER!
We need to point out the clear ideological connections between the NPP and the Nazis. Some may call this slander, but how can it be slander if it's true?
strings.USA_split_our_enemies_desc: The NPP has a massive divide between its right and left wings, and if we were to stoke tension between the different factions, the NPP would have a much harder time operating.
strings.USA_proto_progressives_desc: One way the NPP appeals to people is by promising so-called “progressive reforms”. Although obviously we will never support such un-American ideas, perhaps we could make promises to do so, because after all, nobody says we have to follow through with them...
strings.USA_turn_the_people_desc: Although the fascists in the NPP may have lots of German cash to spend on propaganda, they will never have as much as the Republican-Democrats, with the support of both big business and the people, can muster.
strings.USA_the_yockeys_desc: The Sovereigns, being clearly a proto-Nazi faction funded by the Germans, are an easy way to discredit the NPP. If we were to make them more prominent in the Pact, it would certainly give us ammunition to use against the rest of the NPP.
strings.USA_wrangle_the_senate_desc: The Senate has been a problem for too long. We need to deal with the blatant disregard for coalition unity and stability among many members of the RDC, even if we have to use... forceful methods to do it.
strings.USA_secure_the_party_desc: All these problems started when some fucks in the RDC decided to stop listening to reason. We must exert complete control over the Coalition, so that none of those fucks can screw up again.
strings.USA_the_civil_rights_dillema_desc: The Civil Rights Movement is tearing apart this nation, and we will need to respond to this crisis if it means keeping America stable. Three sides have come out, one calling for the immediate move towards equalization of all races, one demanding the government immediately stomp down on these protesters and activists, and the President's faction, hoping to ride the wave until the situation calms down and a path is more clear.
strings.USA_begin_integration_desc: Beginning integration and peeling back some Jim Crow laws where we can will only be beneficial to us, and will calm protests and allow us some time to think and move forward.
strings.USA_meet_with_african_leaders_desc: In order to better decide a solution to our issues, we will need to discuss this with the great black thinkers who have been leading their movement. Only together can we decide a solution to this crisis.
strings.USA_the_handshake_with_mlk_desc: Our meetings with the activists are bearing fruit, especially with JFK leading the helm. Less known and hated in black communities than he is in white ones, and eager to find a more progressive solution to this issue, JFK has begun correspondence with one Martin Luther King Jr., who has himself expressed great interest in a meeting. Maybe these two minds can decide on the solution together.
strings.USA_ease_peoples_fears_desc: JFK and MLK agreed on several points, one of which being the necessity for dialogue with anti-integration whites to prevent their alienation, or at least the feeling of it. By easing their fears over integration and promoting MLK as a friendly face of the movement, greatly aided by his religious ties, we may begin to bridge these gaps in our society instead of deepening them.
strings.USA_discuss_with_southern_leaders_desc: Open dialogue with southern leaders would help bridge these gaps further. We need to show them we're willing to listen if we can possibly hope to end these issues.
strings.USA_anti_segregation_propaganda_desc: While we need to open discussion with these southern segregationists, that doesn't mean we can sit idly by and let them turn the nation against us. Pushing a healthy propaganda campaign, through the papers, the airwaves and the radiowaves, will ensure public opinion remains on our side.
strings.USA_desegregate_the_south_desc: It's time to push desegregation in the south. While we've begun hedging and trimming laws where we could to keep the people calm, the only way this crisis can end is if it is eventually defeated everywhere. While we can force nothing, doing what we can where we can will make all the difference.
strings.USA_deploy_the_national_guard_desc: While some areas of the south have taken well to our push for desegregation, others are in urpoar. Riots have become widespread, not only from black groups, but by southerners fighting against them. The National Guard will need to be deployed immediately if order is to be restored.
strings.USA_desegregate_little_rock_desc: While most of the uniformed services have already begun moving towards desegregation, an official blanket order for the Defense Department to fully integrate will finally ensure our Armed Forces remain the embodiment of everything we strive to be and show the federal government's policy on desegregation will be the law of the land moving forward.
strings.USA_southern_riots_desc: Despite our best attempts, widespread rioting has consumed much of the south in response to our progressive measures. A firm and decisive response will be needed, though we'll need to be careful not to go too far unless we want to turn riot into revolt.
strings.USA_a_gentle_hand_across_america_desc: Let us guide the people of America like a father handling his children. They must be moved with words, not just with action, and need to be convinced that we only wish the best for every American in the land.
strings.USA_crack_down_desc: While a gentle hand is necessary, a firm one is as well. In response to murders, lynchings, and other such acts, we must come down with the full fury that only God and the people have bestowed upon us. Let them know, that while we are patient and understanding, we will never allow such injustice to occur against other Americans.
strings.USA_unite_the_nation_desc: The Civil Rights Act is moving forward, as Kennedy wished, and it looks like it will pass soon. While the nation is still divided, this will heal, and we must provide a stabilizing, uniting voice as this passes so the people may know that the future will be brighter, now that we have lit the torch anew.
strings.USA_toe_the_middle_line_desc: The best policy is obviously one of sitting around pretending there isn't one, all of this will blow over soon.
strings.USA_ease_civil_rights_leaders_fears_desc: We won't hurt you, so you don't have to worry! Live and let live, jive brother!
strings.USA_rally_segregationists_support_desc: We know those folks are causin' some issues in your lil' homesteads, but don't worry, the government does indeed understand.
strings.USA_nationwide_riots_desc: For some reason our expert persuasion seems to not be working, so now we'll have to figure out the best way to deal with this little crisis. Well... it'll all blow over if everyone just takes a breath.
strings.USA_reinforce_the_police_desc: Reinforcing the police will be necessary if we're to keep order on the streets. As long as the boys in blue have the tools to do what they need to do, we can rest easy knowing that the chaos will be over soon.
strings.USA_keep_it_calm_desc: Keep it calm folks! Change might come if we only all sit down and relax!
strings.USA_keep_it_orderly_desc: Keep it calm, keep it orderly! If everyone would just follow the laws and regulations of our great Republic then we wouldn't have to worry!
strings.USA_they_have_a_dream_desc:
There's no one more tolerant than us in Washington. Let's start by saying that. We've had many great, great conversations with all sorts of black fellows from around the nation. We've won a majority of black voters in every election we've run. Sure, Kennedy got points with the press after calling Mr. King in his jail cell in '60 and, sure, Mr. King has called us a “moral coward” for not doing the same, but we don't let that bother us. No. We respect people's right to run their goddamn mouths off whenever they want.

But never mind that. It seems that the King fellow has come to Washington for a march of some kind or another and delivered a speech that has the nation all up in arms. Senators keep calling us to ask us to finally make a decision on the civil rights business. We could do that and ruin our coalition or, perhaps, we could find some way to stall for time.
strings.USA_the_party_splits_desc:
These goddamn bastards. These goddamn ungrateful bastards are ruining everything. Every day, they call us up. They call us up in our goddamn office trying to push us this way or that on the Blacks. Just the other day, Bob Jones was threatening to leave the Republicans for Wallace and his gang because we're not doing enough to promote “law and order.” Then-can you believe it-the goddamn governor of Michigan didn't want us to visit the state because he's got a hard election coming up and is afraid of alienating the liberals.

It's absurd. We all know this whole awful hysteria about the civil rights thing has been a media-created goddamn thing from the beginning, but we can't take any more of it. We could lose our entire majority unless we convince these whiny bastards to shut the hell up and calm down.
strings.USA_the_kennedy_plan_desc:
What the hell is the matter with Kennedy? It isn't a question, we mean, it's the lack of discretion. The goddamn brat won't stop talking about the Blacks and it's riling people up. He's having all these meetings with these Jew reporters and these activist troublemakers. He's coming to us trying to, you know, rope us into the whole business.

Well, we're not falling for it. We won't sully our reputation. If we can't get him to stop talking, we'll use him as an example of what happens when you ignore Coalition unity. Tomorrow, we'll announce we're putting Kennedy in charge of the whole civil rights mess. Let's see how the press reacts when their progressive golden boy alienates the Republicans and those stupid Democrats can't pass a goddamn bill through Congress. Let's watch Kennedy hang himself with his own goddamn rope.
strings.USA_the_1962_civil_rights_act_desc:
The bastard did it. The goddamn son of a bitch somehow got a bill through Congress. Who knows what the hell he did to get Strom Thurmond to stand down, but the thing is going to a floor vote and it's expected to pass. All the papers are celebrating the brat as some kind of national hero while our entire electoral strategy is going up in flames. Half the Democrats are threatening to split while the bastards in New England are trying to draft Kennedy for '64.

The whole thing is wrong, the whole thing is wrong. We are going on the wrong path, all because the smug, stupid son of a bitch wanted his face in the papers. What a total, pluperfect ass.
strings.USA_remain_neutral_desc: Let them figure it out! Maybe things will change without our intervention, and without us potentially destroying our Coalition. Change may come, America just isn't ready for it.
strings.USA_tape_togerther_the_seams_desc: Our refusal to bring change may have brought... issues. As the Senate increasingly resembles a battlefield between progressive and conservative, we must do everything we can to keep the Coalition from collapsing in the wake of this.
strings.USA_crack_down_on_the_movement_desc:
This country is filled with all kinds of communists and subversives. We found that out in the '48 when the bastards won Kansas and Oklahoma. Now, they're making fools of themselves in the so-called NPP. They're all over the civil rights movement, defaming the country and causing all sorts of havoc.

You know, maybe the Germans have the right approach here. If they go through a town and one of their soldiers gets hit by a sniper, they line up the whole goddamned town and say, 'until you talk, you're all getting shot.' Obviously, we're not going to go that far. We're tolerant people, but something's got to be done about this window smashing and atmosphere of hatred. We've got to clean out the whole damn movement, really root out the troublemakers. It's the only way to stop the mobs and bring law and order back to America. Only then can we find compromise on civil rights.
strings.USA_veto_the_civil_rights_act_desc:
We've had it! No more press conferences. No more exclusive interviews. No more goddamn “Draft Kennedy” nonsense. We're vetoing this bill and we don't give a shit what happens next. Let the progressives whine and moan. Let the entire goddamn Democratic Party throw a fit. We don't care. At least the country will get this nastiness out of its system. Then maybe it will settle down for five goddamn minutes.

Look, we're not animals. Once we dump the poor, humiliated bastard from the ticket in '64, we'll propose our own civil rights bill. We'll find some compromise to tie the Coalition back together, some token reform that gets King and the Dixiecrats on the same side. That'll be a real goddamn achievement, not the half-measure Kennedy cooked up.
strings.USA_bend_to_the_segregationists_desc: Segregation is as American as Apple Pie at this point, and to fight it is futile. It'd be best if the government bows before this, lest we make too many waves.
