The Japanese-Americans may be upset at the government endorsing such portrayals, but can they really be trusted in the first place? A gentle reminder of the internment camps should calm their loudest voices.
strings.USA_Aggressive_Recruitment_Methods_desc: Our decision to not go all in on the draft right away has caused a shortage of volunteer personnel, despite the efficacy of our recruitment campaigns. Well, if the mountain won't come to Mohammed... Let's send our recruiters into high schools and colleges, snag'em early. We can also make it easier to attain citizenship through military service to attract the immigrants, and offer non-felon criminals the chance at a commuted sentence in return for service. Let Uncle Sam squeeze this lemon for juice, even if it is sour.
strings.USA_Cogs_In_The_Machine_desc: The government has extensive powers over private industries in the case of national emergencies. With a bit of creative interpretation of these laws, we can encourage the heavy industries to optimize their production lines for our potential wartime needs. Like a scout, an American should always be prepared.
strings.USA_Ready_For_War_desc: After months of intensive campaigning and pulling the strings of industry, we are as ready for war as any nation has been since World War I. Many of the higher echelons of the party are worried that without mass mobilization of industry and draftees, we will lack the strength to fight a sustained war should the Pacific and Asian conflicts to come devolve into a full on global or continental war, but for more limited conflicts we are as ready as can be, with the party, the economy and the people united behind us. We just need to set the ball rolling, and with some luck the Japanese will be running back to their Home Islands before it loses its momentum.
strings.USA_On_To_Tokyo_desc: The Japanese may be imperialist, brutal devils who have gripped Hawaii and our West Coast ports in their claws for some twenty odd years, but we will still give them a chance at negotiating before we wipe the floor with them. Their intercontinental ballistic missiles are in range of most American states, and many at the Pentagon and White House are worried that should the conflict escalate into nuclear exchange, it could prove... costly. Even if the Japanese missiles are inferior copies of America's (and to a lesser extent, Germany's) quality designs, some of them might actually hit close to their targets, and with atomic weapons accuracy is not the biggest concern. A peaceful withdrawal of the Japanese garrisons would soothe our righteous wrath, for a little while, anyway.
strings.USA_Brothers_In_Arms_desc: The United States, like any true son of liberty, does not stand alone in bringing freedom and prosperity to the world. Besides the many exile governments operating in DC and Ottawa, we have allies in both the Atlantic and Pacific, not to mention our friends in Canada and our loyal minio- er, strategic partners in the Americas. However, our many friends and allies struggle greatly with equipment and manpower needs, as they were heavily reliant on designs, technology and productive capacity from a now fallen European continent. If they are to work in concert with the mighty US armed forces as anything more than cannon fodder, we must help them stay at our level in terms of equipment and training.
strings.USA_Down_Under_desc: Some of our most important allies come from a land Down Under, where the women glow and the men plunder. The Australians produce more than just kangaroos and big knives, they also make for fierce soldiers, as shown in both world wars. Let us review our plans for helping them.
strings.USA_The_Docks_Of_Darwin_desc: A first step in escalating our military aid programs for the Australasian region would be to help fortify and expand the port of Darwin, and important base for the US Navy and our primary unloading point for equipment and vehicles going to the Australians. We cannot leave it vulnerable to the Japanese.
strings.USA_The_Factories_Of_Sydney_desc: Australia is our ace in the hole when it comes to Southeast Asia. But in order for our allies to be of the most help to us when facing our foes, we need to boost their economy with an expanded industrial base. This will make it easier to produce supplies closer to the frontlines with the Co-Prosperity Sphere so we don't have to make them here, truck them to the West Coast, then ship them across the Pacific. As an added bonus it will also help their nation grow as well.
strings.USA_Our_Third_Eye_desc: Though we are already sharing most human intelligence on Japan we have with the Australians, previous administrations have held back on sharing certain signals intelligence info with them, for fear the Japanese would catch on that we had cracked their ciphers. However, we believe that the invaluable aid this would provide the Australians in keeping their country self from the Menace of the Rising Sun is worth the risk of the Japanese finding out. After all, even if they change their cipher, we are obviously just going to crack it again. That plastic junk they call computers in Japan could probably be decrypted by an American computer as small as your typical desk!
strings.USA_Fort_Australia_desc: Australia's vast coastlines and thinly spread population makes it hard to defend from a surprise Japanese invasion. We need to send fortification experts to help the Australians protect their island from such a scenario. A fort can lock down an entire county from attack and needs relatively little manpower to man.
strings.USA_The_OFN_desc: The RDC may be hesitant about sharing the industrial bounty of America with its allies, but we know better. A stronger alliance means a stronger America, and so we must promptly strike up deals with our allies where we give them foreign aid in exchange for them using it to buy American arms and equipment.
strings.USA_Together_Forever_desc: The 25th anniversary of the OFN is coming up soon. We should make this a grand occasion with a joint military parade in DC, celebrations in each member country and televised speeches from each head of state. It is important, in these dark times, that people around the world are reminded that the Torch of Liberty still burns bright in the New World and that the bonds of men cannot be broken by the bootheels of tyrants! We have fought them for a quarter century and we'll fight them for a century more if we have to.
strings.USA_Canada_desc: Our friends to the north are our most important allies after the fall of Europe. Bound by a common language, culture, and origin, we stand proudly together in defense of the ideals once born from the Magna Carta in ages gone by. Sadly their economy has struggled without the old Commonwealth trade. As their most important trade partner, we should help them out with cross-border investments and discounted trade deals, that should get the old lion roaring again.
strings.USA_Guyana_desc: A young lady from Guyana was recently brought to the White House by her brother, a staffer at the Guyanese embassy. Tearfully, she explained that the difficult economic conditions in her home country had driven her town to the verge of starvation, and how countless settlements like hers are almost cut off from the coastal cities due to bandits and wild animals stalking the roads. This could make for good optics, given our past... issues with Guyana. Let us issue an official statement about how touched we were by the story and promise a nice fat foreign aid package for the Guyanese government, to be invested into integrating the countryside into the modern industrial economy. That should win us some hearts and minds.
strings.USA_New_Zealand_desc: New Zealand is small and isolated, and following the loss of her mother country, isolated besides from Australia and the US. Let us remind them that we will never forget their sacrifices during the last war and their importance in the conflicts to come. A tax credit will be implemented for industries willing to invest in New Zealander companies, to encourage trade and homegrown production alike.
strings.USA_Semper_Liber_desc: In a better world, America might have found itself flush with allies, a true champion of democracy and freedom that would stand unrivalled in the world, its manifest destiny apparent to all. We're sadly far from that world, but we can still feel pride in the alliance we have created. In twenty years we have turned a loose coalition of traumatized survivors of the world war, mostly former colonies cut off from their homeland, and turned it into a true alliance of freedom fighters, mobilized and ready to fight tyranny wherever it may encroach upon our shores. Let us take a step back and review our proud past before thinking about where we will take the OFN in the future.
strings.USA_United_And_Ready_desc: The Organization of Free Nations stands poised, ready like a tiger about to leap. The time to tear apart the Co-Prosperity Sphere is nigh. No longer will we suffer the iniquities of tyranny, the monstrous exploitation of despots who think they are living gods. Let a call go out to all the noble sons of the free nations of the world! Rise for Freedom! Stand for Democracy! Fight for Independence! Give us Liberty, or give us death!
strings.USA_The_Eagle_Strikes_Back_desc: While analysts believe agitating China is the best bet to crush the Japanese Empire, for the moment Tokyo maintains too much of a watchful eye on events there for us to do much, while the collaboration government remains uncollaborative towards our silent approaches for support. So, for the moment, we should endeavor to destabilize the Sphere to distract the Japanese, weaken their economy and tie them up in foreign conflicts. The CIA recommends targeting the “soft underbelly of the Sphere,” the Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia. All of these nations have strong resistance movements and difficult terrain that makes them perfect for prolonged guerrilla warfare to tie down and weaken the Japanese. Let us make contact with them.
strings.USA_Set_Up_The_Networks_desc: Our initial contact with the resistance movements have been promising, but we will need an extensive network of spies and informants to keep tabs on the true strength and positioning of both our enemies and our allies. Thorough intelligence will be crucial to identifying the pressure points where our aid can do the maximum amount of damage at the minimum of risk of our involvement being exposed or sabotaged.
strings.USA_Preemptive_Sabotage_dsec: The Japanese are onto many of our resistance friends. To limit their movement in the region and hinder them redeploying their forces to effectively counter the coming operations, commando teams must be sent in to quickly sabotage infrastructure where the Resistance don't have the manpower or equipment to do it themselves. The Japanese should be severely slow to respond to any crisis, not to mention short on supplies. This will buy us some breathing space and allow the endangered resistance friends to reposition themselves.
strings.USA_Meet_The_Resistance_desc: The Filipino Resistance initially refused our cooperation, unlike the movements in other countries. For some movements it was a simple matter of not being informed of our attempts to contact them, either through isolation from other groups or because they do not trust foreigners. However, for many others we appeared as cowards who abandoned them to Japan at best, and as little better than the Japanese at worst. Many of the older fighters fought against our own troops once upon a time, and though only the most ancient of the members remember the Spanish, many of the Filipinos saw our actions during and after that war as naked imperialist aggression. Luckily, our effectiveness in sabotaging the Japanese and the enthusiasm of the other resistance movements in the regions have convinced the larger Filipino resistance groups to finally meet with us and discuss how we can help them in liberating their country. We better prepare.
strings.USA_Train_The_Militias_desc: Before the Germans invaded them, the British were highly successful at training select European resistance fighters into fierce commandos, who could then be parachuted back into their homelands to direct the most dangerous sabotage missions and help train the regular partisans back home into a true threat to the Germans. Some of these British-trained networks, like Milorg in Norway and the Home Army in Poland, still fight on today, twenty years later. Let us emulate this success by bringing key Asian resistance figures stateside for intensive training, so they can return to their home countries with knowledge of the most modern drill, combat and sabotage training procedures available in the greatest country in the world. Before long their ragtag militias will be hardened partisans who won't stop killing Japanese until the last sakura is burned to ash!
strings.USA_Hit_Em_Where_It_Hurts_desc: This month is our first big operation with the resistance movements in Asia. Near-simultaneous sabotage actions will rock the entirety of southeast Asia, targeting arms factories, civilian Zaibatsu factories, auto yards and construction offices. The Japanese ability to supply their troops locally and build new factories will be crippled!
strings.USA_We_Said_We_Would_Return_desc: America's back, baby, back with a bang! We have knocked the feet out under the Japanese in Southeast Asia. For the moment they are scrambling their garrisons to protect critical areas like Java and south Vietnam, this leaves us a nice opening in the Philippines to further impress our new Resistance friends. Operation MacArthur will see another wave of sabotage actions, this time concentrated in the Philippine archipelago. The Zaibatsu have as expected pulled their strings in Tokyo to have the Japanese garrisons protect their factories, meaning the factories of the collaborationist regime are now more exposed than a naked Japanese man at the NPP national convention! Time to teach them the price of treason.
strings.USA_Contact_The_Holdouts_dsec: An unexpected development in the Philippines, as the CIA have received information from several Resistance groups that elements of the old government still survive in the jungles of Mindanao. While key government officials like the President were evacuated to Australia during the collapse of our army there at the start of the war, many more junior ministers and civil servants of the Commonwealth remained trapped in Luzon. Many of them were released or outright ignored by the Japanese during the war, but in the wake of the Akagi Accords, many of them disappeared, which we thought was due to a purge by the Laurel administration. However, now it seems that dozens of them were warned of the incoming purge and were evacuated by the Luzon-based Hunters ROTC guerrilla group to rural Mindanao. On the basis of the former cadets of the Hunters and surviving Army remnants, they formed the Provisional Government of the Army of Mindanao (PGAM). If we can reconnect them with the old exile government in DC, we have a real shot at restoring a legitimate alternative to the collaborationist regime! Their territory is tiny and their fighters fewer than four digits, but combining their small sliver of freedom with the legitimacy of the old regime will prove a powerful symbol. The rest of the Resistance may be less happy at us trying to revive the old regime, though.
strings.USA_Breaking_the_Weak_Link_desc: Somewhat unexpectedly, the resistance movements in Indonesia have proven much stronger than anticipated, with resistance groups we didn't even know of striking Japanese targets all over the islands. They might even have a realistic chance at toppling the government and free the country. Until now our contact has primarily been with the larger groups on Java and Borneo, but perhaps we can make contacts with these smaller groups on the other islands too. If we can help forge a unified front against the Japanese, we could launch a devastating blow against the Sphere.
strings.USA_Free_Indonesia_Forever_desc: Our resistance contacts inform us that a wide coalition has been forged between all the primary resistance groups, and a full revolution is imminent. The time for clandestine smuggling of arms is over, let us load an Australian freighter full to the brim with rifles, ammunition, mortars, trucks and first aid kids and run it ashore near their headquarters. The die has been cast, gentlemen!
strings.USA_Set_Up_The_Supply_Lines_desc: Despite our best efforts to supply them, the Southeast Asian resistance movements still rely primarily on gear looted from the Japanese, whether armories or bodies. However, using the remote villages of the PGAM as a nighttime drop site for crates full of weapons and plastic explosives, we can ensure the gear is easily smuggled in backpacks, cars and fishing boats to all of the Philippines and Eastern Indonesia in significant quantities. We can also contact our friends in Vietnam to see if a similar solution can be found at the other end of the region. Soon, our friends can sabotage and attack as often as they want!
strings.USA_Free_Seas_Exercises_desc: The incompetence of Thomas Dewey's administration saw us frequently outmaneuvered and surprised by the Japanese during the Pacific Theater of the war. We need to stage naval exercises to ensure we can plan and prepare for the next conflict in this region. The Japanese fleet will be little more than scrap should it come to blows between our navies.
strings.USA_The_Land_Of_Spice_And_Honey: The Land of Spice and Honey
strings.USA_The_Land_Of_Spice_And_Honey_desc: Vietnam is unique among the countries in the Japanese Sphere in that practically all resistance to the collaborationist imperial government is united in one front, that of the Viet Minh, a socialist group with nationalist overtones. Our early overtures towards them were met with great interest, as they see the NPP as fellow travelers in the journey towards a more equal and free society. It is time to contact them again and express our desire for a broadened and active relationship.
strings.USA_Hearts_And_Minds_Operations_desc: If we want to make Vietnam a byword for American success, we will need to ensure that the rural populace embrace the Viet Minh leadership as a legitimate government alternative to the Empire. Giving the Viet Minh intelligence about the government's troop movements and soft targets, they can show their incompetence at maintaining a unified and secure state for their citizens. We'll also ensure the Viet Minh always have sacks of rice and luxury products like chocolate to hand out to the rural villagers who need their aid.
strings.USA_Send_In_The_Cubans_desc: Our Cuban allies have asked for our blessing and help to dispatch a volunteer brigade to Vietnam to help their socialist comrades in the struggle against the Japanese puppets. Who are we to deny such a request? Let us make the arrangements, and also provide them with plentiful sabotage gear so they can help undermine our enemies' industry.
strings.USA_Dinner_Menu_Bombers_desc: During the war, our slow naval fighters were often outmaneuvered by the Japanese Zero fighters, and our bombers struggled to hit targets effectively despite secure bases in Australia and New Guinea, due to the air dominance the Japanese had locally thanks to their many airfields and hangar ships. We must revise and update our aerial doctrine, so that this time around we can dominate in the air like we should. Air exercises for the OFN should immediately be arranged in Australia.
strings.USA_The_Sun_Begins_To_Set_desc: It has begun. We have set Asia aflame, and the Japanese, impoverished by their kleptocratic economy and sluggishly reacting under their corrupt and bloated imperial administration, are struggling to bring their enslaved “allies” back into the fold. Slowly, but surely, the simmering tensions and resentments in the Sphere are coming to a boil, and formerly cowed groups in China, Thailand, Korea and the Pacific are smelling blood in the water. The match we threw helped ignite the explosion of violence against injustice in Indonesia, and now we can sense something big on the horizon, the true end of the hegemony of the setting Sun. It may take us years or even decades to get there, but America will not rest until the Japanese clutch is broken and Asia is free for the first time since the colonial era began. The bells of liberty will ring out from Singapore to Peking! For America! For Freedom!
strings.USA_scp_industry_popularity_boosts: Our popularity will increase in heavily industrialized states.
strings.USA_scp_banish_fr: We shall weaken the influence of the £GFX_npp_fr_texticon Nationalist wing of the Party. This will come at the cost of overall NPP support.
strings.USA_scp_banish_extremes: We shall work to eliminate the extremist wings of the party.
strings.USA_scp_military_support: We will gain increased support from those states tightly bound to the military.
strings.USA_scp_military_anger: We will lose support from those states tightly bound to the military.
strings.USA_scp_introduce_army_modernization: We will begin gathering the votes for our Army Modernization. It ont only aims to provide our soldiers with the finest training in the world but also includes substantial funding for education in general. A educated mind is the grwatest tool in our arsenal.
strings.USA_scp_hold_vote: Voting on the program shall commence.
strings.USA_scp_the_jackson_presidency_desc:
Henry M. “Scoop” Jackson, a native Washingtonian who was denied service to his country during the 40's by the dreadful Democrats, has managed to claw his way to the West Wing of the White House, representing the shining ambitions of the Central branch of the National Progressive Pact in his desire to reforge America into a new, progressive, and powerful state in the entrance of the new decade.

To describe President Jackson's ambitions and desires for the new administration would take quite a while to detail the intricacies of the politicians mind, and so, he's taken the liberty to summarize it briefly for all to hear: “bombs and welfare.” Yes, it may take time and money to get there, but America will soon be rid of the extremists who pull and tear at the seams of the constitution, and be able to walk forward with the power of the military at her fingertips, and a well-off American populace standing there to support her in all she does. Here's to the next four years, everybody!
strings.USA_scp_welfare_for_the_people_desc:
Welfare has always been a tricky spot in terms of legislation for the United States, as some of the harshest critics on the right would proclaim that such actions would spur an economic meltdown while making our citizens lazy. However, one thing is for sure of all people: they wanna feel happy and cared for by their government, and, by God, we'll make it happen!

Across the country, the poor and hungry continue to scrounge for what they can, scrambling at the bit to make ends meet and eating the scraps that have been left for them. This cannot do, this will not do, for we are America, We the People, for the People! Sure, the economy has always been a delicate balancing act since the end of the Second World War, but we have grown plenty since those days, and it is our intention to prioritize for the lower classes of our country over the banks and the stock markets!
strings.USA_scp_a_right_not_a_privilege_desc: Oftentimes, American conservatives will speak about social welfare programs as if they're something to be earned. Our administration vehemently disagrees with this notion. The American people deserve a safety net that all can benefit from, and our administration will work to sell that idea, through speeches, ad campaigns, and grassroots organizing. In our America, everyone should be able to reach their potential, free from fear of deprivation or precarity.
strings.USA_scp_contacts_in_the_unions_desc: America's progressive unions have always been an integral part of our political coalition. Their members vote for us, their executives donate to us, and their endorsements have helped our candidates in hundreds of races across the country. We'll need their support again if our agenda is to succeed. Let's have our liaisons reach out to the leadership of unions like the UAW, to advance our administration's priorities and keep our union support strong.
strings.USA_scp_strike_the_fr_desc: The NPP has relied upon its Nationalist branch since the beginning, and in terms of national defense and foreign policy, our faction overlaps with theirs significantly. However, the faction isn't always reliable. At times, they're outright opposed to our policy initiatives. But our administration's influence on Capitol Hill could help to change this. Our congressional liaisons will lean on leadership, getting them to move troublesome Nationalist congresspeople off of important committees, snubbing them at caucus meetings, and using a dozen other tactics to cut the Nationalist influence from the halls of power.
strings.USA_scp_the_two_snakes_desc: While much of the NPP is made up of its Nationalist and Progressive factions, there are those at both ends of the party who go far beyond the mainstream. There are the Nazi-sympathizing Sovereigns, and the outright socialists and communists of the Marxist Caucus. We need to shut them out of the party and make it clear that this sort of destructive extremism has no place in American government. God help us if they ever get near the reins of power.
strings.USA_scp_meet_the_chiefs_desc: President Jackson was elected, in no small part, because of his pledge to support the US military through thick and thin. After all, in the Senate, he was a strident hawk whose military budget requests were legendarily vast. The Joint Chiefs of Staff are surely the experts on what the branches of the military need to thrive in this new decade. Our administration will meet with them and work to improve the United States military through any and all means.
strings.USA_scp_why_we_fight_desc: After all the blood and treasure lost in the wars of the 1960s, America-and the world-needs to know why we have a military. The United States armed forces represent the best of us, standing for freedom and justice in a world so often left wanting for it. We'll have the Pentagon start providing assistance to all sorts of movie and television studios, while simultaneously expanding our direct public relations strategy. America's military might will be known throughout the world in a new way in the 1970s, and if war comes to America, our people will know why we fight.
strings.USA_scp_turn_on_the_hose_desc: We live in an age of technological marvels and strategic opportunity. Everything from satellites to computers to laser-guided munitions will allow our military to achieve incredible things in the field of battle. But to have a more modern, professional, and capable military, we'll need to invest. Officers and specialists will have to be trained. New weapons systems will have to be procured. And all of this will cost quite a bit of money. Fortunately, we were elected with a mandate to expand defense funding. The Pentagon will have all the money it could ask for to build the fighting force of the future.
strings.USA_scp_army_modernization_program_desc:
The United States Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps all stand as the building blocks for Lady Liberty's Sword and Shield against the German Eagle to the East and the Rising Sun's grasp across the Pacific. For years, they've recovered proudly and strongly from the sinking defeat of the Second World War, and has helped promise us a future of freedom, liberty, and justice for all; however, it is undeniable that the sword can be sharpened, and the shield can be bolstered. Thus, it's time to introduce a bill to Congress that will handle two of America's biggest issues: education and military quality. The Army Modernization Program.

With the program in effect, better education standards will be coupled with improved and intensified training methods for members of the United States Army, and may soon be expanded to include all branches of the military. With hope, we will be able to expand the boosts in education towards all of the American public, for the sake of a better tomorrow. After all, smarter people make better soldiers, right?
strings.USA_wal64_roll_back_segregationist_rheto: As much as we want to claim the pride and happiness in our administration's successes, one thing stands as clear as daylight: the people of America stand broken, divided, and at each other's throats. Whether we like it or not, the country would be damned if we continued to wedge a divide, as it will only serve to promote more outrage and disunity, even if taking action has been our greatest weapon in our successes. Thus, in our knowledge in the impossibility of America's success without even a crumb of stability, we must roll back some of our more outlandish statements regarding our policies of segregation. Although our support base will become more confused over the official they voted for, like hell would we allow the nation to break apart more than it already has and stop any process of healing. Besides, no matter what, we will continue to stand up for the states' rights against the federal government, even if we have to smother some of the flames.
strings.USA_wal64_workers_for_business_desc: The company owners and managers are great people, they really are, but the greatest corporation would still be nothing without the thousands of average folk toiling down on the ground. The modern American corporation must learn the lesson from the great Henry Ford, that a happy and well treated worker makes for a more efficient labourer, and for a fine potential consumer. With all the help they have received from the government, big business is now ready to accept some more protections to the worker. In the end, everybody is better off than they were before.
strings.USA_wal64_lower_business_tax_desc: What American business needs to grow and improve this nation is simple and clear - more capital. The first and most intuitive step to ensuring continued growth and more jobs will be freeing business from the unneeded financial burden put upon it by the government. Especially since we've all agreed the federal government needs some shrinking anyway.
strings.USA_wal64_time_to_save_america_desc:
In 1964, a tidal wave of Southern fury crashed down upon the nation and put George Wallace in the Oval Office. His electoral mandate was simple: Repeal Nixon's intolerable act at all costs. Now it's time for Wallace to make good on his promise to the American people, he is about to undo the terrible damage that Johnson, Kennedy, Nixon, King, and all these domestic “civil rights” terrorists have done to the American way of life.

President Wallace will start drafting the American National Traditions Reservation Act. This act will repeal the Civil Rights Act of [?USA.USA_CRA_year], as well as provide timetables and procedures for Southern States to begin re-segregating and, if we have chosen such a path, for Northern States to introduce segregation. We will also implement full segregation in federal institutions and push towards segregation in the armed forces. It will also give police departments a broad range of powers to enforce segregation. But first, we must secure enough support in the Senate to get this bill to Wallace's desk, and some campaigning and compromise may be necessary...
strings.USA_wal64_make_speeches_throughout_the_c:
“And you native sons and daughters of old New England's rock-ribbed patriotism, and you sturdy natives of the great Mid-West and you descendants of the far West flaming spirit of pioneer freedom; we invite you to come and be with us for you are of the Southern spirit and the Southern philosophy. You are Southerners too and brothers with us in our fight.”

And thus, President Wallace will embark on a massive coast-to-coast campaign to promote ANTRA. He will tell Boston housewives that his act will keep their children from being bussed to Black schools, tell Michigan auto workers that he'll keep Blacks from taking their unionized jobs, and tell well-to-do New York suburbanites that without ANTRA, it'll be “there goes the neighborhood” in no time. And then? He'll tell them to write their Congressmen and urge them to throw their votes behind the only act that can save America from chaos and destruction.'
strings.USA_wal64_all_this_does_is_suppress_the_: All This Does is Suppress the Unrest, Not Fix It!

“You think these so-called Freedom Riders are going to quit now that the CRA is passed? You think they won't be burning down your cities thrice over by the end of the decade? Give these uppity Nazi-infiltrated activists an inch and they're going to take a foot and your whole leg! The CRA may have mollified African-Americans for a hot minute but ANTRA will strike at the heart of their unrest by giving our boys in blue the means and the mandate to shut down their riots before they start! You mark my words, pass ANTRA and it'll save your life!”

Wallace will dial his law-and-order rhetoric up to 11. He will denounce the CRA as a broken law that weakens every sheriff in the country and promote ANTRA as America's last hope to save themselves and their property from an onslaught of “Civil Rights” rioters.
strings.USA_wal64_campaign_in_the_west_desc:
The West Coast is hardly the most obvious place for Wallace to seek support. Yet, his analysts see a window of opportunity in that bulwark of progressivism. If he hits the right notes, Wallace could convince even the enlightened liberals of Beverly Hills to see why ANTRA is necessary.

Wallace will make it clear that desegregation isn't just something that will happen in Alabama, it'll happen in California too. The Black Panthers are already using force of arms to terrorize the good people of Los Angeles, and it's only a matter of time till they're emboldened to torch Watts and the whole city with it. If you don't want to be defending your homes, families, and businesses when the police abandon you to the mob, you'll tell your Congressman to vote yes on ANTRA!
strings.USA_wal64_private_discussions_in_congres:
Wallace has a lot to say about the Civil Rights Act. He has a hell of a lot more to say about the segment of our country whose social standing it aims to improve. A good deal of what Wallace has to say about them, however, is better said behind closed doors than on the Senate floor.

President Wallace will meet in private with moderate Congressmen to talk them into seeing his side of the Civil Rights issue. Hopefully this will convince these Senators to quietly vote aye when the time comes.
strings.USA_wal64_convince_lobbyists_desc:
The First Amendment to the Constitution guarantees every American the right to petition their government for redress of grievances, and there is no greater grievance that has been inflicted upon the American people in recent years than the Civil Rights Act of [?USA.USA_CRA_year]. This bill is a fraud, a sham, and a hoax; it threatens our freedom of speech, of assembly, or association, and makes the exercise of these Freedoms a federal crime under certain conditions. It is no “Civil Rights Act”, it is a Federal Penal Code. If the average citizen has been unable to convince their congressmen to see that, then we may have to bring in the professionals.

President Wallace will flood Congress with the finest lobbyists money can buy. They will meet with everyone Wallace can't find time to meet and sell them on his righteous crusade against Federal fascist tyranny. This should bring them to the negotiating table and get them voting yes on ANTRA.
strings.USA_wal64_money_in_congress_desc:
A fascist monster has risen up in this nation. It has invaded the government. It has invaded the news media. It has invaded the leadership of many of our churches. It has invaded every phase and aspect of the life of freedom-loving people. With its ACLU fundraisers and its Japanese-Hitlerite backers, it has bought and paid for countless Congressmen who are holding up the passage of ANTRA.

It's time to fight fire with fire.

President Wallace will make it rain on Capitol Hill. Money will flow into Congress from our patriotic citizen-supporters. After all his lobbying efforts, this may well be the final push we need to secure enough votes to pass ANTRA and save American property rights and human rights once and for all.
strings.USA_wal64_hinder_black_voters_desc:
Those spineless cowards in the RDC have had one foot in freedom-loving American patriotism and the other in liberal-fascist tyranny ever since Thurmond led the Southern Exodus in '52. They may be trying to toe the middle line but they know in their hearts that as soon as their coalition does away with poll tests, black Americans will thank them for their pussyfooting by voting a straight RDC ticket! But President Wallace is a forgive-and-forget Christian; if the Democrats want to repent of their obstinance and support ANTRA, then he will make sure their seats are secure.

President Wallace will encourage governors to ruthlessly enforce the rigged literacy tests that keep Black Americans away from the polls. Conservative Congressmen will be informed that another so-called Freedom Summer will see them thrown out of the capitol, and this fact will hopefully inspire them to vote for ANTRA.
strings.USA_wal64_segregate_the_voting_booths_de:
Voting is an American right, and segregation is the American way, so segregated voting booths are as American as apple pie! If Blacks have no business using the same theater entrances or cemeteries as White people, they can hardly expect to use the same polling stations as their paler compatriots. And should their polling booths be inaccessible, that's hardly our problem.

President Wallace will step up his efforts against Black voters. The Black polling stations could be two hours away from their homes and located within a condemned building, but if they can't make it there to vote, that's their fault. This should further shore up conservative support for ANTRA by ensuring southern conservative senators have nothing more to fear from Black voters.
strings.USA_wal64_detain_possible_leaders_desc:
Martin Luther King Jr. has called Wallace, “the most dangerous racist in America.” That is a false and incendiary remark. He, personally, has done more for African-Americans than any other individual. Our efforts are keyed to a fight to preserve Constitutional Government and States' Sovereignty - not to hurt African-Americans. The races have lived together in the South for generations in peace and equanimity. They each prefer their own pattern of society, their own churches and their own schools - which history and experience have proven are best for both races. All these troubles we're having lately are precisely because of outside fascist-influenced agitators like the so-called Reverend King, the NAACP, the ACLU and all the Japanazi moneyed interests backing them. That ends here and now!

President Wallace will launch Operation Defending Freedom, an FBI offensive that will arrest and detain major subversive leaders in surgical strikes from Coast to Coast. MLK, James Farmer, Roy Wilkins, Abraham Heschel, Gus Hall, Bobby Seale, anyone on Wallace's blacklist. Obviously, they can't be charged with anything that will stick, but detaining them for a while will hinder their ability to instigate Black voters in the elections. Conservative RDC members should certainly be grateful for our efforts to secure their seats and will be more poised to support ANTRA.
strings.USA_wal64_get_back_in_your_place_desc:
“Men like Martin Luther King Jr. and Ralph Abernathy styles themselves as so-called men of God guided by Christian principles. But I, George C. Wallace, am a servant of Christ as well. And I call upon these men to consider two important passages in our Scripture: Deuteronomy 32:8, and Acts 17:26.

'When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.' 'From one man he made all the nations, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and he marked out their appointed times in history and the boundaries of their lands.'

In 1964 the American people confirmed an immortal truth: That the separation of the races is a God-given mandate to mankind. It was not President Wallace who first put up signs saying, ”Whites Only“ and ”Coloreds Only“, it was our Father in Heaven. No one, not the God-hating fascists in Germany and Japan, the tyrants on the Supreme Court, the spineless atheists in Congress nor the liberal elites funding them can erase what God has decreed. The Civil Rights Act is ready to be melted down like a modern Golden Calf, and America will return to God and the way of life that He ordained.”
strings.USA_wal64_repeal_the_civil_rights_act_de:
In [?USA.USA_CRA_year] the President of the United States signed into law the most monstrous piece of legislation ever enacted by the United States Congress. It was a fraud, a sham, and a hoax. Never in the history of this nation had so many human and property rights been destroyed by a single enactment of the Congress. It was an act of tyranny. It was the assassin's knife stuck in the back of liberty.

And today, God willing, it will be shredded and thrown in the waste-bin of American history.

ANTRA will come to a final vote today. All of Wallace's preparations to secure the repeal of the CRA shall be tested. If it passes, Wallace will cement his legacy as the savior of the South. If it doesn't, his failure will never be forgotten in Dixie.

Repealing the Civil Rights Act will unleash a storm of racial unrest, and the Progressive bloc of the NPP will scream bloody murder. the Pact might not survive ANTRA, neither may Wallace's own presidency. None of that matters. This moment is what Wallace has fought for ever since Nixon signed the accursed act and, by God, he shall not be denied this victory.

Alea iacta est.
strings.USA_wal64_support_anti_civil_rights_prot: There are many Americans who reject the civil rights movement. Whether they agree with segregation or simply reject the hooliganism of its opponents, these true patriots continue to stand up while enduring appalling abuse from the so-called supporters of 'equality'. We must give aid to these forces, such as providing them with police protection and giving more support to state troopers to help put down the violent mobs opposing them.
strings.USA_wal64_the_wallace_presidency_desc: The American people have chosen George Wallace as their new President, after one of the most contentious elections in US history. He has a number of plans for America with regards to creating a haven for foreign and domestic business as well as reforming education and welfare policy. Of course, the big issue, the one Wallace was truly elected on, is the Civil Rights Act. Wallace's victory proves that the American people are not happy with having such tyrannical policy forced upon them by the central government. He has promised that under his government, states will have full liberty to decide their own futures, unmolested by the demands of either Washington or of violent mobs. His presidency is sure to be beset by renewed outbursts of unrest from those who support the Act, but he has vowed to press on with his plans regardless of what some idiots who have nothing better to do but protest all day might do.
strings.USA_wal64_beacon_of_democracy_freedom_an: The Beacon of Democracy, Freedom, and Business

America is the last great nation on Earth to preserve the ideals of freedom and democratic government. We owe our success in this regard to the mightiest economy mankind has ever assembled, forged and maintained by American banks and American industries. Free from the state's menacing grip, they had risen to great heights, earned greater profit year after year, until soon America surpassed, then utterly dwarfed, the Old World tyrants and their many inefficiencies. It cannot be said enough: Without its unflinching dedication to free markets and free enterprise, our nation will have been consigned to a footnote in the annals of history long ago.

As a new President enters the White House, so too must America chart a new course for its economy. For thinking men such as you and I, there exists only one option: Promote American business, at home and abroad, whatever the cost. Only then, as American dollars and American businessmen travel from Washington to all four corners of the world, unimpeded, unburdened, will our nation be capable of continuing the fight for the ideals we so deeply cherish in the decades to come.
strings.USA_wal64_foreign_business_desc:
Wiser men than I am have said that America's business is business. That no matter who you are, or where you came from, America always had its door open, ready to make a deal. Guns, cars, pig iron, bread, Playboys -- you name it, we have it, no questions asked. For the better part of two centuries that had been our state of affairs, selling the excess of our plenty to anyone and everyone who wanted it; because of that, we prospered and grew where others keeled over and fell. It died an ugly death when the Depression hit us all -- but most damning was that the Democrats buried it under tariff after tariff without a second thought...

So to the American people I promise this: The good old days are coming back, and we will soon reap the riches that follow. And to all the free nations of the world I promise this: Our doors are always open, our bounty always free to purchase. Come on in with cash on hand, and let's make a deal!
strings.USA_wal64_iberian_desc:
Among the Triumvirate, Iberia is easily the closest to the United States -- a chink in the otherwise firm grips Germany and Italy have on the markets of Europe. Easy access to American lines of credit have helped keep the country's economy solvent and internationally competitive. Additionally, recent tensions with its ostensible allies meant that Iberian businessmen were gradually shifting their eyes away from the inter-Mediterranean and towards the trans-Atlantic.

Our economic advisors believe that now is the perfect time to expand the reach of American trade into Iberia and, consequently, Southern Europe. A trade agreement here, some words of encouragement there, and soon enough our companies will be making Iberian pesos hand over fist.
strings.USA_wal64_canadian_desc:
While business transactions with strangers work fine enough, business transactions with friends have the added benefit of lasting far longer -- and there is no better example of a friend to America than our neighbor Canada. We have always enjoyed warm trade relations with the Great White North, much to the displeasure of the late British Empire. Canadian oil and precious metals freely cross the longest shared land border on Earth on a regular basis, and in return American cars, heavy equipment, and foodstuffs are unloaded daily on the busy docks of Quebec, Toronto, and Vancouver.

Ours is a relationship that spans a hundred years and hundreds of millions of dollars, ultimately contributing to the prosperity of everyone involved. Through increases in our exports to and imports from Canada, we can strengthen these ties enough to last for at least another generation.
strings.USA_wal64_australasian_desc:
With the fall of China, French Indochina, and the Southeast Asian colonies, America's once-domineering sway over the most populous region on Earth came to an end. From Beijing to Batavia, American investments -- trade agreements, loans, company shares, overseas branches -- were written off or dissolved against our will. Untold millions that lasted generations, testaments to our nation's economic and financial prowess, swept away by the Japanese in little more than four years.

But Uncle Sam is far from out. Broken and bruised, yes, but never out.

While Hong Kong kowtowed to Japanese Zaibatsu, Canberra closed an entire continent shut from them. While Japan's new puppets expelled our businesses and our businessmen, Sydney offered them safe harbor. While all of Asia turned to the yen, Australasia alone kept true to the dollar. Twelve million is a far cry from the one billion to whom we used to sell, but that number remained loyal customers when everyone else jumped ship. If we're to reestablish America's presence in the Asia-Pacific, fostering better trade relations with our ally down under is the best place to start.
strings.USA_wal64_deregulate_dc_desc:
Regulations, regulations, regulations. They come in many shapes and sizes, different names for different people. Liberals and pinkos call them “environmental protection” and “workers' rights”; Nazis call them “efficient redistribution of the Führer's money”. But rational men see past the smoke and mirrors and find mountains of red tape, ready to choke the lights out of anyone who dares to found their own business, become their own masters. Like loyal mutts they follow the Feds wherever they go, ruining the lives of many an honest entrepreneur at home... and many an honest entrepreneur from abroad.

See, right now America needs every last dollar it can get to survive the next decade. Dollars to build roads and bridges, dollars to pay our men and buy our guns, dollars to grow wheat in the Plains and feed the American people. Right outside our borders is a whole mountain of cash, ready to flow like manna straight into America's balance sheet, building all the roads, bridges, farms, and factories we want. All we need to do is to loosen up a little -- nothing too harmful, just some... minor readjustments... here and there -- and all that capital will be ours for the taking.

Simple stuff, right? Glad you agree.
strings.USA_wal64_a_necessary_evil_desc: Workers' unions, organizations protecting the average American worker from the overreaching acts and breaches of justice committed by American companies in times past. Many have come to support the mandates of such unions and their protections for the American worker, while large companies have come into conflict with such organizations time and time again. Although these companies are large forces in United States society, it is without question that the strength of the American blue-collar worker can come as a blazing force in American politics. Thus, it is the administration's duty, even if it may restrict the economy, to capitalize on the support of such unions in some form of legislation, as Southern workers will appreciate the concern given to them by the government, while liberal-minded members of the RDC will begin to appreciate our work. Some call unions a new revolution in social policy, some call them a restriction on the American market, but the administration likes to call them “votes.”
strings.USA_wal64_made_in_america_desc:
Now from my understanding, this plant covers eight million square feet of space -- roughly over three hundred acres of prime Alabaman soil. That means it took hundreds of thousands of tons of concrete to build, concrete made with cement from the busy ports of Oregon. Inside we have the latest, most cutting-edge heavy machinery straight out of Pennsylvania and Ohio for to make the mightiest metal steeds ever put to the winding asphalt pastures of our great state, each stamped with tiny imprints of the Stars and Stripes -- our very own seal of quality.

“Built with the finest steel from the gigantic ironworks of Indiana, this auto factory now houses over three thousand workers, foremen, and managers...”
strings.USA_wal64_by_americans_desc:
...from all across the South. That's over three thousand good, hardworking Southerners with new jobs that offer good pay. Three thousand men, young and old, doing their part to expand the largest economy in the world by leaps and bounds. Three thousand families delighted to hear that Pappy'll come home tonight with a spring in his step, ten years younger, and most importantly, dollars in his pockets for the first time in a long while.

“I've spoken to some of these fine folks on my way here. Nathan Sullivan, father of two from Selma, who used to work in his dad's auto shop when he was young. George Greene, an electrician who came all the way from Corpus Christi looking for a new start in the heart of Dixie. Tully Whittaker, once a plumber fixing pipes and leaks down in Shreveport to feed a beautiful wife and three little hellions with all the shrimp gumbo they can eat!”

“These three men, and three thousand more, will be working in this factory in the coming months and years, churning out hundreds of thousands of cars a week...”
strings.USA_wal64_for_those_who_pay_desc:
...which will then be packed in mighty freight trains and water barges headed for America's largest ports -- New Orleans, New York, New Jersey -- ready to be hauled across the pond and to the rest of the world. God willing, every street corner from Montgomery to Tokyo will soon be thrumming with the powerful engines of American Dodges, American Fords, American Chevrolets, and American Chryslers -- all made in American factories such as this, by American men such as you and them.

“Imagine a day where the citizens of Rome and Berlin and all the capitals of all the world's tyrants will be treated to the sight of a morning parade -- not one with drab grey tanks or dour-faced, goose-stepping soldiers, but with cars straight from the Free World; driven by Germans, by Italians, by Japanese, by Europeans and Asians and Africans; roaring freedom with every belch of exhaust smoke.”

“Now won't that be a sight to see?”
strings.USA_wal64_welcome_to_america_desc:
We've done it. The road was long, hard and winding, with dog-headed lefties and duplicitous friends hounding us from every God-forsaken corner -- but we've done it.

From every corner of the world businessmen of every race and nation, every faith and creed, fly in the best planes they can charter to Washington, D.C. Day after day they stream to the Oval Office -- dignitaries, industrialists, magnates, princes, oil barons -- in droves bigger than the last, with the best suits they can order and the shiniest smiles they can muster, suitcases full of proposals and entreaties and promises to Uncle Sam. And with a few words, a few jokes, and a few handshakes, billions of cold, hard dollars enter the treasury in a single meeting. In a matter of weeks, these dollars will travel all over the country, sprouting up farms, roads, and factories wherever they're needed -- spreading America's wealth to her people wherever they go.

The road was long, hard, and winding -- but through diligence and hard work, America is once again a bastion of freedom, democracy, and business.
strings.USA_wal64_american_business_desc: The Nationalists of the National Progressive Pact has begged the great George C. Wallace to reform the American economy one way or another into creating a truly free and capitalistic market through which the Patriots of America will thrive, instead of crying about their loss of welfare programs. However, while we shall continue to act as strongman and greatest voice of the Nationalists for America, what we have to do to get there is answer for ourselves a simple question: shall we act in the favor of the small time business owners of this country, working hard every day to make things right, or the true money makers sitting in the suits of the fancy corporations, bringing in millions from foreign investors across the world?
strings.USA_wal64_abroad_desc:
By the end of the war, America's sway over the world order had shrunk to a fraction of what it once was ten years prior. “Vae victis,” the Axis powers triumphantly gloated, as they carved the Old World among themselves at America's expense -- Germany and Italy in Europe and Africa, and the Japanese Empire in the Asia-Pacific. Her pride wounded, her economy damaged, her influence gone, and her people close to revolt, America could do nothing but watch from the sidelines as three eagles soared to great heights out of the ashes of the Second World War.

That was two decades ago. Much has changed since then. For the world's newest empires, things have taken a turn for the worse.

Where others see the end of days, we see only a golden opportunity for America to return to the world stage -- for what else are we but risk-takers at heart? Let the degenerate tyrants suffer their malaises, just like all the other empires before them. The American Eagle shall spread its wings regardless, and it shall not be denied its rightful perch at the top of the world!
strings.USA_wal64_a_pacific_trade_zone_desc:
The Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere is Tokyo's collection of puppets and conquered nations, kept in line through the brutality, cruelty, and unrelenting barbarity of the Japanese military. For 20 years, the Sphere has kept the riches of the Orient from flowing to American shores, locking off our merchants and traders from Asian silk, Filipino sugar, and East Indies rubber.

Yet, within this tragedy, there lies opportunity. For not all of Asia feels beneath Tokyo's iron heel. Across the Pacific's vast expanse, the Republic of India stands as a bulwark of democracy and freedom against the Sphere's advance. A market of hundreds of millions, untapped by American enterprise.

Secretary of State Fulbright and the State Department see India as America's best chance to aid the forces of liberty and democracy and tie us to our Pacific allies through the bonds of trade and commerce.
strings.USA_wal64_australasian_subsidies_desc:
With the fall of China, Indochina, and the Southeast Asian colonies, America's once-domineering sway over the most populous region on Earth came to an end. From Beijing to Batavia, American investments -- trade agreements, loans, company shares, overseas branches -- were written off or dissolved against our will. Untold millions that lasted generations, testaments to our nation's economic and financial prowess, swept away by a horde of devils in little more than four years.

But Uncle Sam is far from out. Broken and bruised, yes, but never out.

While Hong Kong kowtowed to Japanese Zaibatsu, Canberra shunned them away. While Japan's new puppets expelled our businesses and our businessmen, Sydney offered them safe harbor. While all of Asia turned to the yen, Australia and New Zealand alone kept true to the dollar. Twelve million is a far cry from the one billion to whom we used to sell, but those twelve million remained steadfast when others faltered. If we are to reestablish America's presence in the Asia-Pacific, fostering better trade relations with our ally down under is the best place to start.
strings.USA_wal64_bleed_the_pacific_dry_desc:
Australia and New Zealand are the lynchpins of the OFN's strategic position in the Asia-Pacific. Only a few hundred miles away from the busy routes of the Straits and the South China Sea, the former Dominions pose a credible threat to the continued functioning of the Co-Prosperity Sphere's economy. In their facilities -- their hangars and docks -- we base a significant number of our bombers and ships, the implements we use to project power in Japan's home turf, in turn deterring them from making untoward moves on us and ours.

Their proximity to Japan is, however, a double edged sword; in the event of war, our Pacific allies will inevitably bear the brunt of (and damage caused by) Sphere incursions. Australia's generals are aware of this fatal shortcoming, and had proposed in past summits to develop their country into a 'fortress island': A well-armed, well-fortified bastion fashioned for the sole purpose of bleeding Japan dry -- of men, guns, food, oil, and everything in between. A lack of funding had kept this proposal from becoming anything more than white paper -- but with the recent subsidization program, Australia now has greater latitude in implementing the recommendations therein.

By expanding the current subsidies and extending them to New Zealand, we will expedite their development into capable members of the OFN while at the same time affirming our commitment to strengthening the Free World...
strings.USA_wal64_central_america_desc:
Once upon a time, a narrow strip of land between the Darien Gap and the Isthmus of Tehuantepec fed American homes and American factories with half of the world's cocoa, coffee, and above all, bananas. In exchange for peace, stability, and protection from European colonialism, the nations of this land agreed to pay tribute in the form of that one cash crop cultivated from their fertile plantations. This arrangement, enforced by American companies, saw everyone involved become rich beyond their wildest dreams as they together fed America and the world with millions of tons of delicious, nutritious bananas. Sadly, this fruitful relationship never fully recovered from the Great Depression, and the Second World War put to rest any hopes that it may be revisited in the near future.

One near future later, and things are starting to look up. We now have the means to reassert our position in Central America for the first time in thirty years. Our leverage may have atrophied, but we still have contacts to visit, old favors to call. Tell the State Department to spread the word far and wide: America's coming back for its bananas, and this time we're here to stay.
strings.USA_wal64_the_banana_republics_desc:
One of the most basic principles any businessman worth his salt follows is to “buy low and sell high”. The more dollars you earn with every dollar you spend, the better. Raw materials have the benefit of being easy enough to extract with unskilled labor, while at the same time in high enough demand to command hundreds of dollars per unit in the world market. This is why some countries base their entire economies on one such resource and become tremendously wealthy in doing so -- be it with oil, gold, diamonds, or in Central America's case, bananas.

By signing trade agreements with the region's “banana republics”, our businessmen can gain access to the fruit at bargain prices and sell them to a market willing to pay much, much higher for them. They get steep profits, Americans get delicious bananas, the local caudillos get revenue with which to buy more farmland and plant more bananas, and the federal government gets hefty sums of cash from the taxes pegged to every transaction throughout the whole chain -- a win-win scenario for everyone involved, in other words.
strings.USA_wal64_subsidies_for_fruit_desc:
Several weeks ago, representatives from Cuyamel, Dole, and United Fruit have approached our ambassadors about the renewed interest we have shown in “fostering better trade relations with Central American nations.” In numerous boardroom meetings they “professed their willingness to conduct fair business with its relevant governments once again” while flashing chart after chart of market trends, quarterly reports, revenue projections, risk analyses and other such “indicators of economic performance.”

“To conclude,” they droned, almost in unison, “our executives are shared in their belief that direct investment into their facilities and infrastructure may be needed to fully utilize the region's potential with respect to select harvest crops. Such measures will have the twofold effects of multiplying production by orders of magnitude within the next ten years and granting Americans to a much larger share thereof.”

Beneath the polite, technical language, however, the message was clear: America's largest fruit companies have heard about our plans for Central America, and they want in -- preferably with federal aid money to buy off the farmland for themselves. Lucky for them, corporate cooperation is exactly what we need.
strings.USA_wal64_nip_into_nicaragua_desc:
The tiny nation of Nicaragua may not be known for bananas, but it is relevant for something equally important: Coffee.

In large plantations all over the Isabella Mountains, farmers harvest coffee beans by the ton, day, and night, before ramshackle pickup trucks carry the lucrative produce through winding dirt roads which all converge in the busy port of Bluefields. From there they are loaded in crates to massive, freshly-painted cargo ships, which then deliver the beans to coffee shops and stores the world over.

In the decades since its introduction, coffee has arguably grown to occupy a special place in the American lifestyle. Much like the Englishman and his tea, many Americans drink coffee as part of a daily ritual, one which they can arguably no longer live without. It can hardly be denied that normal business would grind to a halt in the absence of coffee; thus, it's important that we gain as much control over its sources as we can.

If that means nabbing half a country's economy from under its nose, then so be it.
strings.USA_wal64_get_into_guatemala_desc:
The Land of Eternal Spring was once the United Fruit Company's gleaming jewel. As its single largest landowner, United Fruit reaped the majority of the nation's revenue and acted as its overlord in all but name. No Guatemalan farmer planted bananas without the company's knowledge, and no Guatemalan politician ran for office without the company's approval. In such a state of affairs did Guatemala's true suzerain reach unprecedented heights, making record profits off the production and export of Guatemala's most valuable crop, harvested by the Guatemalan people.

Then they decided enough was enough and staged an insurgency. A few severed heads express mailed to the company's headquarters later, and United Fruit left the country in disgrace.

Now that we've decided to allocate more resources towards expanding our influence in Central America, United Fruit claimed they can participate a little more directly in bringing Guatemala back to the fold. All they asked in return is 'broad latitude in the management of our restored assets within the country.' You don't have to be smart to know what they really want from us.
strings.USA_wal64_americas_fruit_baskets_desc:
“After months of negotiations, high-risk investment programs and concentrated effort in general, I am proud to say that we have successfully restored our operations in Guatemala and the rest of Central America. Our plantations are slowly returning to normal levels of production, and our new fleet has been busy transporting crops from ports all along the western coast to New Orleans. Conservative projections from our financial analysts estimate that banana imports to the United States will reach two million metric tons in four quarters, followed by a tenfold increase of the Company's annual earnings.”

“Business has never been better, and we here at United Fruit have you to thank for our success. Mark my words, Mr. President: No man, woman or child in America, rich or poor, will find themselves wanting of a basket of bananas ever again!”

-- Herbert Cornuelle, President of the United Fruit Company
strings.USA_wal64_investments_in_brazil_desc:
Coffee, soybeans, beef, rubber -- you name it, Brazil has it. Blessed by millions of square miles of both temperate plainland and tropical jungle, our large trading partner to the south has immense reserves of natural resources both exploited and pristine. If handled properly, Brazil can grow to a point where it can easily feed its own people and industries while still having millions of tons to export abroad at the same time.

But that's in the far, far future. Right now, our priority should be in ensuring that as much of Brazil's resources go to feed our people and our industries instead. By assisting our corporations in establishing Brazilian subsidiaries through subsidizing the construction of new farms and factories, we can effectively reserve part of Brazil's vast natural wealth for America's purposes alone.
strings.USA_wal64_watch_brazilian_nationalisatio:
Ask an investor their second most hated word ('bankruptcy' would easily top the list), and they would most likely answer with 'nationalization'. Imagine waking up one day to find out that all your investments in some Third World hell hole were seized by buffoons playing government. Millions of hard-earned dollars, funneled over decades, all gone in a flash just like that -- and with not even a single cent for compensation!

So you can understand why our businessmen in Brazil are becoming antsy as of late. It's been all over the news, those grandiose words coming from Brasília: National industrialization, import substitution, Brazilian industries and Brazilian products... Enough dogwhistles to empty every pound a hundred miles away. None of them bode well for American assets in the country.

For the sake of American business, we should monitor the situation in Brazil more closely. We'll teach those macaques a lesson in respect the moment a politician of theirs says the 'N' word in live TV.
strings.USA_wal64_no_more_interference_desc:
Throughout its years of dominance, the disgusting political chimera that is the RDC had increasingly infracted on the foundations of this Union with its federalist politics, chief among them the shameful Civil Rights Act.

While opponents will decry President Wallace as some ridiculous frothing racist, his real agenda is simply protecting the average American from any more government infringement upon his freedoms, something any reasonable person will agree with.
And yes, that does include the freedom to keep the inferior races away.
strings.USA_wal64_business_subsidies_desc: Cuts are not enough, businesses need more money still, money that they can invest in more ambitious projects and spread out through the economy for all to enjoy. Sadly, this is money that they simply cannot gather through their normal day to day operations. Hard working businessmen of America, your cries have now been answered and the years of neglect have now ended. The Federal government must now play a more active role in business.
strings.USA_wal64_old_friends_desc: There is no sense in giving it over to some busybody Washington technocrats, the President's subsidy plan can be discussed an at once with far more practical expertise, and in a far more pleasant atmosphere. Nice dinner talks and meetings with the President's old and new friends in American Business are all the planning and preparation we need to draw up the new monetary injections.
strings.USA_wal64_new_business_desc: There's a place for corruption and cronyism, but deciding the economic future of the nation is not necessarily it. The budget set for new subsidies must be distributed to those who have the most promising ideas and the means to deliver them, not those with the most political clout. That is better for America, and what's good for America is good for President Wallace.
strings.USA_wal64_let_there_be_jobs_desc:
And then President George Wallace spoke “Let there be jobs” and Io and behold a million new workplaces hath opened and in those workplaces the poor and struggling have found daily bread and a path to future riches.
 All of this through just a little deficit spending.
strings.USA_wal64_consolidate_funding_efforts_de: President Wallace had personally laid out some additional guidelines as to where the business subsidies must go. Not only will specific industries that have more strategic importance to America, as the President described it, be given special priority, the subsidies should also concentrate on those state that need them most, where the people can most benefit from new business and work. That those states also happen to be ones that hold on to Jim Crow laws, and which are known to generally favor the President, is a complete coincidence.
strings.USA_wal64_money_for_the_entrepeneurs_des: We cannot let ourselves be enslaved to biases and favoritism, especially not when support of the people and from the people is at stake. The young and aspiring captains of industry must receive the administration's full support no matter what state they are from or what industry they wish to to partake in, as long as it is useful and sensible. At last, any man can become a king.
strings.USA_wal64_favored_states_desc: The NPP's current agenda is all about helping those parts of the country that have long been neglected by the wealthy and privileged parts of the nation. There is no reason to let the damn Yanks and other greedy bastards see any of our money, not when their states are already filled with privileged degenerates. The hardworking and put down people of the South and Midwest are the only ones who will understand the value of such generous gifts.
strings.USA_wal64_support_specific_industries_de: Vice President LeMay, Senator Jackson and some other big names within the Pact have been trying to influence the President's investment plans by making them focus primarily on heavy industry and the defense sector. Very well, a job in the defense sector is a job like any other and if it gets the damn hawks to shut the hell up for a minute Wallace will be more than happy to throw them a bone.
strings.USA_wal64_jobs_for_every_state_desc: Spite is not a good guide for economic policy, and as infuriating as the Yankee states are you simply cannot deny that they have greatly developed industry and many talented businessmen. It would be foolish to deny them funding to score cheap political points, when fairness bring much better results. And who knows, perhaps this can make some of them warm up to the President. Just maybe.
strings.USA_wal64_even_out_the_subsidies_desc: President Wallace has decided to listen to economic experts instead of caving to the pressures of the NPP's powerful hawk lobby. Getting the government in bed with the military industrial complex is a dangerous path for America, and a more even spread of subsidy money will allow for strong improvement of the average quality of life in America. After all, that is what this plan is all really about.
strings.USA_wal64_business_for_workers_desc: There is no purpose in helping business if said business only works to enrich the few at the top. With the opportunities they were given, the businessmen of America must accept that all of the employees who work for their wealth must receive their fair share of the profit. In a good, American business, everybody profits.
strings.USA_wal64_defederalization_desc:
Protecting the Rights of States shall be the guiding principle of the Wallace Presidency. The institutions of Federal government must be cut down before their creeping growth gets out of control, and their functions shall be far more effectively fulfilled by private entities and state governments.
 The Yankees and communists will say that this is nothing but a smokescreen for enforcing racial segregation, but the real America knows better.
strings.USA_wal64_american_welfare_desc:
The recent administrations have foolishly decided that government provided welfare is the answer to America's economic problems. This insanity stops now.
Cut and slash is the answer, and let the invisible hand of the free market elevate those worthy from their misery.
strings.USA_wal64_no_work_no_pay_desc: At the end of the day, the poor, downtrodden, unemployed members of American society are just that: poor and unemployed. And where there's unemployment in a society, there's rising economic fallout among the majority of citizens. In analyzing our economic standings in the world, the American economy's stagnation would open the door to overstepping overseas, and thus we must cut back on the unnecessary programs that drag down our progress. That being said, our administration realizes that the cutting back on support for the needy in America is not the most popular sounding action; however, we will not let our blue-collar workers to be without any support, and will make it up to them in due time. In this, defederalization will allow the American markets to flex outwards, and give them the support that they need soon. The South's campaign, along with our actions across the United States, all costs money, and cutting back on unemployment programs will bring us exactly what we need: funds.
strings.USA_wal64_american_healthcare_desc: In our administration's efforts for a freer and more independent American market, the elephant in the room has managed to flaunt itself more and more with every passing day and every incoming financial report: the drain of the American Healthcare system on our country's budget and the effects this has on the sick of our country. Even more unfortunate is the amount of Americans out there willing to tarnish and slander our administration by calling us “deplorable” and “heartless” in our recognition of the sacrifices we must make as a country. Scaling back federal funding of the American healthcare system will allow the budget of the nation to be far more flexible, and offer a more privatized system of care for our country, stimulating the economy further. With this in mind, those liberal fools in the Progressive Caucus and beyond will get what they want when they see we've developed a balanced economic standing for the United States of America.
strings.USA_wal64_privatized_healthcare_desc: Our efforts to rebalance the American economy in our scaling back of the healthcare system's budget has left a hole in the provider of care for the sick and injured Americans out there, some even being dedicated veterans of the United States military. That being said, it is time for the administration to look towards a greater supplier for care than the federal government ever could be: the private sphere of the American economy. There, big businesses have been looking to grow for years, and what better service to provide care to Americans than fellow American workers? These businesses have poured money into exploring options for American care, and if it can make a profit while doing so, what's the harm in that? Our administration's efforts have been to secure American freedom, and if the citizens can see our boldness in reforming the healthcare system, then they will know that we are a powerful force in fighting for their rights and freedoms!
strings.USA_wal64_help_your_doctor_help_you_desc:
“Doctors, they are some of the most hard working and most crucial members of Americans society. So, when you think your healthcare insurance is too expensive, just remember it goes into giving those irreplaceable lifesavers the compensation they need.”
Hopefully, if we drive this idea hard enough people will stop asking inconvenient questions about the healthcare system.
strings.USA_wal64_who_do_you_work_for_yourself: Who Do You Work For? Yourself!
strings.USA_wal64_who_do_you_work_for_yourself_d:
Now that Social Security and Medicare are out of the way, Wallace can turn his attention back to defending freedom on the homefront. Specifically, his plans to overhaul the American welfare state and replace it with American welfare states. See, federal aid is federal tyranny; it comes with too many strings attached and became just another way for Washington to force the South to toe the liberal line. President Wallace is going to change that forever.

Wallace will begin considering a revision of federal welfare laws to give states more control over how welfare funds are allocated. He could either retain some federal funding for state welfare while giving states more say over how it's spent, or he could cut the strings completely and let states fund their own welfare programs.
