The latter would be the purest economic expression of his defederalized vision, but may prove to be a bridge too far for rural white voters...
strings.USA_wal64_federal_aid_desc: The ideals of state autonomy are important, of course, but we cannot let them be the be all end all of our policy. Sometimes the federal government simply has to have a hand in how they spend their money, to ensure everything is done properly and the rights of honest Americans are respected. It's not hypocrisy, just common sense.
strings.USA_wal64_states_own_spending_desc: As any self respecting American Conservative knows, the local state governments always know best what the real needs of their people are. The governments must be free to set their own policy and use their budgets in whatever way they deem most appropriate.
strings.USA_wal64_the_federal_government_aint_no: We must get rid of the idea that the Federal government can replace the states in their duties. You are all responsible for your own problems, work on your own solution to fixing them instead of begging Washington for help.
strings.USA_wal64_end_of_the_subsidies_desc: If any of the states wants to start giving handouts, they are free to do so. Just don't expect to suck up any more money from the Federal Government. Certainly, every state should have enough money to finance its needs, and if they don't then maybe they should think about the weird little thing known as “sustainability”
strings.USA_wal64_the_dirty_state_of_schooling_d: The state the American education system has been brought to shows that not even the well-being of our children is sacred to the perfidious progressive. Overburdened with central Washington interventionism, their curricula and even administration distorted to the dictat of leftists social engineering. We need to tear this atrocious system down and replace it with a proper American one at once. For the sake of our children.
strings.USA_wal64_funding_for_schools_desc: The fact of the matter, upsetting as it may be to the parents and the educators, is that funding for public education is already bloated beyond control, and taking up millions that could be spent towards improving the economy. Remedies are not always pleasant, but the government must find a way to completely restructure how education is funded and cut out all the unneeded fat. By the time it's done, nobody will see any real damage to the school system.
strings.USA_wal64_lower_funding_for_black_school: It is blatantly unfair that the government is taking vast amounts of money from hard working white Americans just to pour them into trying to educate lazy inner city black youths. This solution kills two birds with one stone - not only are we saving money, we will also be giving those blacks a good reminder of their proper place in this society.
strings.USA_wal64_cut_education_funds_desc: If those goddamn progressives want things to be “non-discriminatory”, we can give them non-discriminatory. Let's institute some big general education cuts, with a few subtle provisions so that they hit harder where we need them to of course, but nothing the left can attach their claws to. We are saving money one way or another.
strings.USA_wal64_enforce_segregated_funding_des: Funny tricks with basic budget cuts are clearly not enough. With some new guidelines the remaining school subsidies can be redistributed so that they reach schools with good enough results that we can know it will be used properly. And everybody knows what “better results” mean. The figures don't lie.
strings.USA_wal64_states_own_salaries_desc: Why do hell is the Federal government expected to give out cash for the salary of every single goddamn teacher in the country? Managing these kinds of day to day expenses is much better left to local state administration, they'll know much better how to spend it and how to get the money than some Washington pencil pusher. Not to mention, look at how much money the Federal Government can save on it.
strings.USA_wal64_the_states_can_pay_in_full: The States Can Pay in Full
strings.USA_wal64_the_states_can_pay_in_full_des: While our previous funding reforms have already helped a lot, they were merely the first step to true education reform. As with the wages of teachers, so too should as much of the funding as possible be administered on that state level. Not only will this help our agenda of promoting every state as a unique and independent institution, it will also relieve a lot of burden from the Federal Budget.
strings.USA_wal64_lower_subsidies_to_the_states_: Since a more localized administration is clearly far more efficient, there is no need to keep pouring as much federal money into schools as before. If a state feels the need to put in more money, they can get it out of their own funds.
strings.USA_wal64_maintain_educational_subsidies: Some radical types within our pact and even among conservatives in the RDC believe that we should devolve education funding to the states, thus giving them greater political and cultural autonomy. While this might sound enticing, radical social experimentation with our youngest is exactly the kind of thing the Wallace administration stands against. No radical reform is needed at this point, we cannot accept the risk coming from completely revamping school organization... or the giving up of control over how our children are educated.
strings.USA_wal64_schools_cost_how_much_desc: Trips, training, labs, all sorts of expensive wasteful nonsense is being pushed to the top of the expenses list. The school's job is to get a bunch of whiny kids together in a room for a couple of hours and telling them how numbers work, how much money do you really need to do that? If the government is to give its valuable funds over to the education system, maybe for once it's the schools that should learn a little about managing finance. Some more cuts are in order.
strings.USA_wal64_separate_and_equal_it_was_made: We've tested the legal waters with some of those sneaky spending bill, now is the time to see what happens when we throw all subtlety out of the windows. A new bill written by National Progressive stalwarts shall enter votes, representing the purest form of the pro segregation faction. Naturally a bill this offensive will die in the water, but seeing the proceedings will let us gauge responses, and when time for the real bill comes everybody will remember the alternative.
strings.USA_wal64_segregate_teachers_pay_desc: Having a more direct oversight over how school funds are dealt out gives the administration some interesting options. Blatantly forcing educational facilities to give lower wages to black teachers is a risky and radical move, but the symbolic value of such an act would be invaluable in showing who is in charge.
strings.USA_wal64_american_education_desc: Education is the cornerstone of America. A free public education for all people is a wonderful thing, and it lets America's best and brightest shine. That's exactly why we must keep good, all-American schools! Separate but equal is the law of the land, like it or not, and the Wallace administration will make sure that American kids get a square, American education.
strings.USA_wal64_the_federal_government_has_no_:
Our predecessors have purged American schools of the two vital qualities that make them great: Segregation and the Christian faith. Brown v. Board, Engel v. Vitale, Abington School District v. Schempp, all these rulings by our lib-bribed Court have undermined our educational system and threatened our children's future. Our school-children may be divided by color but they are truly united in prayer! Today, God and America's children are going to return to their rightful place: Segregated school districts.

President Wallace will embark on a speaking tour of Southern high schools. Alongside sympathetic Christian leaders like Jerry Falwell, Bob Jones Sr., Pat Robertson, and W. A. Criswell, Wallace will expound on the importance of Our Savior and our traditional domestic institutions to America's youth. He shall swear to them, upon Scripture itself, that he will protect the integrity of their schools and lead them to a bright future.
strings.USA_wal64_i_encourage_you_to_follow_the_: I Encourage You to Follow the Southern States

President Wallace believes in states' rights. A state should be able to make their own decisions, especially when it comes to an issue as important as segregation. That said, the southern model has proven itself time and time again as the most effective model for the American people. President Wallace encourages the states of this great union to adopt the system of separate but equal treatment in all regards, but most importantly, education. Are the children not our future?
strings.USA_wal64_encourage_patriotic_curricula_: This world is a harsh one, especially for the children. They should be thanking God every night for the fact that they were born in the gold old U.S. of A. We have to show them just how lucky they are! We have to make sure that schools are teaching the good, wholesome facts of American history, and none of that good-for-nothing, gray fascist propaganda.
strings.USA_wal64_segregate_the_curricula_desc: It may be time to take separate but equal to its logical conclusion. If we adopt a segregated curriculum, we'll make sure that every American is getting an education tailored to their... people. Essentially, we'll make sure the true-blue Americans are getting a solid education getting them ready to lead this great nation, while not wasting too much time on... uh... er... more subservient Americans, if you understand me, sir.
strings.USA_wal64_the_yankee_schools_desc: Those damn Yankees! They just don't know how to sit down, shut up, and leave the government work to people who actually know what they're doing! They keep protesting the whole idea of segregated schools, and they're really making us look bad. We're gonna have to do something about these protesters at some point, before it gets too far out of hand. We have to either double down on segregated education or ease up a little bit.
strings.USA_wal64_enforce_segregation_through_le: Ultimately, we are the elected government entrusted with upholding the institutions of this great nation. The Supreme Court has found segregation to be all-American, and the Southern States have found segregation to be a superior system. We must secure an effective educational system. We must enforce segregation.
strings.USA_wal64_segregation_isnt_for_everyone_: “Segregation isn't for Everyone.” The words which fell upon Americans, whether by ear, by radio, or by television. No matter what, “Segregation isn't for Everyone” were the words that shocked some, relieved some, appalled others, but mostly, confused everyone. But more importantly, it was the words that President Wallace knew had to be spoken in order to patch the wounds dealt to the country after years of breaking apart. Even if we have recognized the overstepping committed by the federal government done in the past, we cannot continue to allow a single issue of American society to tear the entire foundation apart. Rather, we will scale back the overall radical take of the administration, and allow the people of the United States to solve the issue more calmly before the entire thing blows up in all of our faces.
strings.USA_wal64_a_true_devolutionary_education: The American people chose President Wallace and our administration in an effort to ensure that states felt as though their freedoms from the government were ensured, especially in the time of crisis that we find ourselves in now. However, in this, we would only serve to break apart the nation further if we reach too far, while if we give in to every demand, we will lose any chance of success in any regard by losing our base of support. Thus, we must seek to employ the most middle-driven answer possible to be found: we will not take direct action to enforce segregation within our school systems, nor will we give up on our efforts. We will stay true to our words, and give the states the rights they want by allowing them to decide upon the issue of segregation of the states' education system themselves. That way, the American people have a choice in their decision without the influence of the federal government to bog down the progress of the American individual.
strings.USA_wal64_devolve_the_choice_desc: In our efforts to secure the rights of states for everyone in the United States, and with it please the supporters and opposition of segregation within the school system, now the citizens seem angry over the lack of details. Therefore, so as to not lose the possible solution we have developed for the situation, we will give the states more of what they want: the segregation of water fountains, bathrooms, and public entertainment such as dances and ball games, and any other debate in segregation shall be opened up to the states. That way, we are in no way betraying our value of states' rights, but also allowing the opposition of segregation to earn their right as well. Even if the choice seems favorable to the citizens of the United States, especially within our support base in the South, it seems as though that former supporters of our administration have continued to grow disillusioned by our attempts at repair, and we may have a new foe at hand.
strings.USA_wal64_this_is_a_union_not_an_empire: This Is a Union, Not an Empire!
strings.USA_wal64_this_is_a_union_not_an_empire_: Our nation is not some imperial dominion where the emperor in DC can tell every man and woman and goddamn child what kind of land he should live in. America is a coalition of states each with their own culture, identity and way of life! We've got to let the people know this is how America is, and how it's going to be. President Wallace is going to go on the TV and give the people a very stern talking to - the federal government is not going to hold your hand, nor is it going to trample over the rights of the states! After all, wasn't there a whole civil war over states' rights?
strings.USA_wal64_this_is_a_family_States: This Is a Family of States
strings.USA_wal64_this_is_a_family_States_desc: The United States is our home. Like many homes, it is home to a family. Each member is unique and has their own agendas and systems of belief, but they all ultimately work together to keep the household running. Those members sometimes argue, and that's okay, because what family is perfect? What's not okay is for the head of the household to beat down anyone who doesn't like what they're doing! This is the situation with the states and the federal government, who tells the states that they can't do the things they want to do because some man in Washington thought it was unfair. President Wallace intends to present this argument to the American people - just because some states think things like segregation are wrong does not mean others can't stand differently.
strings.USA_wal64_increase_states_authority_desc: While the state governments have many rights within their borders, there are some things that they have to wait until some pencil pusher in Washington tells them they are allowed to do. And in the time that the bureaucracy takes to churn out its permission slip, the opportunity to act passes! We've got to cut the red tape and allow the states to act on their own initiative. It'll make their job easier, it'll make our job easier, and it will make those loudmouth losers in the streets' job - or lack thereof - a hell of a lot harder!
strings.USA_wal64_state_police_over_federal_desc: In their efforts to 'protect and serve' the federal government has in the past sent their own goons as 'reinforcements' to put down the so-called 'riots' by those opposed to their tyranny. How this is tolerated in our great and free country defies belief! Enough is enough. We are going to tell the federal authorities to get the hell back to Washington and go look for the actual enemies of America. The states themselves will be given total authority to use their own local forces to deal with issues as they see fit. Issues like those violent mobs of “progressives,” for example.
strings.USA_wal64_the_perth_conference_desc: The Australians have kindly agreed to host our economic conference for the Pacific nations of the OFN, and representatives from the United States, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand are scheduled to meet in a few days in Perth to discuss the most ambitious attempt at trade liberalization in modern history. But there's a great deal at stake, beyond just the bread and butter of tariff schedules. Industrial policies, subsidies, non-tariff barriers, labor protections and harmonization, business regulations, common working standards: all of these are the trusty tools of a trade negotiator. And with their deft application, we could one day hope to expand our trade pact, to transform a means of survival into a means to strangle the Japanese Empire and its dominions.
strings.USA_wal64_a_wall_of_dollars_desc: After weeks of tense negotiations, we've made good progress on the nitty-gritty details of streamlining tariffs and paving the way for a mutual opening of the protected sectors of the free Pacific nations. It is, in itself, a momentous achievement, which will give American industry the means to establish itself abroad without worrying about being squeezed out of a hostile market. As soon as the ink dries, tariffs, duties, and onerous regulations within a region comprising over two thirds of the world economy will disappear. More importantly for us, all tariffs, duties, and onerous regulations that had stonewalled America from accessing the Far East in its own terms in the past will vanish overnight. And in doing so, we will quarantine our allies from the economic predation of the Co-Prosperity Sphere on their doorstep, while promising the remaining neutral nations a viable economic rationale to resist the siren song of Tokyo.
strings.USA_wal64_the_indian_market_desc:
Sitting right outside the Sphere's outer limits is the Republic of India. Despite being blessed with the world's most fertile farmland, millions of square miles of mineral deposits, and the second largest population on Earth, the newly-independent nation still remains a dysfunctional state years after having broken free from the hold of the Raj. Nevertheless, India still has plenty of untapped potential -- potential which, in smart hands, can be harnessed into a very tidy profit.

This is where we come into the picture. Several Indian magnates and business leaders had attended the Perth Conference as self-proclaimed observers “acting upon Delhi's behest”. At length they spoke of the need for the Republic of Indian to formally join the CPFTCA -- God, that's a handful -- and how both we and they can benefit from the arrangement. Far be it from any good American businessman to decline free money, so we sent them away with a promise to “take their words under advisement”, a wink, and a nudge.

After a few dinners and dealings with our congressmen, they...
strings.USA_wal64_breach_the_market_desc:
...are fully on board with letting the Republic of India join the organization. It didn't take much to convince them; in fact, we may have gone overboard with the graphs and charts the interns had prepared days before. All they really asked for was how much money the companies putting jobs into their districts and “donations” into their campaign funds would make out of it. You can understand why it looked as if dollar signs popped out of their eyeballs when we multiplied the price of a can of Spam by five hundred million.

Now that we've taken care of things on our end, it's time to send Delhi the good news. Soon they'll be card-carrying members of the largest trade zone in the world -- and soon we'll get an extra half-billion loyal customers to profit from. Score another point for American business, baby!
strings.USA_wal64_quota_agreements_desc:
...are fully on board with letting the Republic of India join the organization -- under one condition: We'll have to ensure that our dealings with them are as fair as they can get. That means letting them decide how much of our goods will enter their markets every year, which of them get to enter and which don't, how much of a cut they'll get from our profits there, and so on and so forth. Likewise, we'll be able to set up quotas and restrictions for their own goods entering our borders.

Now why our Senators and Congressmen are all suddenly so gung-ho about trade barriers and regulations -- the very things we aimed to break -- we'll never know. They prattled on to a man about how we should assist “Indian development” and insulate ourselves from a supposed flood of Indian goods, but you can't help but think they were all led by wild guesses pulled straight from where the sun doesn't shine.

Now that we've taken care of things on our end, it's time to send Delhi the good news. We might not get as much money as we should've, but if our congressmen are right, then we'll have secured ourselves a good ally for a lifetime.
strings.USA_wal64_the_indian_market_2_desc:
YANK OR NOT, SPAM HITS THE SPOT!

From adai to appam, there's nothing that can't go with SPAM! SPAM is the perfect blend of pork shoulder, ham and spices. Packed full of meat and easy to prepare, SPAM can be made however you want it and still taste perfect: Cooked, boiled, chopped, ground into filling, hot, cold, spicy, dry, and so much more!

Fun for the whole family in a 12-ounce can! Whether it's to greet the kids in the morning or greet the mister after work, SPAM can be made at any time and for any occasion. Start or end the day right with a healthy serving of meat -- and nobody does meat better than SPAM!

It's an Indian sensation! From Punjab to Madras, SPAM has become a welcome companion in kitchens and tables all over the country. Families in America love it; now families in India can't live without it!

Own a can of the world's best canned meat for the low, low price of Rs. 25! Buy now!
strings.USA_wal64_lower_industry_specific_tax_de: The President's friends and acquaintances in the business world have been very pleased with the recent tax cuts, however the common sentiment is that more could be done. Many new and promising industries remain unviable due to myriad and complex reasons relating to the remaining corporate tax cut laws. With some furhter strategic cuts and breaks in specific places, those new investments would become entirely viable, and even extremely profitable.
strings.USA_wal64_I_love_capitalism_desc: President Wallace loves America, and few things are more American than true unrestrained capitalism. Who would ever want to fight against trusts and conglomerates and behind the door corporate deals, when the enrichment of the great industries is the enrichment of the nation? Let us now hold hands together in one grand public-private parnership and walk together into the sunrise.
strings.USA_wal64_the_american_dream_desc: The last two decades were a dark time for America certainly, but anyone who would declare that the American dream has been broken by the years of economic depression and national humiliation was dead wrong. The National Progressive Pact promised to let America arise like a Phoenix from the ashes, and arise it did. Now every day in this country a new business opens, a new undertaking is started and with it a new opportunity to those who dare to dream. Tell the tyrants and savages that America is back in the game, and this time it will not allow itself to be beaten so easily.
strings.USA_wal64_segregate_states_subsidies_des: Just because the States have been given more freedom in how they use their funds doesn't mean we can't budge the system in our favor a little. Giving more money to states that properly distribute their funding, by denying that funding to black schools for example, we can encourage some states to modify their policy so that can get a bigger share of the pie when it comes to the precious and quite scarce subsidies and reward those which are more important to the President. Certainly that would be very dubious from both a legal and ethical standpoint, but the political benefits far outweight the risks.
strings.USA_wal64_those_who_work_shall_see_their: Those Who Work Shall See Their Bounty Yield

To show that President Wallace really cares for the honest American worker, a higher Federal minimum wage will be established, one that will ensure the dignity of labor, hopefully we can find a way to persuade the businesses that investing in America is still as worthwhile as before.
strings.USA_wal64_lower_amount_of_claimants_desc: Some of those damn states are just giving money left and right, to whoever they find. We must enforce far stricter guidelines to guide their hand, so that they finally learn to have their policy guided by reality, not the softness of heart.
strings.USA_wal64_the_american_worker_desc: Hard choices and painful sacrifices had to be made, but at last all of it is paying off. We have created a new legal environment, one in which healthy business can grow while the worker can enjoy the fruit of their labor. America is now a better and more prosperous society, for anybody willing to put in the work necessary.
strings.USA_wal64_look_at_this_spare_cash_that_i: Look at This Spare Cash That I Just Found

One benefit from the Wallace administration's surgical focus on state driven education is that the exercise has rationalized a great deal of the education budget - perhaps not to the extent Wallace's most ardent states' rights supporters had crowed of, but enough to meaningfully impact America's fiscal metrics. It never hurts to have more cash, after all.
strings.USA_wal64_override_the_states_desc: Quite frankly, it appears the state governments of many of the Yankee states are run by utter and complete morons. They're fighting us back and forth, left and right over segregation (and just about everything else), and it's time for decisive action. States' rights are vital to the American experiment, but not when it threatens the Union! Let's remind these idiots who's really in charge.
strings.USA_wal64_i_will_not_stand_by_whilst_the: Like it or not, segregation is the future of the United States! Nationwide protests at every corner led by upstarts like MLK, school principles sneaking black kids into white schools; it seems this country has forgotten that segregation is the law! The Wallace administration will not stand by whilst the law is broken!
strings.USA_wal64_threatean_action_desc: We have made clear that this administration will not stand idly by while the law is broken. We have made clear that segregation is the future of the American education system. We have done just about everything we can. If we are to quell the unrest plaguing America, we must make clear that this administration will do what needs to be done. Make it clear to the nation that, should the need arise, we will mobilize the National Guard to enforce segregation.
strings.USA_wal64_jim_crows_crutch_desc: Our efforts, President Wallace's efforts, the administration's efforts, everyone's efforts to provide the citizens of America with a greater voice and choice in the direction of their lives within the United States, has not been fought for in vain. Consistently, the federal government has taken up way too much power for themselves, without feeling concern for the average American. But throughout all of our efforts, we have secured each and every right possible for the American citizen in a bloody, exhausting war of attrition against the strong opposition of freedom within the United States. Even now, after all we have done to serve them as the leaders of the country, the unyielding liberals in the North poke and prod, calling President Wallace “Jim Crow's Crutch” in an effort to portray backwardness, rather than our administration's upholding of freedom and tradition. Is it not right? Have we not worked to simply try to maintain American society's morals and rights for the individual?
strings.USA_wal64_legitimize_the_states_authorit: The federal government and the state governments do not always see eye to eye on things, nor should they. States, after all, have a more clear picture of what is best for them than the ivory tower politicians in the capital who are too busy making sure the Japanese don't blow up the world to care. So, state governments should have much more of a say in how they are governed, specifically with regards to ensuring that the constitution is abided by. State governors might consider... certain... laws to be unconstitutional, and should have the right to reject and void any directives that defy the constitution. Per their perception of it, at least.
strings.USA_wal64_you_are_a_citizen_of_a_state_a: You Are a Citizen of a State and the Union

America is a glorious land, for sure, but perhaps we have focused too much on praising the whole before the parts that make it up. When people think politics, they think DC, not the legislative battles going on in their own state courts. We must remind the people that true representation begins at home, and President Wallace means to give a big fancy speech to achieve this. The people must always salute Old Glory, of course, but by getting them to remember the cause of their own state as well, we can get them more interested in local politics. And in doing so, we secure more support to defend each state's way of life.
strings.USA_wal64_encourage_state_level_identifi: Back in the good old days of America, a man considered himself a man of his state first and the union second. A man from Georgia called himself Georgian, and a Virginia boy took pride first and foremost in his Old Dominion state. Why did this ever stop? Let us make the states proud again! A public campaign to encourage the fine folks of our nation to take joy and honor in their home state will bolster the unique American spirit, and perhaps finally drill into those civil rights activists heads the idea that not everyone in this country is exactly like them. We will celebrate the diversity of the American nation!
strings.USA_wal64_restore_states_militia_desc: Since the founding of our great country, many states have maintained their own militias outside the control of the US Armed Forces. These patriotic bands of brothers serve their state governors directly, keeping their homeland safe and responding to local crises. Membership of many of these militias has declined gradually since the end of the war, but now is the perfect time to kick them back into gear! Put out some recruitment campaigns, let's get the red-blooded sons of our nation back to protecting the states that gave them birth. And with a few relaxed restrictions, state governors can put the militias to work dealing with these... current crises.
strings.USA_wal64_the_matter_of_segregation_belo: Many states want segregation. We heartily agree with them, but we must confess that even with us in charge, the federal government coming down to do all the work for them would be slightly hypocritical to our campaign promises. No, instead we must ensure that each state has a clear path to implementing segregation on their own terms. And that means ensuring that they have the resources they need to bulldoze any obstacles that stand in their way. From now on, the word of each state's governor shall carry as much authority within their state as the President's word does to the nation.
strings.USA_wal64_stop_whining_desc: Still, the whiny activists march out in our streets, demanding that the democratically decided will of the people be overturned. Still, they damage public property, block our highways, and callously beat up good, honest Americans. No more. It's time to throw the book at them. Lock them up, smack them down, do whatever needs to be done to shut them up. And if any demonstrator ever lays down in front of my car, it'll be the last car he'll ever lay down in front of.
strings.USA_wal64_fully_segregate_transport_desc: A couple of rabble rousers keep trying to sit in the wrong place on the bus. How quaint. How radical. How incredibly inconvenient to honest Americans just trying to get to work. In any case, the matter of segregated transport is apparently an issue now. Well we're going to end the issue, by federally encoding the right for states to tell people exactly where they can sit, be it on a bus or a boat or an airplane. If you're too damn lazy to walk to the back, you're clearly too lazy to be going anywhere of importance, and should leave the seats to those who actually have someplace to be.
strings.USA_wal64_segregation_is_the_american_wa: At this point, segregation is a way of life for many states, and why should they be stopped? America is the land of the free, and being free to choose what people you want to associate with is as American as apple pie. We'll put out a media blitz encouraging people to see things our way. Newspaper ads, TV hitpieces, hell we'll send some guys to speak at universities and public rallies if we have to. Everyone is equal, but we have the right to choose to be separate, and we need to make it known that this is what America stands for!
strings.USA_wal64_unlock_the_door_for_jim_crow: The End of the Civil Rights Act
strings.USA_wal64_unlock_the_door_for_jim_crow_d: Mister President, throughout your entire time in office you have had one single goal and that is to end the abomination known as the Civil Rights Act which not only tramples upon our God given American liberty and independence, but also threatens our way of life and everything with it. All the groundwork is now in place, the segregation of our bureaucratic trickling, the removal of opposition from the Northern States, and all your other projects. We have the groundwork, we have the support. It is time to remove the desperate work of a misguided man and open the door for Jim Crow!
strings.USA_wal64_the_government_shall_maintain_: What the hell are we waiting for? The people have spoken! We promised to keep segregation and that's exactly what we're going to do. The federal government has until now used its power to put the states down, but now we shall use it to instead lift them up. They want laws? We've got em. Lots of them. So many laws that Martin Luther King and his thugs won't know where to begin trying to oppose them. The federal government shall legally back every state looking to maintain its laws on segregation, so that opponents won't just have to go through local courts, but the full might of our own legal dominion. Is this federal tyranny? Of course not, it's what the people voted for!
strings.USA_wal64_dirty_state_of_schooling: Wallace will look into reforming the education system.
strings.USA_wal64_Gage_Central_American_intrest_: The nations of the world have endured long pains of suffering from the crushing weight of Japan's influence. In this, the countries of Central America have grown in an economically difficult scenario, leaving them clawing to get any form of support possible. Larger nations, such as Mexico, continue to dodge away from their neutrality; however, smaller nations, such as Nicaragua, Guatemala, and Honduras, are able to be swayed in the interest of financial opportunity in their desperate scenarios, and have even resorted to accepting Japanese diplomatic action to aid themselves. No more. We won't allow neutral nations of the world to fold more towards the Japanese's bullying. Thus, we will offer all we can afford to make sure the close countries of Central America will be warm to the idea of the Pacific Trading Zone, while also showing an act of good faith to the American people of the administration's willingness to impede Japan's domination. Besides, Americans love tropical fruit, right?
strings.USA_wal64_Gage_Oceanian_intrest_desc: The Empire of Japan's rampage across the Pacific before, during, and after the Second World War left countless of nation's bruised, bloody, and broken. With no one left to turn, these nations were first in having to succumb to the coercion wrought by the Japanese. Now, after years of this suffering, countries like Australia and New Zealand can finally find the strength to turn towards a larger power to help them fight against Japanese influence: the United States. The administration will send multiple nations to these countries in an effort to offer subsidization in their steps forward, while also encouraging new and empowering trade deals between the United States and their governments. As far as our work has produced, these countries appear to be the most sympathetic to our cause after their suffering, and it is the governments' greatest interest to secure allies in the face of the dangerous Empire of the East.
strings.USA_wal64_gauge_indian_interests_desc: Across the Pacific, within the foreign lands sprawling across Asian lands, lies a powerful force to contend against the Japanese Empire's coercians: India. The Indian people of the subcontinent have managed to survive against the prowling of imperial predators for centuries, and now, they are forced to protect themselves against the Empire's growing sphere of influence. In this, they have strived to protect their interests in an individual standoff; however, we know better. We know that the fight against the Japanese does not require a single fiery will for change, but a group's collective fury in destroying the gross force in the world, not from theories and estimates, but from American blood. Now, although we may seem foreign, or even alien towards the Indian government, we must extend our hand through ambassadors to discuss the joining of the Pacific Trading Zone, to fight against the Japanese Empire not one on one, but as brothers in arms.
strings.USA_wal64_negotiate_the_terms_desc: Now that the administration has managed to collect our possible allies together, it's time to begin settling the terms of our agreements in Perth, and attempt to fully solidify the Pacific Trading Zone. Consistently, we have managed to see that our offerings to these democratic nations have been viewed with great respect and honor, and together, it appears that our plan to curb the Japanese's power over these free nations is succeeding more and more. Each collection has a different part to play in the trading agreements, be it Oceania's stock profits, Central America's fruit and agricultural exports, and India's production market, but no matter what, the United States of America is benefitting, and the Empire of Japan is suffering. Having said this, the ROI government continues to make arguments with some terms involved in the agreements; thus, we must do all we can to maintain the strength of the Pacific Trading Zone during the conferences at Perth.
strings.USA_wal64_promptly_pass_the_perth_pact_d: Our administration has been more than successful in our interconnecting of the various regions around the world into the Perth Pact, and thus into the Pacific Trading Zone. Already, the agreements have been ratified domestically as well; in this case, the Senate has willingly approved of our designs and work put forth into the Perth Pact, and allowed our ideas to succeed. The citizens of the United States, along with the peoples of Oceania, Central America, and India, have consistently felt the crushing weight of Japan's heel dig into their backs by means of economic and political strong-arming. Now, however, we shall turn the tide within the international sphere and put Japan on the economic defense with the loss of its potential assets. Furthermore, our administration will be able to say it has successfully fought back against the Japanese, and show that by the will of the National Progressive Pact does our country step forward in progress!
strings.USA_wal64_drawn_out_trade_authorization_: Unfortunately, it appears as though the domestic powers of the federal government in the United States have come to seek the death of a fair and empowering deal struck by our administration with the international community. Although the Conference has demonstrated a sense of greatness and possible prosperity within the possibilities of the Perth Pact's creation, various political entities have stood against the Nationalists in its striving for greatness for greatness for both American and people around the world. The RDC as a whole seems to hate the notion of actually producing an effective form of shielding against the Japanese, as if they don't give a damn about the suffering of the world at the hands of the Japanese! And then the more liberal-minded wingnuts across the nation don't seem to care if the Perth Pact is useful or not, due to our disagreements over social policy. Our administration will not fold against the political bullying of a just alliance due to some petty squabbling!
strings.USA_wal64_win_em_over_desc:
The National Progressive Pact is founded on one great principle: America First. American interests come first in diplomacy, especially when it comes to reclaiming our stolen State, but the needs of American workers and families come first as well. Sure, some of them may be on the fence about our government thanks to the segregation issue, but we're going to show Americans across the country that they have no greater friend than President Wallace!

President Wallace will expand his support base through two expansions of popular social welfare programmes: Medicare and Social Security. By giving workers across the country some more federal support, he should be able to coast to victory again by grateful seniors and the newly-insured.
strings.USA_wal64_partys_plan_desc:
Like it or not, we're all in this together. The Progressive bloc of the Pact has supported Medicare and Social Security for a long, long time; they can take the lead on this issue. After all, this is about unifying the Pact, so we should let the Pact collectively chart our course.

Wallace will cede the floor to the Progressive when it comes to these new bills. By letting the likes of Marine Neuberger and Scoop Jackson be the primary champions of the bills, Wallace will demonstrate that he is putting party ahead of ideology. By doing so, he will be able to reach out to Progressive politicians, northern Nationalists, and even a few Democrats to secure their votes or his legislation. Of course, just because the Progressive is leading the charge doesn't mean he can't slip a few of his own policies into these bills...
strings.USA_wal64_WALLACE_SHALL_LEAD_THE_WAY_des:
When will these namby pamby “progressives” get it through their heads that Wallace is their President? He won the primaries and the general fair and square, and if they don't want a good old Southern boy defining their doctrine then they can find another party! They're getting their Medicare, they're getting their Social Security, but they're getting those bills exactly the way President Wallace wants 'em written!

President Wallace will make clear that this is his party by being the main champion of Social Security and Medicare. The Nationalists will take center stage in policy advocacy and spread its own Dixiecrat message across the country in the process. The nation will see these bills as classic, down home Southern mutual aid just like the Kingfish proposed back in the day. This may alienate the Progressive, but can rally new voters from coast to coast to the Nationalist bloc.
strings.USA_wal64_social_security_desc:
We got a lot of old timers in this country who are still working into their twilight years. Who can blame 'em, when they got no savings to retire on? But this makes the job market that much harder for youth to break into. If we want to keep this economy going, we gotta get these geezers out of it; Lowering the Social Security age could be just the ticket...

Wallace will begin drafting his Social Security revisions. By proving the NPP is a friend to the aged, this will boost their support among America's most frequent voters. There may be several opportunities to alter this bill to fit the interests of certain members of our pact as well...
strings.USA_wal64_segregated_security_desc:
Social Security isn't just for retirees, it also includes unemployment benefits as well. Therein lies a problem. The Southern economy thrives on dirt cheap labor performed by Black hands. Millions of Blacks perform farm labor or domestic help for a pittance because they have no other options to feed themselves, especially if they lost their jobs elsewhere. But providing them with unemployment benefits and old age pensions could leave them with enough money to refuse taking low-wage agricultural and domestic work. This could throw the fragile Southern social and economic system into disarray. Thurmond wants us to guarantee that won't happen, and we have just the plan.

We will exclude farm workers and domestic laborers from Social Security coverage. No work they perform shall entitle them to unemployment benefits or old age pensions, so they will have no freedom to quit their job on a whim and look for better ones. This will de facto segregate Social Security, since the overwhelming majority of those workers are Black. It'll shore up support among our Dixiecrat base, but horrify the Progressive wing of the Pact.

Thurmond is adamantly opposed to any social welfare programs that could threaten Southern domestic institutions, and will take as many votes as he can from us if we don't placate him.
strings.USA_wal64_northern_adjacents_desc:
The Nationalist bloc has always had two wings: Southern Dixiecrats and the old-school northern Republicans. The latter are far more business oriented, so it may take a little convincing in order to get them behind Social Security, but for the sake of this bill we have to try.

Wallace will meet with Northern Nationalist leaders Margaret Chase Smith and Spiro Agnew to secure their support for the Social Security Expansion bill. By explaining its effects of getting the elderly to retire, he will show that it will enable more youth to enter the workforce and make enough money to drive consumer spending. With our entire bloc behind us, passing the bill should be easy peasy.
strings.USA_wal64_spend_spend_spend_desc:
You want a pension? You got a pension! You lost your job? You ain't losing your house! Wallace is your friend in Washington and he's here to bail you out of a jam. Name your price, and we'll foot the bill! Give me your poor, your tired, and your needy and we'll get 'em back on their feet!

Wallace will offer incredibly generous entitlement payouts in his Social Security Expansion bill. The business-minded Nationalist leaders in the North will balk, but this strong bill will win us so many votes they can eat crow.
strings.USA_wal64_asses_as_allies_desc:
Across the aisle, our closest counterparts are the Republican wing of the RDC. They're a mite more conservative than the Democrats, but they generally understand the value of social welfare. We might be able to reach out to Goldwater and get him on board with our new legislation, all though the Buckley-ite Yankee will be a tough fella to convince.

Alternatively, we could reach out to Bobby Kennedy and his more progressive Democrats. He despises us for our stance on the Civil Rights issue, but he's always been a friend of the working man. We're honestly surprised he hasn't defected to the Progressive Bloc by now.
strings.USA_wal64_medicare_desc:
Social Security Expansion will help get the elderly out of the workforce and stimulate economic mobility, but it's not enough on its own. Many employers provide health insurance, and a lot of seniors are afraid to lose their healthcare if they retire. Thus, the NPP is proposing we further expand on national Medicare - a plan that will provide more retirees with health insurance.

This new legislation will not only prove popular with retired voters, the largest voter group by far, but also with the Progressive Caucus of the NPP. If we can mollify them with Medicare, they might look the other way on Wallace's states' rights legislation...
strings.USA_wal64_restrict_coverage_desc:
Byrd and Thurmond are up in arms about the new Medicare law. They say that if Blacks start getting coverage under the program then hospitals will have every incentive to desegregate and accept their payment. Moreover, they're quite worried that Blacks will start quitting their low-paying jobs in the delicate Southern economy, knowing their medical needs will be taken care of by Uncle Sam. Wallace hardly needs to assure them that they have nothing to fear.

We will add clauses to the Medicare law exempting retirees who were previously domestic and agricultural laborers from coverage. As these professions are overwhelmingly Black, this will dramatically reduce the number of Black patients hospitals could conceivably see, and also serve to keep those individuals in the cheap workforce.

Thurmond is adamantly opposed to any social welfare programs that could threaten Southern domestic institutions, and will take as many votes as he can from us if we don't placate him.
strings.USA_wal64_more_more_more_desc:
You want healthcare? You got healthcare! Lower cost insurance for the elderly! Uninterrupted nursing home care for the chronically ill! Annual cost of living increases for benefits! No earning limitations for seniors! Disability benefits too! If you need health insurance then Doctor Wallace is in!

We will greatly expand the benefits package offered by Medicare. Our budget will take a hit, and the Northern Nationalist Bloc will cry foul, but by God will the voters love it! This bill will build the momentum we need going into the next elections!
strings.USA_wal64_encourage_elephants_desc:
Johnson was always ranting and raving about his so-called Great Society. Now, we ain't standing for any infringements on state sovereignty over their domestic issues, but his healthcare policies may dovetail well with our own. Maybe we could find an unlikely ally in the Dems.

We will reach across the aisle for a meeting with LBJ and the liberal Democrat leaders. We could offer to make Medicare a bipartisan bill, and hopefully secure their support when the bill reaches the Senate floor.

Johnson is as stubborn as a Texas longhorn on the integration issue, and won't stand for any coverage restrictions.
strings.USA_wal64_finalize_the_act_desc:
We are now in the process of completing the final draft of our Medicare Expansion bill. This bill, if passed, will hopefully ensure better healthcare coverage for millions of less fortunate Americans.

This bill is controversial among the Northern ranks of the Nationalist Bloc, but has broad support amongst the South and the Progressives. We can still make a few changes, if necessary, before sending it to the Senate.
strings.USA_wal64_get_it_ready_for_congress_desc:
Now that we've decided what we want Social Security to accomplish, it's time to prepare it for the Senate floor. We will formalize the particulars, shake hands, and get a final draft out of committee and into Congress.

Depending on the actions taken previously, we may have secured or ruined our chances of getting it to Wallace's desk. There's still time to prepare in case we have any other changes to make.
strings.USA_wal64_senate_votes_desc:
At long last, it's time for Medicare and Social Security Expansion to have their day on the Senate floor. Let the discourse, debate, and hopefully not filibusters begin!

These new laws are critical to the unity of the National Progressive Pact. They are humanitarian ventures that will cement our status as the Party of the little guy. They are the foundation upon which we will build our self-help initiatives. They are the populist credentials Wallace and his party will need in the next election.

Hopefully he'll see these on his desk after the Senate vote.
strings.USA_wal64_the_job_corps_act_desc:
The American Dream has always been that any man can achieve prosperity through hard work and determination. Consequently, we will never get over our post-war Malaise unless we can get our unemployed youth into the workforce. President Wallace once again has a plan for that.

Wallace will draft a bill to create the Job Corps: A federal program that offers free-of-charge education and vocational training to young people ages 16-24. This will allow young men and women of low income and good character to get the training they need to pursue a fulfilling career path. From welding to nursing to seamanship, Wallace's Job Corps will allow our young down and outs to find their calling in life!
strings.USA_wal64_looks_towards_rust_belt_desc:
Wallace is harsh, but he is fair. The Job Corps is here to serve all Americans, not just the ones who voted for him. We will have to make this program nationwide if it's going to be taken seriously by the public.

Wallace will inject the funds necessary to set up Job Corps offices in every state. While more expensive, this will broaden the appeal and effectiveness of the program. Who knows? We might just pick up some extra votes in the Steel Belt while we're at it...
strings.USA_wal64_dixies_land_desc:
It's no secret that the South suffers the worst from unemployment. The Yankees burned our country to the ground and then their carpetbaggers looted whatever was left. It's time to rectify this injustice and pay reparations to the South in the form of the Jobs Corps.

The Jobs Corps will be restricted to “underprivileged” states, that is, the South. All the funds will create new work opportunities in the land of cotton, and the unemployment subsidies will enlarge their prosperity as well. This should bring the South up to par with the North in economic terms, as well as shore up our support base.
strings.USA_wal64_the_USP_desc:
Now we can actually hash out the details and implement our plan for Southern subsidies. The North will roll their eyes but they can take a hike. We're talking geographical wealth redistribution on a national scale, progressives should love it!

Our programs to aid underprivileged states will come into effect. As well as localizing the Job Corps, this will also involve large subsidies to construct infrastructure and bring business to the South. We'll start to see real returns from this policy in the form of improved Southern infrastructure and copious Southern votes.
strings.USA_wal64_expand_UE_subsidies_desc:
The Job Corps is a marvelous tool to relieve unemployment in the South, but it's hardly enough. For those who don't qualify for the Job Corps, Wallace may have to pinch his nose and expand entitlements. The South can rest assured, however, that these entitlements come with no strings attached.

President Wallace will announce an expansion of the unemployment subsidies offered by the Underprivileged States Program. This will hit our budget hard, but significantly raise the Southern standard of living. It'll nab us more Southern votes and help bring Dixie up to the national average. Of course, States will decide where that money shall be spent, and it's hardly Wallace's fault if some population groups receive less than others.
strings.USA_wal64_segregated_corps_desc:
Wallace won his election on a mandate to defend “States Rights”; everyone and their mother knew what he meant. Now that the Jobs Corps has been restricted to the South, it is necessary and proper that the Job Corps embody Southern social values to the fullest extent.

Wallace will fully segregate the Job Corps. The races will work more efficiently when they work separately. More to the point, Black corps members can be given priority assignments to work for which they are more traditionally suited: agriculture, cooking, and domestic labor. Progressives may cry foul, but the South has a right to run its Jobs Corps however it feels best.

This will be extremely controversial and likely be challenged in court. Hopefully, SCOTUS is on our side.
strings.USA_wal64_hurrah_hurrah_desc:
General Robert E. Lee once said that “duty” is the sublimest word in the English language and President Wallace truly understands what he meant. He has done his duty to every man, every woman, and every child in the South. He fulfilled his duty toward honesty and economy in the national government so that no Southern man shall have a part of his livelihood cheated and no Southern child shall have a bit of his future stolen away.

And lest the progressives jeer, Wallace has shown that he wants jobs and a good future for both the South's races. He has invited the African-American citizens of the South to work with us from their separate racial station, as we will work with them, to develop and grow in individual freedom and enrichment. This is the basic heritage of Wallace's religion, of which he makes full practice, for we are all the handiwork of God.

President Wallace has come home, not to burn the South to the ground as the Yankees did, but to bring the true jubilee; he has come to usher in a new era of prosperity and restore its antebellum glory. Three cheers for Wallace, and three cheers for Dixie!
strings.USA_wal64_ad_with_union_boss_desc:
The AFL-CIO hates Wallace. They court integrationist activists, even in Alabama, and deride the President as an enemy of the working man. They have betrayed the Progressive Bloc, their old allies, to back the RDC's next campaign against the Wallace administration. The AFL-CIO is fully committed to throwing Wallace out of office in the next election.

At least, that's what their leadership says.

Behind closed doors, the union bosses panic about the “Wallace plague” sweeping their rank and file. According to an internal poll, a full third of AFL-CIO members supported President Wallace in the last election, and their numbers are only growing. President Wallace is going to use the new Job Corps program to seize the moment and bolster his support base among unions. He will put out a new ad for the program in which he meets with ordinary workers, including ones recently employed thanks to the JOBS Act, and tell them he's the best friend that a union man ever had. He'll hopefully expose the disconnect between the labor aristocrats and their members, weakening the credibility of the unions in the political scene.
strings.USA_wal64_create_the_cccs_desc:
The Job Corps was a good start to relieving unemployment, but there's more work to be done. Our nation's precious natural resources are under threat and we need plenty of manpower to protect them. Time to put our remaining layabouts to work maki9ng our nation beautiful again.

Wallace will create a temporary work relief program, the Civilian Conservation Corps, which will put unemployed Americans to work building infrastructure and taking care of our natural landscapes. They will work to build state parks, prevent floods, pave new roads and air ways, and so much more. States, of course, will be in control of the structure of their local CCC's, so the South may determine work assignments for individuals of each race precisely as they see fit.
strings.USA_wal64_incentivize_work_desc:
Wallace's unemployment programs are built around the principle of self-help. We give people jobs so they can work and build our economy, we don't just dole out entitlements! In order to keep our welfare system economically viable, we'll need to completely reorient it towards self-help work programs!

Wallace will gut funding for unemployment benefits after implementing the Jobs Corps and CCC initiatives. This will save our budget, and shouldn't hurt most workers since they'll either already be employed or be eligible for Job Corps and CCC assistance. Of course, if some States act with discretion as to which racial groups benefit more from those programs, that's their prerogative.
strings.USA_wal64_court_the_center_desc:
Wallace has little patience for the Progressive bloc; Wallace also badly needs their support. Most importantly, he needs the Progressives to assure the North that his new programs aren't racially biased. Time to give Guy a call...

President Wallace will recruit Progressive leader William Guy to go on a media tour praising his job-creation programs. He will assure the public that they will benefit all Americans, regardless of their color, as they put the country to work from coast to coast. This should bind our pact closer together and maybe get us a few more votes in the next election.

strings.USA_WAL_new_deal_desc:
President Wallace won his election on a promise to defend the little guy from two bullies: Federal tyranny and crippling poverty. To make good on the latter, he has proposed new expansions to Medicare and Social Security programs to provide Americans with health insurance and retirement benefits. Yet while they are meant to promote unity within the £GFX_npp_texticon National Progressive Pact, these bills may prove to be as controversial as his states' rights legislation.

The Dixiecrat wing of the Nationalist Bloc supports the general goals of the new programs but insists on restricting their coverage to exclude Black Americans. Meanwhile, the £GFX_npp_c_texticon Progressives Bloc and the northern £GFX_rd_d_texticon Democrats demand equal access to these programs for all, regardless of race or color. Finally, the fiscally conservative Republicans and Northern Nationalist Senators are ambivalent on the race issue but are averse to expanding the welfare state.

The President's political acumen will be put to the test as he juggles the competing ambitions of these factions in hopes of securing enough votes to pass these bills. Success will cement Wallace's credibility as a bridge-building statesman, while failure will damage his reputation for years to come.
