It was an old building, an unfashionable one. The few times he was in his office pretending to work, he would catch glimpses of aging clerks and stockbrokers, a relic of an older, drabber time. Looking at them made him feel a pang of annoyance, an awareness of his own mortality.

He was so focused on the old men that he failed to react as his associate Robert walked in, jacket missing. He slapped a copy of the Times on his desk. “You see this?” Robert said, furious. “The fucking morons in Washington. The fucking...”

Bryce forced himself to turn. “There's a reason I don't read anything outside the Style and Finance sections, Robert. You're going to develop wrinkles reading about Nazis, gridlock, the situation in Africa, more Nazis, that Imperium guy...”

“You bastard, I'm angry because this is about our finances. LeMay, fucking incompetent, just blew our biggest chance to make bank. Completely fumbled his goddamn bill like a-.”

He broke off and let out a frustrated grunt as Bryce leafed through the newspaper. There was a photo of a sullen LeMay and an overwrought op-ed from someone with the Chamber of Commerce. Deeper in the folds was some kind of horse-race analysis, speculation about LeMay's shrinking credibility. Bryce tried not to think of the money he'd lost, of how he might one day become like the old men across the street.

“You know, aside from the whole segregation thing, I didn't think Wallace was that bad,” Bryce said. “At least he knew how to pass a goddamn bill. How are we supposed to compete with those Nazi fucks now?”

Bryce did not disagree. “Obviously, none of this is ideal but screaming won't change anything. Let's talk about ways forward over a working lunch. Consider how we can make our frustrations known.”
strings.USA_sen_bill.225.a: I'll tell my secretary to get a reservation at Sardi's.
strings.USA_sen_bill.225.b: Good luck getting a reservation at Sardi's this late.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_700:
The Trade Expansion Act is a radical attempt to promote free trade, perhaps the most radical attempt to be seriously considered by the US Congress. Masterminded by Secretary of Commerce Henry Fowler, the bill would grant the President of the United States unprecedented authority to negotiate tariff reductions with other nations by up to 80 percent. It includes various provisions meant to spur free trade arrangements and otherwise “strengthen mutual trade benefits in an open and nondiscriminating way.”

While the bill has enthusiastic support from the Chamber of Commerce and other business groups who extol the virtues of free trade in “unshackling America's economic potential,” the response in other quarters has been notably muted. Trade unions have expressed concern that unrestricted trade will undermine US wages and encourage manufacturers to relocate their factories overseas. Even the White House's support appears tepid, with the President offering bland platitudes about the ways the bill would expand OFN cooperation and little more.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_900: No one said cleaning up America was going to be easy...or good for optics. However, it is best to eat your vegetables before getting to the steak. The Clean Streets Act are the metaphorical vegetables of our Urban Renewal agenda. This Bill will give police the authority and funding needed to keep high-traffic areas, both pedestrian and vehicular, free of the homeless. Instead of being forced to grovel on the street for funds, the homeless of America will be given paths to wealth and generate upward mobility. However, it must all start with this Act.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_901:
It is a moral failure that we punish the poor for being in such circumstances. With the passing of this bill, not only will we give expanded funding to Soup Kitchens, but a vast quantity of homeless shelters will be opened in every metropolis in America.

Each resident will be provided with amenities and a roof over their heads. Along with a plethora of opportunities to get back on their feet. The days of being forced to beg on the streets are over.
strings.USA_sen_bill_name_902: The Substance Abuse and Recovery Act
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_902:
It is time to act on our promises to the poorest of us Americans. The Substance Abuse and Recovery Act is aimed not just at the homeless, but the addicted and the afflicted. Alcoholism, and drugs, these are silent killers across America. It affects Veterans, the Homeless, Wall Street investors, and all those in between.

This act will not only be a step toward destigmatizing seeking help. It will also give crucial money to underfunded Substance Rehabilitation centers across the country. A bill like this is long overdue, and it is only right that our Administration makes a push toward passing it.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_903:
For generations of Americans, the pathways offered by education have provided the means to achieve the American dream, to do better, and leave for their children more than what they had themselves. Historically Black Colleges and Universities have provided this path for many African-Americans who have otherwise found their future locked away by the doors of racial prejudice.

While the barriers of racial segregation have fallen in recent years, these HBCUs still provide a crucial role in facilitating Post-Secondary education to millions who'd otherwise be denied.

The Equality in Education Act will provide these institutions the funding needed to modernize facilities, improve salaries, and increase admissions to help a new generation of African-Americans access opportunities denied to their parents.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_904: Safe housing is a human right in the 20th century, and it is high time that government takes action against surging rates of homelessness among minority communities. The Urban Housing Opportunity Act is just one prong in President Philip Hart's assault on inequality in the great American city, and it cuts no corners in the process; the act will fund studies on the depth of racial inequality in housing, its origins, and potential solutions. While the act itself does not provide immediate benefits for these bereaved communities, this pilot into proactive policy planning will allow our administration to reap benefits in future policies.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_905:
The Department of Commerce is maxed out, we cannot give it any more funding without drawing the anger of Debt Hawks...However, that doesn't mean we can still funnel money towards our highway system construction! The USDOC Modernization Act of {year} will give the Department of Commerce crucial funding that they have been lacking for years. The US highway system has been determined by the Department of Commerce as a vehicle of economic opportunity.

Therefore, any funding given to the Department of Commerce will find its way back to the highway system. Everyone knows this, the Department of Commerce, Congress, Mrs. Jacobs, and the President. However, everyone ends up getting something they want.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_906:
The results of the Highways built so far have been phenomenal! So it is only fitting we construct more. If we could have our way, every small town in America would have an on-ramp to the highway.

Alas, we will take what we can get from the Highway Expansion Act. It will be pivotal in giving additional funding to infrastructure projects that are currently lagging behind. The age-old solution to these problems is to merely throw more money at the problem! So, if we play our cards right, thousands more miles of highway will keep the wheels of Americans rolling across the country.
strings.USA_sen_bill_name_907: The Arm Control and Indexing Act of {year}
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_907:
Indexing, a pretty formidable weapon in our arsenal of gun regulation. The Indexing Act of {year} will make sure that guns are less likely to fall into the hands of extremists. A national database of individuals flagged as dangerous gun owners will be available to police departments across the country and across federal levels.

An action as small as indexing can have far-reaching effects. It does not infringe on the Second Amendment, yet it can easily tip off authorities to people who wish to abuse their right to bear arms to do harm.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_908:
There is nary a steel worker on coal miner that has forgotten the Battle of Blair Mountain. The United States would not be where it is without the laborers that built this country. It is long overdue that the Federal Government took an official stance. The Cooperative Act of {year} is a Resolution to affirm the Government stands on the side of Labor.

While a Resolution is ceremonial and used to express the opinion of Congress. It is important to show the hard-working men and women of America that pay their Union dues that we are on their side. That whatever platitudes our adversary offers, it is mere lip service. While we actively advocate for the workers of this country.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_909:
It doesn't matter if you were clanking on typewriters in Cape May, or caught a bullet in the Balintawak Blitz. Any Veteran is eligible for GI Bill. No more purity tests to see if your service was worthy of reward. No more exclusion of black veterans from their benefits.

The Forever GI Bill will ensure that the veterans of the past, present, and future are given ample compensation for answering the call of duty to their homeland.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_910:
They say there is no such thing as a free lunch. Well, the Primary Course Meal Act begs to differ. Every child can count on their public school to provide three square meals a day for them. Not only that, but programs will be established to help the food insecure youth of America will be fed during the summer.

When a child isn't hungry, they can instead divert their focus to the pursuit of knowledge. That is how a generation of innovative Americans is made.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_911:
It is time to get involved in the curriculum across the country. With the National Education Act, the Federal Government will be able to test and explore the best methods of education for each grade.

Every year our education committee will gauge the success of the curriculum. Rinse and repeat until every American is the best and brightest they can be.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_912:
The best way to solve a problem is to throw money at it. Our urban renewal seemed to have hit a Grey area before we are seeing a return on investment. The Hart Administration is convinced that this can be solved with the old reliable.

The America Invests Act will foot the bill for our more audacious investments that have yet to yield results.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_913:
The massive size of the Hart Administration's economic revitalization and urban renewal policies have required significant discretionary spending. The sheer volume of this is prompting a growing backlash against the Administration's policies by its political opponents both within and outside of Congress. According to these “budget hawks,” the Hart Administration's spending is grotesquely unsustainable and is both bloating the federal government and saddling the United States with levels of debt it will struggle to pay off. Many in the Democratic and Republican parties alike have levied concerns about the financial health of the URI, and Chep Morrison has put forth a solution.

The Urban Commitment Act aims to stabilize the expenditures of the federal government by offloading some of the cost of the Hart Administration's programs to state and municipal governments. The federalization of the URI should calm the budget hawks, though it will not fully alleviate the burden placed on cities that are attempting to implement Hart's programs.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_914: The first tranche of urban renewal initiatives were pilot programs to test the effectiveness of the Hart Administration's policies on the communities most eager to accept them: the so-called “New Model Cities.” With the promising results this has yielded, it is time to expand these programs across the country. Now, we shall apply them to the most prominent examples of urban decline: megapoli such as New York, Chicago, Philadelphia, and Saint Louis which have suffered the most from white flight, yet remain emblematic of American civilization. We shall also include all the lesser cities of America, such as state capitals or the many new municipalities that have sprung up in the Sun Belt. No community shall be left behind.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_915:
For decades, America's urban working class has made do with shabby tenements, unable to afford a decent home. The New Deal attempted to resolve this by funding the construction of public housing under the auspices of the Federal Housing Administration. However, such efforts were curtailed by the Dewey Administration, and degradation of housing quality in America's cities has only intensified since then as a result of white flight, which has left downtown areas bereft of investment. It's high time something is done about this sordid state of affairs, and Secretary Jane Jacobs has put forth a solution: the Municipality Housing Act.

Unlike the centralized initiatives of the New Deal, Jacobs' plan allocates significant federal grant funding to municipal governments so they can launch their own public housing projects. This bottom-up approach will empower local communities to find their own solutions to the housing crisis, both strengthening local democracy and alleviating concerns of federal overreach. After all, an association with socialism is the last thing the Hart Administration wants.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_916:
For decades, America's urban working class has made do with shabby tenements, unable to afford a decent home. The New Deal attempted to resolve this by funding the construction of public housing under the auspices of the Federal Housing Administration. However, such efforts were curtailed by the Dewey Administration, and degradation of housing quality in America's cities has only intensified since then as a result of white flight, which has left downtown areas bereft of investment. It's high time something is done about this sordid state of affairs, and after discussions with Senator Romney, the Hart Administration has put forth a solution: the Rebuild the Ghettos Act.

This proposal will serve as a middle ground between Secretary Jacob's radical urbanism and the budget hawks' obstructionism, authorizing the one-time construction or redevelopment of thousands of housing projects through the National Housing Administration. This way, the Hart Administration hopes to transform the tenement rows of America into places worthy of being called “home.” This one-and-done has earned the skepticism of HEW Secretary Jacobs, due to it not providing the funding municipalities need to construct and maintain housing according to their own wishes. However, with Governor Romney's support, this bill may be a necessary compromise that can actually get passed in the Senate, providing some immediate relief to many Americans struggling to pay their bills.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_917:
The NYPD, the Miami-Dade PD, the Juneau PD up in Alaska. There are thousands of police departments and hundreds of thousands of Policemen and women across America. They're from different backgrounds, practice different religions, and enact different methods in their law enforcement. Nevertheless, what binds them together is the will to wake up every morning and risk their lives to protect Americans.

The Law Enforcement Act, tailored by the Hart Administration, is an effort to once again give ample funding to Police Departments. So they can afford the personnel and equipment to better protect everybody in the line of duty.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_918:
“We cannot have a fair prosperity in isolation from a fair society.”

The National Health Insurance Act may be the final battle in the fight for universal healthcare in the United States. A federally managed single-payer program that will ensure medical care in the United States is dependent on a family's health rather than a family's wealth.

Teddy Roosevelt couldn't, Franklin Roosevelt didn't, Eisenhower wouldn't. Hart can.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_919: Companies have been getting away with polluting our environment, causing damage to wildlife and citizens' health. No more. With this bill, punishments for companies that pollute are significantly enhanced, with major fines for breaches of the statute. In addition, more regulations for automobile emissions will be introduced as well. Not only is smog an increasing problem in many cities but doctors are concerned about the effects of car fumes in the human body, particularly leaded gasoline.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_920: Nazism should never be normalized or accepted. Instead it should be viewed as an unnatural and evil ideology that must be contained and eventually defeated. To prevent it ever spreading seriously in the free world, the United States will immediately embargo the German Reich and its partners. This embargo will not only harm their collective economy but also prevent them from cementing themselves into the global system, the first road on the step to normalization.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_921: A genuine masterstroke of diplomacy, this treaty with Japan solves many of the longtime issues the two nations have faced. The issues regarding naval and fishing rights will be resolved with this treaty. And moreover, Hawaii will no longer be enemy territory as new provisions provide Americans with easy travel to and fro. Broadly popular and praised by hawks and doves alike, Kissenger's treaty is eagerly welcomed by the public who anticipate its quick passage.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_922: One of the more controversial international agreements the United States has ever signed, this treaty promises peace in the Pacific, but at a cost. Hawaii is de-facto recognized as a territory owned by the Japanese Empire. For this high cost, little will be gained by the United States save an official end to the issues regarding the island. Many in the Senate are incensed by this, and it seems likely they will try and use their powers to tank what they deem a new Akagi Accord.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_923: Simply put, Realpolitik at its finest has been put before Congress. This treaty, to the surprise of everyone, has gone far beyond a mere agreement over the territory of Hawaii. Instead, Kissinger has hammered out an agreement where the US and Japanese will not compete in proxy conflicts, and even commit to demilitarizing the Pacific. This treaty will promise peace and certainty in the Pacific, but some fear it is allowing the Japanese to consolidate their sphere at the expense of the people in it.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_15000:
The only liberal democracy in Asia finds itself under assault - by a Japanese puppet state, no less. We must rescue the Republic of India from the enemies that beset it upon all sides, or else suffer the greatest blow to our sphere of influence since the Second World War. While we have already begun providing aid to the Indians, our hands are tied by various budgetary and procedural requirements. This bill will free our hands, and allow us to begin piping in military aid as fast as it comes off the factory floor.

The humanitarian aspects, too, cannot be ignored here - most of America has seen the images of starving Indian children on their television sets, and there exists a public demand for aid to India - one which should not be discarded as a negotiating tactic. Food aid must increase if we are to do anything substantial against this famine, and this bill, too, will solve that.
strings.USA_sen_bill_name_20999: Vice Presidential Confirmation of Birch Bayh
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_20999: With the ascension of Chep Morrison to the Oval Office in the wake of President Hart's departure, his former seat now lies open for a steady and competent second-in-command to take over. The President has selected Birch Bayh, the moderate liberal congressman from Indiana, to replace himself and become his right hand man for the times ahead. Birch Bayh by himself is a fine choice for the position, but with far greater political forces at hand, the success or failure of this vote may well determine the course of Chep Morrison's oncoming administration.
strings.USA_sen_bill_name_21000: Vice Presidential Confirmation of Birch Bayh
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21000: With the ascension of Chep Morrison to the Oval Office in the wake of President Hart's departure, his former seat now lies open for a steady and competent second-in-command to take over. The President has selected Birch Bayh, the moderate liberal congressman from Indiana, to replace himself and become his right hand man for the times ahead. Birch Bayh by himself is a fine choice for the position, but with far greater political forces at hand, the success or failure of this vote may well determine the course of Chep Morrison's oncoming administration.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21001:
The Urban Affairs Act is a piece of legislation put forth by the Morrison Administration with support from staffers formerly associated with the Hart Administration. The bill would instigate a reform of the federal bureaucracy, splitting the existing Department of Health, Education, and Welfare into three new departments—the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, and the Department of Urban Affairs.

The bill is seen in Washington as part long-needed reform and part overture to current Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare Jane Jacobs, a way to allow her to operate autonomously on urban reform while ensuring Morrison's ownership over other priorities. While generally supported by liberals as a way of continuing the programs of the Hart Administration, conservatives have argued that the bill dramatically expands the size and scope of the federal government.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21002:
Introduced by Rep. Donald H. Clausen of California, the Land Reform Act is the first conservative package seeking to reform the Urban Renewal Initiative. The bill would allow public housing authorities to refurbish and sell units to private interests and, in certain contexts, allow these groups and individuals to purchase extra rooms and sell them for marked-up costs.

The proposal has been characterized by the Hoover Institution and other conservative groups as a vital reform that both provides flexibility to communities and ensures the solvency of public housing. However, the bill has been loudly condemned by many liberals and urban reformers as defeating the purpose of public housing, reducing the number of affordable units and reducing the overall housing supply.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21003:
The America's Choice Act, introduced by Indiana Representative Earl Landgrebe, is a conservative package that seeks to reform jobs programs initiated under the Urban Renewal Act. The bill would transfer administration, control, and financing of existing federal jobs programs to “private sector partners.” While these programs would still be liable to some degree of federal oversight, program sponsors would be free to use workers for any purpose they deemed fit. Employers would further be free to disregard federal requirements on affirmative action.

The bill's sponsors have argued that this bill reduces distortions in the market created by the previous Hart Administration, removing the federal government from most job markets and ensuring employment figures are not artificially inflated. Proponents also point to projections by the Congressional Budget Office suggesting that the bill would substantially reduce federal spending without significantly impacting the economy. Liberals, including former Hart officials, have strongly opposed this bill for reducing support for workers.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21004:
Representative Paul Laxalt's Responsibility in Government Act is a conservative bill created with the ostensive goal of furthering accountability and transparency in government. If passed, all recipients of federal funding through the Urban Renewal Initiative would be required to complete and submit an audit on their financial activities within 24 months. Additionally, some funding currently devoted to Urban Renewal Initiative grant programs would instead be redirected to fund investigations into alleged corruption.

The bill is part of a larger conservative effort to identify waste, fraud, and mismanagement that may harm taxpayers. While it has received mild support in the press as a straight-forward good governance bill, many liberals have warned that the bill places the URI under permanent investigation, at its own cost, and would provide its opponents with a steady stream of examples of urban malfeasance. Others have expressed concern that the audits could discourage some smaller municipalities from seeking URI funding.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21005:
The Workers' Welfare Act is Earl Landgrebe's latest attempt to modify the Urban Renewal Initiative. The bill would, quite simply, require those seeking welfare through federal programs to provide evidence that they have or are actively seeking full-time employment. Those unable to prove they are seeking gainful employment would face steadily increasing “penalties” limiting the amount of welfare money available to them and their families.

The Workers' Welfare Act has been applauded by a variety of conservative activists, including Missouri firebrand Phyllis Schlafly, as both reducing federal expenditures and providing people with “incentive” to pursue work. These individuals argue that current programs reward “laziness” and other self-destructive behavior. Urban activists have roundly condemned the bill, saying that there is little evidence that welfare programs disincentivize job seeking and that the bill harms those already facing financial hardship.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21006:
Paul Laxalt's Transportation Assessment Act is the latest conservative attack on the Urban Renewal Initiative, one targeting its most basic component: infrastructure. Recognizing the huge costs that the United States Government took upon itself to manage and maintain previously privatized rail and road systems, the Transportation Assessment Act would re-privitize these transportation networks. Properties currently held by the government would be available for bid by private interests, both removing recurring maintenance costs as well as granting the government a one-time infusion of cash to address challenges such as the Oil Crisis.

Many private sector companies argue that the bill would represent a return to normalcy for the United States. Many of the roads and railways held by the government operated sufficiently before federal involvement and would likely continue to do so if re-privatized. Many in Philip Hart's cabinet view this as a dramatic winnowing of the government's ambitions and one that could bring a permanent end to efforts to improve transportation management.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21009:
The Presidential Libraries Act of {year} is a bill written by the senior advisors of H.E.W. Secretary Jane Jacobs and President Chep Morrison to transform the historical archival process for Presidents. The bill would establish a publicly accessible, federally funded system of facilities dedicated to preserving the papers, records, and all other material pertaining to former US Presidents. Certain decision-making authorities pertaining to the style, operation, and location of these facilities would be granted by the former Presidents themselves (acting with oversight from the National Archives) or, in lieu of them, their immediate family.

The bill has garnered broad support across Congress, with even the most firebrand conservatives refusing to provide robust opposition. Many see this bill as a way to guarantee the legacies of the past generation, to preserve examples of political honesty and integrity for future generations. Many in the press have hailed what they see as a new system of civic temples and hope that past Presidents — among them Philip Hart — remain in the public consciousness forever.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21007:
The Federal Finance Act is the latest conservative effort to bring an end to the Urban Renwal Initiative using Congress's oversight authority. If passed, the bill would impose intense restrictions on URI recipient cities. Any city that receives URI funding and runs a deficit would be stripped of debt protection. Cities that are consistently unable to deliver balanced budgets would be forced to drop out of the URI and made ineligible for future loan and grant packages.

The advocates of this bill, including Representatives Laxalt, Clausen, and Landgrebe, have not concealed that their intention is to force as many cities to drop from the URI as possible. While there has been vague language about ensuring cities don't abuse taxpayer money, the overall objective is clearly to cripple an expansive federal program supported by liberal Democrats.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21008:
The Urban Divorce Bill is a sweeping conservative attempt to reverse the “consolidation” of metropolitan areas into large, “ungovernable” municipalities. The bill would require the Census Bureau to assess each community by zoning. Then, based on this assessment, communities containing demonstrably different types of housing would be split into new groupings. In practice, this bill would end urban sprawl by permanently severing suburbs and exurbs from downtown urban areas. All future federal funding would then be made based on these reduced groupings.

The bill is a transparent effort to reduce the strength of cities and the amount of URI funding they are eligible for. If passed, it would effectively kill the initiative and seriously compromise the ability of cities to seek federal support through other programs. City leaders have spent the last week begging Congress not to pursue this bill, warning of cataclysmic consequences if signed into law.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_1776: A massive overhaul and expansion of the Central Intelligence Agency, this act removes plenty of the burdensome and inconvenient restrictions the CIA has faced. Budgetary wise, it will no longer be subjected to the extremely rigorous and bureaucratic methods of accounting other government agencies have been subjected to. Rather they can instead spend their funds in any way they deem necessary. Additionally, the bill includes new immigration overhauls to fast track certain “persons of interest” to citizenship, a measure aimed at enticing cooperation from possible foreign assets.
strings.USA_sen_bill.1776.d_passed:
One of the more controversial measures of President Kirkpatrick's first hundred days, the CIA Act of 1973 has passed the Senate and is now headed to the Oval Office. In a statement, President Kirkpatrick said she was pleased by Congress expediting the bill to “provide urgent and necessary action to protect our national security.”

The CIA Act was widely praised by many of Kirkpatrick's national security oriented supporters, who saw it as removing red tape that hamstrung the agency and made it harder to do its job. However, it attracted controversy from those who saw it as removing necessary oversight from an organization with a checkered past. Regardless, the President's arguments carried the day, and the new administration has secured a major success in its first few days.
strings.USA_sen_bill.1776.d_failed:
One of the more controversial measures of President Kirkpatrick's first hundred days, the CIA Act of 1973 has died on the floor of the Senate, having faced an overwhelming wall of opposition. In a statement, President Kirkpatrick said she was disappointed by Congress refusing to “provide urgent and necessary action to protect our national security.”

The CIA Act was widely praised by many of Kirkpatrick's national security oriented supporters, who saw it as removing red tape that hamstrung the agency and made it harder to do its job. However, it attracted controversy from those who saw it as removing necessary oversight from an organization with a checkered past. It turns out these concerns over giving the Agency too much power were impossible to overcome, and now President Kirkpatrick has suffered her first massive legislative defeat of her administration.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_251: This bill institutes a benefits program for America's unemployed. Previously supported by ramshackle state programs, America's unemployed have been in a difficult spot. This new federal plan will make support payments to unemployed Americans provided they meet certain criteria including a criminal record check and proof of attempts to gain employment.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_252: This bill is intended to prohibit discrimination on the basis of race or sex in employment. Since the founding of America, women and non-whites have been excluded from workplaces and discriminated against in employment. This bill would allow the Department of Labor to initiate actions against employers found to be in breach of the statute, as well as creating federal causes of action for private suits by wronged parties. With a focus on protections based on gender rather than race, time will only tell how it affects discrimination in the workplace.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_401: The Primary Education bill aims to reform the American school system from top to bottom, with federal dollars renovating facilities, purchasing new materials and instituting modern curriculums to guarantee quality education for American students. Naturally, with federal dollars come federal strings and new mandates for equality and non-discrimination will be imposed on public schools to guarantee equality in education.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_402: The Higher Education act aims to fundamentally reform American universities. Through the creation of federal loans and scholarships, deserving but impoverished students will have an opportunity to attend the university of their choice. Schools that wish to be eligible for these tuition dollars must comply with the Civil Rights Act and provide comprehensive education to all students enrolled.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_403: Ever since there has been voting in America, there has been voting discrimination, primarily targeted at limiting African-Americans' participation in the political process. The Voting Rights Act will crack down on such activity and ban the use of literacy tests, poll taxes and other racist voter suppression strategies. The Department of Justice will receive new powers to investigate and prosecute such abuses with further provisions for private litigation to allow citizens to assert their rights.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_404: The United States for the past decades has operated on a national quota system that has greatly prioritized European immigration while minimizing any from Africa, Asia or South America. The flaws of the system have led to a large population of illegal immigrants living clandestine lives within the country while many overseas pine for an opportunity to become an American but are denied any chance. With the Immigration and Nationality Act, the discriminatory national origins quotas will be scrapped while many illegal immigrants will be granted amnesty and some form of permanent status.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_405: Discrimination in housing is one of the pernicious ways that de-facto segregation in schools, in addition to a number of other social wrongs, can persist. To combat this, the Fair Housing Act would forbid racial discrimination in housing sales and rentals as well as make investments in a few public housing projects. With a small public option and anti-discrimination measures, it is hoped that non-whites' struggles for a home will be greatly alleviated.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_406: The American worker could use a helping hand and luckily for him, President Johnson has just the right thing: the Economic Opportunity Act. The Act not only raises the Federal minimum wage, guaranteeing a huge swathe of American labor a payhike, but also institutes plenty of new public works projects to assist in the construction of Johnson's Great Society. The economic implications of the bill are grand indeed.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_407: The Social Security Act revolutionized American society as for the first time the federal government promised workers some amount of retirement support. Now, the Johnson administration wishes to advance the law one step and extend its reach to the disabled. Unable to work and often existing in dire poverty, disabled Amercians seem a natural candidate for an expansion to Social Security.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_408: Even as American healthcare reaches new heights of recuperative and restorative capabilities, access to it remains based on economic factors, leaving the poor undercovered and unhealthy. To improve healthcare access, the Workplace Healthcare Act will place new regulations and price controls on health insurance companies, preventing discrimination against patients with pre-existing conditions as well as restrictions on medical bills for simple procedures.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_409: Racism runs deep in America, corrupting all it touches and extending the misery of the marginalized. The Right to Liberty Act aims to take the most ambitious stance against racism in America yet. By instituting affirmative action programs for the federal government and its contractors, non-white Americans will be assured of equal opportunity to account for centuries of disadvantage. Furthermore, the Civil Rights Act will be extended to cover those under the poverty line, protecting the poorest in society from discrimination.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_410: For millions of Americans, healthcare is a luxury and a medical bill a potential disaster. The Johnson administration will seek to change that with the Medicare and Medicaid bill. Under the bill, citizens over the age of 65 will have a great deal of coverage for healthcare costs by the federal government while medicaid will focus on assisting poor workers and other groups. While expensive and an ambitious plan, it is a necessary one for proper healthcare reform.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_411: Universal access to healthcare should be a priority for any just society. Allowing our citizens to go bankrupt from medical bills or die from preventable diseases due to unwillingness to incur costs is unacceptable. By expanding Medicaid to become a fully opt-in program available to all citizens we shall guarantee all Americans universal coverage. While certain to be expensive, the benefits surely outweigh any price to be paid.
strings.USA_sen_bill_desc_21010: The American Education Modernization Act, the first of President Romney's legislative efforts has been introduced to the Senate. The bill not only aims to fix the funding and resource issues many poorer American schools face but also to fill in some of the cracks in the fractious RDC with a bipartisan bill. Under this legislation, schools shall receive federal funds to bridge the gaps they are facing as well. Updated curriculums and testing standards will follow to ensure taxpayers' resources are used productively and that progress on this issue is made. Most agree the state of education could use reform and Romney believes the disparate wings of the coalition will unite around his bill.
strings.USA_saf_pays_us_little: South Africa will compensate us for our support.
strings.USA_sen_bill.1007.desc: Told you it was a bad idea
strings.USA_sen_bill.1008.desc: Wow, you only had a 10% chance of getting this, good for you

strings.USA_VEN.1.desc:
“Though he did his best to maintain an upstanding composure, Charles Allan was still getting used to his new functions. Long gone were the nonchalant journalistic days when the only concern he had to meddle with was the next day's print. From a lowly counselor to Venezuela's diplomatic mission, he had just overtaken the role of Ambassador after the untimely end of his predecessor's tenure.

And there he was, sitting in front of a Foreign Minister, sweating like a pig as he displayed his best unprepared charm. God. Was it the stress, or Caracas' unbearable tropical humidity? The heat was far from unsettling compared to what he had to contend with back in Arizona, but the wet, heavy climate was a definite contrast from the dry air.

He must have been quite a sight to behold, he thought, trying to reassure himself; a poor consolation at the idea that he might have just failed his first proper assignment since reaching his new position. What was he thinking? Minutes ago, he had just tried to convince Minister Burelli to support a clandestinely funded military operation to overthrow a Caribbean dictator barely half a thousand miles from their coast. Sure, Trujillo was at least twice the threat to the Venezuelan government as he was to American interests, but even he had qualms about this whole ”Caribbean Legion“ shenanigan.

Perhaps he should have tried to strike more smoothly. Crack a few jokes here and there. Do anything to disarm this awkward silence as the Minister went ruminating in his mind, tapping his pen against the counter of his desk. Now, all he could do was wait with a dumb smile as the man facing him pondered an answer. Hiding the concern weighing on his shoulders at least as much as the damp air. And his surprise when Burelli stood up, his face locked in a grin of eager complicity.

”Mr. Stewart,“ he began, his palm reaching for a handshake...
strings.USA_VEN.1.a: “...I had already made up my mind before you even started speaking.”
strings.USA_VEN.2.desc:

FROM FBI DIRECTOR J.EDGAR HOOVER
MEMORANDUM FOR THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF STATE

SUBJECT: FALLING ECONOMIC TIES WITH VENEZUELAN REPUBLIC

1. Recent reports of closed-door negotiations between the Venezuelan government and officials from the Mexican state oil corporation further confirm our worries about growing economic interdependence between the state and the Veracruz sphere.

2. This budding new relationship comes at the expense of our own mercantile bonds to the country, and it is now within reasonable belief that Mexico has unfortunately overtaken our position as Venezuela's primary trading partner.

3. While forfeiting what is a relatively minor strategic ally in the region remains a nonetheless undesirable outcome, it is of additional concern that we consider the expected loss in standing it will represent on our future influence for petroleum investments.

4. Despite any official statement having yet to be announced by the Venezuelan administration, we remain vigilant in monitoring the situation for any overtly threatening move from Pemex against our own industrial interests.
strings.USA_VEN.3.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM THE VENEZUELA OFFICE OF THE FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT
SUBJECT: IMPENDING VENEZUELAN ELECTIONS

Following the ousting of the dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez, Venezuela is currently under the rule of Wolfgang Larrazábal. Previously responsible for helping restore democratic rule, Larrazábal is nearing the end of his term in office. Our intelligence indicates three parties in prime place to take the Presidency soon.

The Democratic Republican Union, the incumbent party, is seen by many local commentators as the favourite to win thanks to Larrazábal's successes in office. The party is generally in favor of liberal values and considered compatible with the OFN. However, there is also a significant socialist contingent within the group, anathematic to the military.

The other most noteworthy party is Democratic Action, a favourite of many after their slim defeat in the last election. They are a Gaitanist party in favor of greater cooperation with us to counter the spread of fascism and secure democratic rule. This has attracted the ire of Venezuela's military, many of whom are still sympathetic to Pérez Jiménez.

Last and likely least of our concerns is the Independent Electoral Political Organization Committee. A moderate and centrist faction, the party is often seen by local pundits as a distinct contrast to the more left-wing inclinations of the other parties. Led by Rafael Caldera, his diplomatic cool-headedness is likely to aid in delicate matters, such as the Essequibo.

Our office advises that only one of these parties is backed out of budgetary concerns, and to avoid overly frustrating our Venezuelan partners, but the choice rests with you.
strings.USA_VEN.3.a: The invisible hand of freedom prepares an intervention.
strings.USA_VEN.3.tt: New intelligence missions have been unlocked to influence the upcoming Venezuelan elections.
strings.USA_VEN.4.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM STEVE W. HARTFORD

MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: MILITARY BUILDUP ALONG COLOMBIA-VENEZUELA BORDER, IBERIAN TIES

A significant military build-up has been detected in the Colombian cities of Bucamaranga, Cúcuta, and Villa Rosario, all surrounding San Cristóbal, Venezuela. Naval observation of Iberian-flagged cargo vessels corroborates in-the-field operatives' reports from the CRU that Franco is backing rogue elements in the Venezuelan military with the aim of toppling Venezuela's government.

Both Caracas and Bogotá are unaware of the activity on the border; the putschists have taken advantage of the disruption caused by the civil conflict in Colombia. With continued preparation, they are poised to seize San Cristóbal as a first step toward regime-change.

U.S. assets in the region are insufficient for an intervention. The crisis in Africa depleted operational resources. A joint response led by Brazilian intelligence is ongoing. Continued cooperation with Brazil is recommended and essential as they assist Venezuela against the Dominican-backed coup plot.

FROM STEVE W. HARTFORD

MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: SIM ACTIVITY AND MILITARY BUILDUP ALONG COLOMBIA-VENEZUELA BORDER

A significant military build-up has been detected in the Colombian cities of Bucamaranga, Cúcuta, and Villa Rosario, all surrounding San Cristóbal, Venezuela. A source embedded within the Dominican Republic's SIM corroborates in-the-field operatives' reports from the CRU that Dominican intelligence is backing rogue elements in the Venezuelan military with the aim of toppling Venezuela's government.

Both Caracas and Bogotá are unaware of the activity on the border; the putschists have taken advantage of the disruption caused by the civil conflict in Colombia. With continued preparation, they are poised to seize San Cristóbal as a first step toward regime-change.

U.S assets in the region are insufficient for an intervention. The crisis in Africa depleted operational resources. A joint response led by Brazilian intelligence is ongoing. Continued cooperation with Brazil is recommended and essential as they assist Venezuela against the Dominican-backed coup plot.

strings.USA_VEN.6.desc:
In a quaint little office in Brasília, comfortably nested in clear viewfront of the Praça Portugal, Ambassador Gordon held the phone's tip as far as he could from his left ear, firmly hoping a few inches of air would prove to be adequate shielding from the flow of insults that hadn't stopped pouring for the past five minutes.

It wasn't a surprise for him: all his previous exchanges with the Secretary of State had oscillated between the mildly unpleasant and the agonizing. Today, it was unfortunately leaning towards the latter.

“Care to explain why your boys failed to prevent a bunch of fusspot brass and fascists from overthrowing a friendly government?” As usual, Gordon deftly repressed any thought of engaging. He remained stoically silent, patiently waiting for the word torrent to subside. And eventually, it did.

Only when he was absolutely sure that the floodgates had dropped did he even begin to answer, slowly unraveling his own thoughts. Calmly explaining that the coup's success was an unfortunate consequence of its overwhelming support by the Venezuelan military, and not to blame on any incompetence from their Brazilian partners. That their hands had been kept clean by the lack of direct American engagement in the conflict. That their diplomatic ties to Venezuela were not only far from unsalvageable, but relatively untainted by this less-than-preferable outcome.

Though it did nothing to sweeten the tone of the conversation, nor make it more bearable, he could feel his interlocutor slowly relaxing. Solace finally came when the Secretary eventually hung up, not without mumbling something barely intelligible about “having to arrange something with the new bloody fascists in charge”. He, however, would just fall back on his chair, trying to wrap his head around what had just happened.
strings.USA_VEN.6.a: Mostly, he was just glad he would keep his job for yet another day.
strings.USA_VEN.7.desc:
RESTRICTED/{date}

FROM THE VENEZUELA OFFICE OF THE FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: GOVERNMENT VICTORY IN VENEZUELA COUP

With former general Jesús María Castro León having reportedly been incarcerated in the Cuartel San Carlos while awaiting military trial for high treason, the recent uprising in Venezuela has drawn to an end, in major part thanks to considerable intelligence support from our Brazilian allies.

Claiming victory in the locally nicknamed “Easter Coup,” Venezuelan President Fabricio Ojeda has now officially taken proper functions in the Palacio de Miraflores. Our intelligence suggests that this outcome is only sure to bolster his already soaring popularity, and even the most ardent voices among right-wing opposition figures have grown silent, as many fear association with the putschists.

While this is certainly a preferable result compared to a fascist takeover by Castro León's Iberian-backed military clique, Ojeda's platform remains uncomfortably close to a communist rhetoric that is just as sure to clash with our local interests. A former student activist mirroring his own support base, he has since grown closer to the model of the Cuban Revolution, especially following Fidel Castro's visit to Caracas back in 1959.

Despite these concerns, although enjoying a relatively muted opposition for the time being, it is yet to be seen if Ojeda's term doesn't anger the conservative bloc enough for him to be democratically ousted in the next few years, or even spark another attempt at a military coup, which might just offer us an opportunity should he prove to be a thorn on our side.
strings.USA_VEN.7.a: Plucking it before the prickles show.
strings.USA_VEN.9.desc:
“Coffee?”

James blinked a couple of times, shaking the blur that had started to seep in again on his exhausted eyes. He looked almost surprised at the figure holding the still-fuming white cup, gazing at him with genuine concern. She definitely seemed out of place in the room full of disheveled men whose drained stares were still focused on the ABC news report following the press secretary's address. “Thank you,” he finally answered as he grabbed the hot beverage from his secretary. “I need to get in line with the State Department,” he added. “Quickly.”

The man on TV spoke of an “unprecedented act of aggression against our local industries,” labeling the Venezuelan government's recent oil nationalization policies “not only unacceptable from a fellow democratic nation,” but “of dangerous similarity to those that would take practice in full-on communist regimes.” Then, he warned in absolute confidence that Ojeda's regime would face the “full consequences of its strike on American assets.”

But facing the other side of the screen was a completely different mood. Right here, in the Standard Oil Company's New Jersey headquarters, the spirit was far from outraged statements, but one of livid silence and empty faces of figures who'd just seen their entire livelihood snatched away from them in a fortnight. Some, like James, had stayed here from dusk onward, drawing figures and figuring out numbers. Not great numbers. Not at all. And even staring at the dark liquid now resting in his hands could not make him forget about them.

Somewhere in a D.C office on 2201 C Street NW, a phone rang to a spokesperson who'd just spent the last couple of days putting out fires. “Our administration is already handling the situation,” said the voice on the other end of the line. “We will do our best to address these concerns,” it continued...
strings.USA_VEN.9.a: ...and rest assured that it remains a top priority for us.
strings.USA_VEN.9.b: ...however, I hope you understand that other matters...
strings.USA_VEN.9.tt:
If the democratic opposition becomes stronger than {ven_getflag} Ojeda's government and the military, {usa_getflag} our interests in Venezuela will prevail over {mex_getflag} Mexico and {ibr_getflag} Iberia.
------------------------------------
strings.USA_VEN.10.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM THE VENEZUELA OFFICE OF THE FBI
MEMORANDUM FOR THE PRESIDENT

SUBJECT: ONGOING ISSUES IN VENEZUELA

1. President Fabricio Ojeda's fiery anti-American rhetoric, blaming U.S influence on Venezuela's industries for its ongoing economic troubles, has continued to fuel the nationalization programs occurring across the nation. His administration's deliberate focus on the petroleum industry is already proving its expected destructive impact on our own oil companies.

2. Unsurprisingly, these aggressive policies have sparked outrage beyond our own borders, especially within the country's conservative opposition. In particular, figures from AD and URD's right-wing bloc have started to draft contingency plans to displace the current government, likely through an impeachment process.

3. Even following the purges enacted after the failure of the Easter Coup, there remains a significant number of dissatisfied elements within the Venezuelan military. Our intelligence points to agreements being struck between rogue officers and the previous groupings: an uneasy alliance that would open the door to military action, failing a removal of Ojeda through democratic means.

4. While the situation gifts us with a striking opportunity to replace the ruling socialist regime with one lying closer to our own interests, further instability might provide grounds for another military coup, which is an outcome to be avoided at all costs. Accordingly, our suggested course of action would be to...
strings.USA_VEN.10.a: ...provide them with adequate funding, and support impeachment efforts through any means.
strings.USA_VEN.10.b: ...divert more field agents to Venezuela to covertly assist opposition efforts.
strings.USA_VEN.10.c: ...closely monitor the situation, and avoid kicking the nest.
strings.USA_VEN.11.desc:
The country club in La Lagunita served all kinds: from people walking the halls of power to those bribing them. Six thousand yards of El Hatillo's primest real estate were attended year-round to entertain the crème of Venezuela's high society, across scenic golf courses and exquisite dining venues not even an hour's drive from Caracas.

But among the charming country club's exceedingly well-off clientele, many fancied themselves as the slightly more conscious kind. The ones with opinions to voice, sometimes even indulging its disciplined workforce in their banters. For his colleagues, it often meant the opportunity for some spectacular tipping, should they mingle with the right minds. For Luis, it meant a first seat to whatever private bits of gossip their owners would spew when they forgot he stood within earshot.

From what he'd gathered pouring their glasses back to full, these ones seemed alarmed about the nation's recent direction. One feared the less-educated masses were falling to dangerous populist promises that threatened to steer them into becoming a second Cuba. Too much change, too fast; sweeping reforms that, while well-intentioned, would strip the country of the sensible democracy they'd worked so hard to bring. Another confidently dismissed these worries, hinting at a couple of military figures he knew were just as eager to displace the overstepping Ojedistans; yet a third seemed reluctant to trust the army not to turn on them as soon as their common foe vanished.

But what startled him most was the general apathy of his coworkers as he returned to share these precious bits. In fact, many actually seemed to concur with the seditious talks. Most, however, would only express indifference as he went on to describe the arrival of another sharply-dressed man, introduced as some kind of lawyer, or representative, for a well-established oil conglomerate; even when the figure mumbled something about an amicable third party within the U.S diplomatic apparatus, and...
strings.USA_VEN.11.a: ...requiring every tool at their disposal against the socialist menace.
strings.USA_VEN.11.b: ...being curious regarding these officers sympathetic to their cause.
strings.USA_VEN.11.c: ...the need to maybe keep their talks less overt to prying ears.
strings.USA_VEN.12.desc:
It all felt so wrong.

“As Mr Stewart said, you can expect the full backing of the American diplomatic mission-” Ever since moving to Caracas, all Charles Allan had done had been some form or another of cloak-and-dagger scheming.

“...and official recognition from the United States, as well as continued support for the new government-” In the span of barely three years, he'd gone through convincing a minister to support a clandestine invasion, to surviving a military coup, and now...

“...you will receive funding and armament supplies, as long as you can ensure they don't fall into the hands of more radical elements,” continued the FBI field agent accompanying him. He used to be a journalist, for god's sake; so why, now, was he sitting in a room full of rogue politicians, helping plan the overthrow of the country he was supposed to serve in as ambassador?

“Rest assured that every officer gathered here is just as committed to democratic principles,” retorted the URD official, prompting nods from the interested parties. “You can trust their loyalty and cooperation through the entire operation-”

“I'm sorry, but what about the rest of the army?” The ambassador had sat through the conversation largely silent, which added to his surprise when the words slipped from his mouth. Shit. Suddenly, all eyes were turned on him; even the FBI lad rose an eyebrow at his interruption.

But then, that gaze moved to the group of conspirators struggling for an answer that still would not come. Both could sense the immediate shift in the room. The growing malaise. They just couldn't promise anything. After a long, uncomfortable moment, he would eventually break the silence by suggesting...
strings.USA_VEN.12.a: ...to cut anyone they couldn't completely trust from the conspirator circle.
strings.USA_VEN.12.b: ...to send more weapons as insurance against the prospect of a counter-coup.
strings.USA_VEN.12.c: ...to let the Venezuelan officials handle the matter themselves.
strings.USA_VEN.13.desc:
Pictures from the NBS report showed the streets of Caracas packed with thousands of Ojeda supporters gathered in protest of the coup attempt that had just occurred during the morning.

Clashes between left-wing demonstrators and the conspirator remnants had continued throughout the day, and the camera panned to officers and officials affiliated with the coup being escorted to the Libertador district after facing arrest by loyalist police and military units.

As the scenes continued to flash across the screen, it all seemed almost palpable.

The anger. The outrage.

The voices denouncing US interference as one of the leading causes for yet another strike against Venezuelan democracy, and vowing to hold those deemed responsible, accountable. Even as the broadcast proceeded to gauge the reaction of various American citizens, it did nothing to ease the growing discomfort.

Some seemed horrified at the prospect of yet another coup occurring in the ever-volatile nation. Others did little to hide their disappointment, having hoped for any off-chance of removing the socialists in power. Nonetheless, most of those interviewed seemed to share some sense of unease at this outcome; unsure what to make of it, or its likely consequences.

Yet as this range of emotions continued to ooze from the TV to meet the eyes of the figures watching from the Situation Room, it would only find a single one in return.
strings.USA_VEN.14.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM FBI FIELD AGENT IN VENEZUELA
MEMORANDUM FOR THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF STATE

SUBJECT: CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OF VENEZUELA COUP ATTEMPT

1. Despite our significant support, the scheme by disloyal Venezuelan officials to overthrow the country's ruling socialist regime has ended in complete disaster. Many of the liberal conspirators, including President of Congress Luis Augusto Dubuc, have found their way to prison in military vans under fierce harassment from Ojeda's supporters; many of whom had no qualms tossing eggs, fruits, and rocks at them.

2. According to our intelligence, several members of the coupist cabal have reportedly managed to evade arrest by escaping to the neighbouring nation of Colombia. Others have sought asylum in the American embassy, where our local ambassador, Charles Allan Stewart, has remained confined until further notice.

3. While currently remaining out of reach from Caracas authorities, these surviving conspirators have asked for our protection against reprisal by the Ojedistas, with some asking for covert extradition to American or Canadian soil.

4. Considering our illegal association with the group, and to avoid further radicalizing the Ojedistas, we advise immediately cutting all contact with the coupists, as well as proclaiming an official condemnation. While salvaging our relationship with the Venezuelan government might prove impossible, we need to prevent any further distancing with what was once a close ally in South America.
strings.USA_VEN.15.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM FBI FIELD AGENT IN VENEZUELA
MEMORANDUM FOR THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF STATE

SUBJECT: SUCCESS OF VENEZUELA COUP ATTEMPT

1. Following the forceful overthrow of Fabricio Ojeda by a cabal of disloyal liberal officials, President of Congress Luis Augusto Dubuc has been sworn in as the country's next leader. The long-brewing plot to remove the socialist regime from power was ignited when sympathetic military officers seized the National Assembly to encourage the delegates to vote in favor of impeachment through a constitutional loophole.

2. With the socialist menace now largely under control, the interim government has immediately shifted its efforts to addressing the looming threat of a counter coup by reactionary figures within the armed forces, which is under the process of being purged of its more radical elements by loyalist and liberal-minded officers.

3. Pending further notice, the military has been placed on standby in anticipation of riots sparked by Ojeda's supporters, especially in Caracas' poorer neighbourhoods and other significant left-wing strongholds. For the time being, however, it seems the freshly restored democratic institutions remain safe under the helm of the interim government until new elections occur.
strings.USA_VEN.16.desc:
CONFIDENTIAL/{date}

FROM FBI FIELD AGENT IN VENEZUELA
MEMORANDUM FOR THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF STATE

SUBJECT: MILITARY COUNTER-COUP IN VENEZUELA

1. While the plot by liberal party officials to overthrow the ruling socialist regime showed initial success, a betrayal by anti-communist elements within the Venezuelan armed forces has led to an officer clique being installed as the country's de facto government.

2. Despite clear anti-communist leanings, the junta tries to project a largely apolitical image and has not declared any intent to usher in significant changes to the country's economy beyond reversing Ojeda's recent policies. This was enough to convince many of the more politically indifferent sectors of Venezuelan society to keep their head down and refrain from voicing opposition to the soldier regime, going on as if nothing occurred.

3. Of particular note, the junta declared openness to pursue economic dealings with the United States. This, however, should *not* be considered a diplomatic overture; furthermore, it is now fair to consider Venezuela as falling under the Iberian sphere, with Madrid predicted to be supplying aid to combat any remaining resistance within the country.

4. Even though their operations are expected to face significant civilian resistance, it is believed that the coupists have learned well from the failure of the previous Easter Coup, and retain reasonable odds of remaining in power. Lacking any significant opposition beyond the shattered left-wing bloc, it seems the country has just come to terms with falling under the yoke of yet another military dictatorship for the foreseeable future.
strings.USA_VEN.23.desc:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF STATE DIPLOMATIC CABLE - VENEZUELA

1. Professor Jóvito Villalba is a person of interest in Venezuela. A known statesman and advocate for democracy as well as a prominent advocate for friendly relations and trade with the United States, he is considered a voice of reason with potential to significantly increase OFN standing among the Caribbean and within the Veracruz Pact. Villalba has the potential to help shape Venezuelan democracy into an enduring, robust, and friendly government in South America. The Department of State has outlined two potential means to boost Villalba's public profile and ensure that Venezuela remains on this track.

2. The first is to arrange a prominent goodwill tour in the region with famous Americans that would lend Villalba celebrity status and ensure that he remains within the public's minds. The cost of such a visit would be high, and it has the potential to stoke nationalist fervor against the United States if the visit garners negative reaction. However, this visit has the chance to evoke broad appeal, even among those who might otherwise be politically opposed to Villalba.

3. The second is an investment package into Caracas, focusing on businesses and infrastructure that could boost trade in the country. Villalba can sell these investments as the fruit of cooperation with the United States that provides stability, employment, and an upward trajectory to the economy that would benefit Venezuelans of all stripes. These investments might not create enough appeal to be measurable, and it's possible that Venezuelans won't attribute them to Villalba's influence, which could undermine the ultimate goal.

4. Both initiatives do not require Congressional approval, but have received mild opposition due to their price tag and the opportunity cost for foreign aid to be delivered to other regions.
strings.USA_VEN.23.a: A high-profile visit would certainly help boost Villalba's appeal.
strings.USA_VEN.23.b: Tangible investments in Caracas will make an impact. People will believe things they see.
strings.USA_VEN.23.c: These options are too expensive. Villalba's on his own.
strings.USA_VEN.24.desc:
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF STATE DIPLOMATIC CABLE - VENEZUELA

1. Under Rafael Caldera, Venezuela has been a staunch ally and a strong presence within the Veracruz Pact. They have not made any significant shifts in foreign policy, and have backed American action since he came to office. Where instability has emerged in the Veracruz Pact or in the West Indies, Venezuela has been a broadly stabilizing force and has helped to boost the profile of a free, stable Latin America internationally.

2. American businesses have also been prospering. With existing trade agreements heavily advantaging American businesses, Venezuela has become both a valuable ally in the export of goods such as oil and fruit, and has increasingly become a destination for both tourists and for the import of American-manufactured goods, such as cars, tractors, and furniture. Some frustrations have been noted by local manufacturers in competition, but the potential application of tariffs should not be pushed immediately, and could risk harming our relations.

3. In recent weeks, Caldera has sent out feelers to us, as well as to the foreign offices in Ottawa, Canberra, and Georgetown, stating interest in resolving the current territorial dispute they have with Guyana. The dispute, which is over the Essequibo Delta, involves a significant portion of its territory and is not currently active, but has remained a frustration of many Venezuelan nationalists and has historically brought tension between both them and the Commonwealth, which remains a significant partner for us.

4. There is little risk that this could blow into a wider issue from Venezuela, with the discussions raised only as a possibility. The discussions will likely see some concessions to them on trade, but could also see them abandon their claim, which would be a major boon for regional stability. Although the talks will likely have to be further in the future, we could help to shore up his government to limit the damage that his concession could do to relations with Venezuela after his term.
strings.USA_VEN.24.a: Caracas is rich, but not as rich as it could be. Let's invest in local businesses.
strings.USA_VEN.24.b: Get Air Force One fired up. Let's see if we can organize a Presidential visit.
strings.USA_VEN.24.c: This dispute isn't currently active. Let's not go overboard with our support.
strings.USA_VEN.25.desc:
MEMORANDUM FOR:                 HS, PARAMARIBO Office
SUBJECTS:                                   1. Historical Notes
                                                     2. Rapid Loss of Government Control
                                                     3. American Interest

1. The Fuerzas Armadas de Liberación Nacional (FALN) has been a thorn in the side of the Venezuelan Government since it cut ties with the Communist Party in 1961. Since then, the PCV, and their subsidiary front the Frente de Liberación Nacional, have engaged in armed resistance. Efforts to crush them have had limited success. Rather, they have seen rising support in Venezuela's impoverished classes.

2. Following recent successful communist uprisings in the Americas, the Domino Theory hypothesis has received another proof as the FALN-FLN attempted an armed coup. Despite being able to secure several major cities and much of the countryside, in the Western regions the uprising stalled and was pushed behind the Andes. Countryside control is contested.

3. The Venezuelan Government is beset by a huge insurgency and open civil war but maintains an effective military. Should it fall, another unfriendly nation will arise in the region increasing instability in South America and the Caribbean. White House must be directed to preserve the current Government to prevent an oil rich communist nation threatening regional interests. Every indication is the strength of the uprising will only grow: support must be prompt.

Signed: WL, Caracas Office
strings.USA_VEN.28.desc:
A great buzzing sound came down to the hacienda. The cattle scattered as the helicopter and its American riders set down, its rotors kicking up dust. A group of men in fancy uniforms and suits materialized from inside the machine.

Nearby, Isidro leaned against a wooden post, bleached by the sun, chewing a stem of moriche grass in his mouth. He watched as a squad of Venezuelan soldiers, in ragged mismatched uniforms holding guns from World War 2, waited outside the hacienda. They escorted the US advisors to a military base far off the hacienda, rifles slung low, boots cracking in the heat and dryness of the vast Venezuelan llanos.

Beneath his hat, Isidro frowned, pressing his lips tightly together as he watched the group of men disappear into the distance. The old llanero had seen this before. He had lived through Cipriano Castro and the subsequent Andean Hegemony under the great Caudillo Gómez, followed by the period of transition, Betancourt and Gallegos, God knows how many coups and juntas. He had seen many flags and heard many slogans, all from men who promised certainty and stability. And yet, he had not seen it.

The helicopter flew off and gave the cattle some peace. Isidro stayed, watching the hacienda and chewing on the stem.
strings.USA_VEN.28.a: The man was used to this, after all.
strings.USA_VEN.29.t: Justice Under the Shade of the Banana Tree
strings.USA_VEN.29.desc:
Captain John Davis wiped away drops of sweat stinging his eyes and tried to maintain a posture worthy of a representative of the free world. The village he found himself in was the devil's asshole - a stifling, dusty hole where even the air smelled of hopelessness. Yet, here he was, under a sprawling banana tree, trying to instill the concept of a “community tribunal” in these people.

In his impeccable Castilian, honed in the lecture halls of Virginia, Davis spoke of the rule of law and transparency. He felt like a missionary among pagans. The local peasants, huddled in a semicircle, listened in silence, exchanging glances. Their rapid, rough dialect, swallowing endings, sounded to the Captain's ear like the barking of yard dogs.

“Justice must be visible...” he began, but was interrupted by a hunched old woman stepping out of the crowd.

Davis expected gratitude but met a gaze full of such ancient fatigue that it seemed heavier than the Andes themselves. “My son was killed by soldiers in uniforms just like those standing behind you,” she creaked, pointing a knobby finger at the convoy. “And my brother was butchered by those tied up over there, for a sack of maize. You speak of law, gringo? There is only one law here: whoever has the machete is right. And you are all the same.”

Davis pursed his lips. “Savages,” he thought with habitual irritation, getting into his jeep, enroute back to San Juan de Los Morros. He had followed the instructions: conducted the procedure. What happened next, he preferred not to see. As the jeep disappeared in a cloud of dust, the Venezuelan infantrymen silently pulled up the guerillero prisoners and led them into the thicket. That night, the jungle screamed with human voices, but Captain Davis slept soundly - his report stated: “Law and order restored.”
strings.USA_VEN.29.a: Civilization ends where the asphalt begins.
strings.USA_VEN.30.desc:
Sergeant Reyes hated night-time Caracas. From the heights of the hills, the city looked like an overturned starry sky, a black ocean where the slums shimmered like swarms of fireflies. But down here, in an alley of the Cota 905 slum as narrow as a throat, romance died, yielding to the smell of urine and rotting refuse.

“God, what a stench,” whispered Private Perez, walking on the left. “Like someone died here a week ago.”

“Shut up,” Reyes hissed without turning. “Watch the rooftops. 'Cocktails' fly here more often than greetings from mommy. Hold the sector, like the Yanks taught in Panama.”

Suddenly, a metallic clatter tore the silence. Perez had snagged a rusty oil can with his boot. The sound of it hitting stone rang out like a gunshot, and a wave of fat cockroaches, feasting on scraps, poured out of the tin. Somewhere in the distance, dogs barked hysterically.

Reyes instantly raised a fist, halting the group. A small figure appeared in the shack's doorway. A child, barefoot, in a t-shirt three sizes too big.

The tactical flashlight's beam slid past the boy and snatched a wall from the darkness. Simón Bolívar was painted on it. But not the one from ceremonial portraits in ministries. This one looked furious, and scarlet paint screamed over the uniform: “EL PUEBLO NO SE ARRODILLA” - “The people do not kneel.”

The Sergeant lowered his barrel. In the capital's center, Bolívar was a symbol of power; here, an icon of rebellion. And gripping the handguard of a rifle stamped “Made in USA,” Reyes felt a pang of conscience: if the Father of the Nation is one for all, why do they look at him from different sides of the gunsight? And which of them is truly betraying his will?
strings.USA_VEN.30.a: In the dark, all cats are grey, and all ideals are blurred.
strings.USA_VEN.31.desc:
“Dear mom, dad, and Liz,

It's been a while since I wrote, but don't worry, I'm alive.

I've been moved to Valencia and the heat is as suffocating as in Barinas, but this time there's the constant noise of bikers, or 'motorizados' as they call them here, on the highway next to us. Despite this, it is a very nice place. The sunsets are beautiful, look like paintings, and the girls here look even better.

It seems that the war is ending, and thankfully in our favor, so expect me back soon!”

Fred stared at the letter he wrote, tapping his pencil to the table. The letter mentioned nothing. It didn't mention the constant ambushes. It did not mention how he got separated from his platoon. It did not mention how they got killed later on somewhere in the Andes. It did not mention the boy he shot in the alley, or how he closed his eyes when he killed him.

He folded the letter carefully into an envelope, wrote the address and set it aside.

But the mail truck was shot and stolen three days ago by guerrilleros. He knows it will never be sent.

He reached for another piece of paper and envelope anyway.
strings.USA_VEN.32.desc:
Though it wasn't an entirely unusual occurrence for the U.S embassy in Venezuela to be brimming with as much activity in the hours before dawn, what'd strike anyone as much less familiar was the odd silence that permeated from the imposing brick structure erected upon the hills near Caracas.

Not odd in how much it lacked of sound. It was actually quite the opposite: the entire embassy bathed in the tunes of the shredders that hadn't yet jammed from a whole night of tearing extravaganza, and the crackle of flames emerging from barrels beside piles upon piles of more crates awaiting their contents to be consumed.

No. It was odd in the way of what was precisely lacking. Which, in this case, was because in the entire multifloored edifice, absolutely no one could be heard saying anything.

Not the sleepless staff members thoroughly walking the halls to ensure no scrap of paper would be left to discover. Neither the livid-looking diplomats, nor the marines in light tactical gear who were slowly escorting them outside the building.

Nothing would be heard but the car's engine roaring through the night as they carefully rode towards the airport, or the rattle of the chopper's blades carrying the American officials away from the city as they watched the sunrise dim through the tinted windows in a hazy orange blur.

Of course, neither would they hear the scarf-clad youth in the slums miles below them running away from their piece, still dripping on the concrete floor in wet, perfect red. Nor would the 'YANQUIS GO HOME' in bold letters be seen by any of its intended recipients, which was perhaps a subtle victory in itself, like the fact that, for once, this graffiti would remain long after this dawn and the one that'd follow, forever echoing a sentiment shared by many, many others.
strings.USA_VEN.32.a: Many whose voices, from now on, would assuredly be heard.
strings.USA_VEN.32.tt: Opportunities to utilize the Condor Legion as a tool to assassinate Gustavo Machado can be found in the Intelligence Tab.
strings.USA_VEN.33.desc:
It wasn't much of a fanfare.
